explanation: Form 17 is the formal document used by Drug Inspectors to disclose the purpose and receipt of taking drug samples for analysis.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The first Central Council was constituted by the Central Government in
explanation: The first Pharmacy Council of India (Central Council) was constituted in the year 1949 under the Pharmacy Act, 1948.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Order came into force in
explanation: The Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Control, Regulation and Review Order came into force in 1993.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: If a drug contains any harmful or toxic substance, which may render it injurious to health, it is called
explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, a drug containing any filthy, putrid, or decomposed substance, or any harmful/toxic ingredient rendering it injurious to health, is deemed an adulterated drug.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The number of nominated members to the State Pharmacy Council are
explanation: State Pharmacy Councils consist of 6 members nominated by the State Government under Section 19 of the Pharmacy Act.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Inventories moving temporarily because of seasonal production are called
explanation: Surplus or seasonal inventory refers to items that accumulate temporarily due to seasonal production fluctuations.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: A modern drug store should fulfil all minimum requirements as specified in ___________ of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940 and Rules 1945.
explanation: Schedule N outlines the minimum requirements for the efficient running of a pharmacy or modern drug store.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: One among the following is not a source of secondary data for market research
explanation: Sales turnover represents primary internal company data rather than external or published secondary data.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The method in which a code is assigned to stored items for easy identification is called
explanation: Mnemonic coding uses letters and abbreviations to help easily remember and identify stored items.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The inventory carrying cost is represented by items like (i) Cost of insurance (ii) Cost of paper work (iii) Cost of taxes (iv) Cost of posting
explanation: Cost of insurance and taxes are direct holding/carrying costs associated with storing inventory.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The capital necessary to maintain a minimum level of stock and for payment of regular expenses is called
explanation: Permanent working capital represents the minimum amount of liquid capital required continuously to maintain essential stock and operations.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The bank launched in India for promoting the export and import of goods and services is
explanation: The Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank) was established for promoting international trade and financing exports/imports.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The lower limit below which the stock of any item, should not normally be allowed to fall is
explanation: Buffer stock (or safety stock) is the minimum reserve level maintained to prevent stockouts.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The items which consume 70% of the total budget of inventories, but represent only 10% of the total inventory are called
explanation: In ABC analysis, 'A' items account for the highest value consumption (~70%) despite making up a small percentage (~10%) of total items.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Pre-determined scrap is refered to as
explanation: Anticipated or planned scrap is estimated in advance before manufacturing or processing begins.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: The efficiency of HEPA filter can be tested using
explanation: The DOP (dioctyl phthalate) smoke test is a standard method used to test the integrity and efficiency of HEPA filters.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Pharmacy and Therapeutic Committee has role except in

options.B: Preparation of drug list and emergency supplies

explanation: Medical record services are managed by the health information management department, not the Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) committee.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: MEDLINE is a drug information resource categorised under
explanation: MEDLINE is a bibliographic database indexing biomedical literature, making it a secondary literature resource.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Test for water holding capacity is stated in Indian Pharmacopoeia for
explanation: Absorbent cotton wool is tested for its water holding capacity according to pharmacopoeial standards.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: ‘Clean room area’ means

options.A: Socially clean area free from particulate matter
options.D: Area with high standards of cleanliness and hygiene

explanation: A clean room is defined as a socially clean area controlled for airborne particulate matter and environmental parameters.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Satellite pharmacy a mode of drug distribution system under
explanation: Satellite pharmacies operate as decentralized units to dispense medications close to nursing units, typically in decentralized unit dose systems.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Automatic stop order is used for
explanation: Automatic stop orders are policies applied to dangerous or controlled drugs (such as narcotics and sedatives) to limit prolonged unmonitored use.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Absorbable suture is
explanation: Chromic catgut is a natural absorbable surgical suture, unlike nylon, silk, and cotton which are non-absorbable.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Tuberculin syringe is available in
explanation: Tuberculin syringes are small-volume syringes typically designed with a capacity of 1 ml for accurate intradermal administration.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Which one is used for aspiration of stomach contents ?
explanation: Ryle's tube (nasogastric tube) is inserted through the nose into the stomach for feeding or aspiration of gastric contents.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Withdrawal symptoms of opioids can be managed with
explanation: Methadone is a long-acting mu-opioid receptor agonist used for detoxification and maintenance therapy in opioid dependence.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Bioavailability increases when drugs are in
explanation: Non-ionized drugs are lipophilic and can easily cross biological lipid membranes, thus increasing absorption and bioavailability.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Insulin induced hypoglycaemia is classified under
explanation: Type A ADRs are dose-dependent, predictable extensions of a drug's pharmacological action, such as hypoglycemia caused by insulin.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: A method to improve patient compliance is
explanation: All listed methods (counselling, proper labeling, and regimen simplification) effectively enhance patient medication adherence.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Serum sodium level is
explanation: The normal physiological reference range for serum sodium in humans is approximately 135 to 145 mmol/L.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Metoclopramide if given with paracetamol
explanation: Metoclopramide accelerates gastric emptying, thereby increasing the rate of absorption and decreasing the onset time of analgesia for paracetamol.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Fatigue, weight loss, chronic cough, night sweats, chest pain are clinical symptoms of
explanation: Chronic cough, night sweats, fatigue, and weight loss are classic hallmark symptoms of pulmonary tuberculosis.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: HBsAg testing is done to detect the presence of
explanation: HBsAg (Hepatitis B surface antigen) is a serological marker specifically used to screen for Hepatitis B virus infection.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: Amphetamine poisoning can be treated with
explanation: Sodium bicarbonate alkalinizes the urine, which ionizes amphetamines and enhances their renal excretion during overdose.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: If two or more dosage forms of same drug contain same labelled quantities of the drug, they are
explanation: Products that contain the same active ingredients in the exact same labeled quantities are defined as chemical equivalents.
source_exam: Pharmacist gr 2 health services and medical education 2020

question_text: In which theory is the acid an electron pair acceptor and the base an electron pair donor ?

options.D: Hard and Soft acid base concept

explanation: The Lewis theory defines acids as electron pair acceptors and bases as electron pair donors.

question_text: Muriatic acid is the synonym of
explanation: Muriatic acid is the historical and industrial synonym for hydrochloric acid.

question_text: 2% W/V iodine and 2.5% W/V Potassium Iodide
explanation: Weak iodine solution (iodine tincture or Lugol's relative formulations depending on vehicle) contains 2% w/v iodine and 2.4-2.5% w/v potassium iodide.

question_text: Astringent compound exhibit the following properties except :
explanation: Astringents act locally to precipitate proteins, exhibiting styptic, anti-inflammatory, and antiperspirant properties, but not antitussive properties.

question_text: Flower of sulphur is the synonym of
explanation: Sublimed sulfur is commonly known as flowers of sulfur.

question_text: Chlorine reacts with Calcium Hydroxide to produce
explanation: Reaction of chlorine gas with calcium hydroxide yields chlorinated lime (bleaching powder).

question_text: Which of the following is not used as expectorant ?
explanation: Sodium nitrite is a vasodilator and antidote for cyanide poisoning, whereas the others are recognized expectorants.

question_text: In the assay of Hydrogen Peroxide the indicator used is
explanation: Hydrogen peroxide assay is a permanganometric redox titration where potassium permanganate acts as both titrant and self-indicator.

question_text: Drugs that help in removing sputum from respiratory tract either by increasing fluidity of sputum or increasing the volume of fluid that have to be expelled from respiratory tract
explanation: Expectorants facilitate the removal of bronchial secretions by decreasing viscosity or increasing volume.

question_text: The assay of Calcium Gluconate is conducted by which titration method ?
explanation: Calcium gluconate is typically assayed using complexometric titration with disodium EDTA.

question_text: The sterilization technique in which the final container is heated at $80 \ ^\circ\text{C}$ for one hour on each of three successive days
explanation: Tyndallization involves intermittent heating (often around 80-100 degrees Celsius) on successive days to kill bacterial spores.

question_text: Unequal distribution of colour on a coloured tablet is known
explanation: Mottling refers to an unequal distribution of color on the surface of a tablet.

question_text: In hot air oven the heat is transferred from source to the article by
explanation: Heat transfer in a hot air oven involves a combination of conduction, convection, and radiation.

question_text: The following compounds are used as binders and adhesives except :
explanation: Stearic acid is commonly used as a lubricant or glidant, not as a binder or adhesive.

question_text: Capsules that do not disintegrate in the stomach but break up in the intestine are known as
explanation: Enteric-coated capsules resist gastric fluid and release their active ingredients in the intestine.

question_text: All the gases given below are used for gaseous sterilization except
explanation: Nitrous oxide is an anesthetic gas and propellant, whereas the others are well-known sterilizing gases/vapors.

question_text: The hygroscopic or eutectic substance that can be filled into hard gelatine capsules as adsorbent are
explanation: Magnesium oxides, calcium carbonates, and kaolin can all serve as adsorbents for hygroscopic or eutectic mixtures in hard gelatin capsules.

question_text: In hard gelatine capsule the approximate capacity in mg of capsule number "0" is
explanation: A size "0" hard gelatin capsule has an approximate capacity of 680 mg (commonly cited around 650 mg depending on powder bulk density).

question_text: Which of the following is not used as enteric coating materials ?
explanation: Gelatin is soluble in the stomach and is used for capsule shells, not as an enteric coating.

question_text: In sterilization the time required at a given condition to achieve log reduction that is to kill 90 percent of organism is called
explanation: D-value (decimal reduction time) is the time required to reduce the microbial population by 90% (1 log reduction) at a specific temperature.

question_text: Irregular lumps in which modular masses are embedded is the microscopic character of
explanation: Socotrine aloe powder exhibits irregular fragments in which yellowish-brown modular masses are embedded under the microscope.

question_text: Purgative action of aloe is due to
explanation: The primary active purgative constituent of aloe is aloin (barbaloin).

question_text: Legal test is the identification test for
explanation: Legal test is used for identifying certain glycosides, specifically C-glycosides found in Aloe.

question_text: Saffrole is the chemical constituent present in
explanation: Safrole is a phenylpropene derivative found naturally in nutmeg and mace.

question_text: Chemical constituent of Nuxvomica which is a dog poison
explanation: Strychnine is an extremely toxic alkaloid from Nux vomica historically known as a dog poison.

question_text: Hydnocarpus oil is the synonym of
explanation: Hydnocarpus oil is also known as chaulmoogra oil.

question_text: The water soluble chemical constituent of ergot is
explanation: Ergometrine (ergonovine) is water-soluble, unlike most other ergot alkaloids which are water-insoluble.

question_text: Azadirachtin is the chemical constituent present in Neem act as
explanation: Azadirachtin from neem is primarily known for its potent insect antifeedant and growth-disrupting properties.

question_text: Which is used in cheese manufacturing as a substitute of rennin ?
explanation: Papain and other plant proteases like microbial proteases are sometimes utilized as rennet substitutes in cheese making.

question_text: Vitamin A can be synthesized from
explanation: Lemon grass oil contains citral, which serves as a starting material for the industrial synthesis of vitamin A.

question_text: Coalescence of the dispersed globules and separation of the disperse as a separate layer in an emulsion is called
explanation: Cracking (or coalescence) is the irreversible breaking of an emulsion where dispersed globules separate into a distinct layer.

question_text: An example of ointment prepared by chemical reaction method
explanation: Ointment of sulfur (specifically precipitated sulfur ointment) involves a chemical reaction or special trituration, but sulfur ointment USP is prepared incorporating precipitated sulfur.

question_text: Abrasive agent used in dentifrices
explanation: Calcium carbonate is a standard abrasive agent widely used in toothpastes and dentifrices.

question_text: Antioxidant used in lipsticks
explanation: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is a common phenolic antioxidant used to prevent rancidity in cosmetic products containing fats and oils.

question_text: Non-aqueous oily vehicle used in parenteral depot formulations ?
explanation: Arachis oil (peanut oil) is a commonly used non-aqueous oily vehicle for intramuscular depot injections.

question_text: Test which is used to ensure parenteral product is free from foreign particles
explanation: The clarity test is performed visually or instrumentally to ensure parenteral solutions are free from suspended foreign particles.

question_text: Percentage w/v of Benzalkonium chloride in eye drop used as preservative
explanation: Benzalkonium chloride is typically used in ophthalmic preparations as a preservative at a concentration of 0.01% to 0.02% w/v.

question_text: Hair removed by chemical method is known as
explanation: Depilation refers to the chemical or physical removal of hair from the skin surface, whereas epilation removes hair from the root.

question_text: Which is the pyrogen test for parenteral product ?
explanation: The Limulus amoebocyte lysate (LAL) test is an in vitro assay used to detect bacterial endotoxins (pyrogens).

question_text: Lyophilisation is the another name of
explanation: Lyophilisation is synonymous with freeze-drying, a dehydration process typically used to preserve labile materials.

question_text: The chemical nature of the antineoplastic drug cisplatin is
explanation: Cisplatin is an inorganic platinum-based antineoplastic coordination complex with the cis configuration of diamminedichloroplatinum(II).

question_text: The mechanism of action of Ethacrynic acid as loop diuretic is due to

options.C: the presence of $\alpha, \beta$ – unsaturated ketone forming covalent bond with sulfhydryl groups

explanation: Ethacrynic acid possesses an $\alpha,\beta$-unsaturated ketone group (an activated double bond) that undergoes Michael addition with sulfhydryl groups of transport proteins.

question_text: Identify the antiparkinsonian drug
explanation: Biperiden is a centrally acting anticholinergic agent used as an antiparkinsonian drug.

question_text: Identify the antidote for cholinesterase inhibitors
explanation: Pralidoxime (2-PAM) is a cholinesterase reactivator used as an antidote for organophosphate poisoning.

question_text: IUPAC name for Salbutamol
explanation: Salbutamol (albuterol) IUPAC name is 4-[2-(tert-butylamino)-1-hydroxyethyl]-2-(hydroxymethyl)phenol.

question_text: Haloperidol – A tranquilizer belong to which class of drugs ?
explanation: Haloperidol is a typical antipsychotic drug belonging to the butyrophenone chemical class.

question_text: Penicillin V is also known as
explanation: Penicillin V is biosynthetically or semisynthetically known as phenoxymethylpenicillin.

question_text: Identify an antitubercular drug which is chemically an aliphatic diamine.
explanation: Ethambutol is an oral chemotherapeutic agent that is classified chemically as an aliphatic diamine derivative.

question_text: The antibiotic obtained from Streptomyces venezuelae
explanation: Chloramphenicol was originally isolated from the soil bacterium Streptomyces venezuelae.

question_text: Co-trimoxazole contains two antibiotics. What are they ?
explanation: Co-trimoxazole is a fixed-dose combination of sulphamethoxazole and trimethoprim in a 5:1 ratio.

question_text: Identify the barbiturate used as general anaesthetic.
explanation: Methohexital is an ultra-short-acting barbiturate commonly used for intravenous induction of general anesthesia.

question_text: Which of the following is used in obstetrical pain ?
explanation: Pethidine (meperidine) has traditionally been preferred over morphine in obstetrics because it causes less neonatal respiratory depression and uterine contraction interference.

question_text: Identify the method of metabolism of salicylates in our body.
explanation: Salicylates are primarily metabolized via conjugation with glycine (forming salicyluric acid) and with glucuronic acid.

question_text: Drug of choice for trigeminal neuralgia.
explanation: Carbamazepine is established as the primary drug of choice for the medical management of trigeminal neuralgia.

question_text: These compounds inhibit the reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin into adrenergic neurons. What are they ?
explanation: Tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs) exert their pharmacological activity largely by inhibiting the neuronal reuptake of norepinephrine and serotonin.

question_text: Drug used in the diagnosis of Myasthenia gravis
explanation: Edrophonium is a very short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used in the Tensilon test to diagnose myasthenia gravis.

question_text: Identify the calcium channel blocker.
explanation: Verapamil is a non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blocker used for hypertension, angina, and supraventricular arrhythmias.

question_text: Loop diuretics act as
explanation: Loop diuretics inhibit the $\text{Na}^+/\text{K}^+/2\text{Cl}^-$ cotransporter in the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle.

question_text: The following is not an antifungal drug :
explanation: Neomycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic, whereas Amphotericin-B, Clotrimazole, and Terbinafine are antifungals.

question_text: Oral hypoglycaemic agent causing lactic acidosis as most serious complication
explanation: Phenformin is a biguanide that was largely withdrawn due to a high incidence of fatal lactic acidosis.

question_text: Schedule M1 deals with the requirements of factory premises for the manufacturing of
explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, Schedule M1 specifies the factory premises requirements for manufacturing homeopathic preparations.

question_text: A license to sell stock and exhibit or offer for sale of distribute drugs specified in schedule C1 shall be issued in form
explanation: Form 21A is issued for a license to sell, stock, exhibit, or offer for sale or distribute drugs specified in Schedule C1.

question_text: The drug Clofazimine comes under schedule
explanation: Clofazimine is an anti-leprosy drug that falls under Schedule H of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules.

question_text: The place where the licensee employ the services of a qualified person but drugs are not compounded are called
explanation: A chemist and druggist establishment employs a qualified person to sell drugs without compounding them on-site.

question_text: The ER 1991 prescribes practical training for registration of pharmacist is
explanation: The Education Regulations 1991 (ER 1991) prescribes 500 hours of practical training spread over not less than three months.

question_text: Pharmacy inspectors are appointed by
explanation: Pharmacy inspectors are appointed by the State Government under the provisions of the Pharmacy Act, 1948.

question_text: Who among the given is not the common member of PCI and DTAB ?
explanation: Director CDRI is not typically a statutory common member of both the Pharmacy Council of India and the Drugs Technical Advisory Board.

question_text: The schedule of drugs and magic remedies act 1954 includes which of the following diseases ?
explanation: The Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisements) Act lists numerous prohibited conditions including dropsy, diabetes, and Bright's disease.

question_text: Example of narcotic drug
explanation: Poppy straw, cannabis resin, and coca leaves with ecgonine are narcotics, while the listed options (such as plain poppy seeds or leaves without tops/ecgonine) are typically excluded or exempted.

question_text: Which of the following is a psychotropic substance ?
explanation: Mazindol, methyprylon, and pentazocine are all controlled substances classified under psychotropic schedules.

question_text: Which of the following method is used for sales promotion ?
explanation: Coupons, trade stamps, and free samples are all common promotional tools used in marketing and pharmaceutical sales.

question_text: B category items represent which of the following money value ?
explanation: In ABC inventory analysis, category B items typically account for an intermediate value of about 15-20% of total inventory cost.

question_text: A method of recording store balances after every receipt and issue to facilitate regular checking and to obviate closing down stock taking
explanation: Perpetual inventory control is a continuous system of recording inventory balances after every transaction to eliminate the need for a total shutdown stock take.

question_text: Which of the following are essential qualities of a salesman ?
explanation: An effective salesman requires a combination of moral integrity, mental aptitude, and vocational training/skills.

question_text: The scrap which can be anticipated during manufacturing is called
explanation: Legitimate (or normal) scrap is that which is expected and can be anticipated during standard manufacturing processes.

question_text: Mixed bank is a combination of
explanation: A mixed bank combines the functions of commercial banking and industrial banking (financing industries).

question_text: Given in the following are the sources of primary data except :
explanation: Trade associations usually publish secondary reports or aggregated statistics, whereas consumers, salesmen, and dealers provide direct primary data.

question_text: The minimum area required to open a wholesale drugstore is
explanation: According to the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules in India, a minimum area of 10 sq. meters (approximately 108 sq. ft.) is required for a wholesale drugstore.

question_text: The tender issued only in those cases where an item of a proprietary nature or where repetitive order is to be issued in short period
explanation: A single tender is issued for proprietary items or urgent repetitive orders where only one specific supplier is approached.

question_text: Creditorship securities which provide funds to the company on loan basis rather than capital basis is called
explanation: Debentures represent debt instruments or creditorship securities that provide loan capital to a company.

question_text: According to Indian Pharmacopoeia, the storage condition : “Store in refrigerator” means store between :
explanation: Storage in a refrigerator according to the Indian Pharmacopoeia is defined as maintaining a temperature between 2°C and 8°C.

question_text: What is the principle of Limulus Amoebocyte Lysate (LAL) test for pyrogen ?
explanation: The LAL test relies on the enzymatic coagulation of amoebocyte lysate by bacterial endotoxins.

question_text: Who is the secretary of the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee (PTC) ?
explanation: The chief pharmacist typically serves as the secretary of the Pharmacy and Therapeutics Committee in hospitals.

question_text: Which of the following glass container has high hydrolytic resistance and a high thermal shock resistance ?
explanation: Type I glass is borosilicate glass, which possesses high hydrolytic resistance and excellent thermal shock resistance.

question_text: Choose the incorrect statements about HEPA filter :

options.A: It is useful for the preparation of parenteral product.
options.B: It has the efficiency of removing 100% of particles of 0.3 mcm or larger.
options.C: It is generally described as high-efficiency particulate air filter.

explanation: HEPA filters have a nominal removal efficiency of 99.97% (not 100%) for particles of 0.3 micrometers, making option B the technically incorrect statement.

question_text: The word “Ambulatory care” means
explanation: Ambulatory care refers to medical services provided on an outpatient basis, allowing patients to walk in and out without overnight hospitalization.

question_text: The time taken between placing of an order and receipt of items is known as
explanation: Lead time is defined as the total latency or time elapsed between placing a purchase order and receiving the delivered items.

question_text: Which of the following criteria should be taken into consideration for entry or deletion of drugs in Hospital formulary ?

options.A: The manufacturer of drug should have the license under Drug and Cosmetic Rules.
options.B: The drug must be recognized by Pharmacopoeia.
options.C: The drug should not have secret composition.

explanation: All listed criteria are essential standards and regulatory requirements for including a drug in a hospital formulary.

question_text: The appropriate pH range for ophthalmic preparations is
explanation: The normal pH of tear fluid is around 7.4, and ophthalmic preparations generally aim for a physiological pH range between 6.5 and 8.5 to minimize irritation.

question_text: The process that eliminates many or all pathogenic micro-organisms, except bacterial spores, on inanimate objects is known as
explanation: Disinfection is defined as the process of destroying pathogenic microorganisms on inanimate objects, excluding bacterial endospores.

question_text: Drug-induced fatal malformations are more if the drugs given in which of the following weeks of pregnancy ?
explanation: The period of organogenesis, which spans from the 3rd to the 11th week of pregnancy, is the time of highest susceptibility to major structural malformations.

question_text: Red blood cell destruction can be triggered in individuals with Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency by the following drugs except :
explanation: Diphenhydramine does not cause hemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients, whereas sulfonamides, quinine, and nalidixic acid are known oxidative triggers.

question_text: What are adverse drug reactions (ADRs) ?

options.A: The noxious and unintended effect of drugs which occurs at normal doses.
options.B: The synergistic effects that are seen when some drugs are administered concurrently.
options.C: Harmful chemical interactions between two drugs that are used to treat the same clinical symptoms.
options.D: Responses to increased drug doses required to achieve the same physiological outcome.

explanation: By definition, an adverse drug reaction is a noxious and unintended response to a medicinal product occurring at doses normally used in humans.

question_text: Which of the following agents is an opioid antagonist ?
explanation: Naloxone is a competitive opioid receptor antagonist used primarily to reverse opioid overdose.

question_text: Which route of drug administration is most likely to undergo first-pass effect ?
explanation: Oral administration subjects drugs to hepatic first-pass metabolism before reaching the systemic circulation.

question_text: Which one of the following drugs is used as an antidote in organophosphorus poisoning ?
explanation: Atropine is a competitive muscarinic receptor antagonist widely used to treat the excessive cholinergic symptoms of organophosphate poisoning.

question_text: What is the normal fasting blood sugar level range ?
explanation: A normal fasting blood glucose level is typically between 70 mg/dL and 100 mg/dL.

question_text: The following food stuffs can cause hypertensive crisis during non-selective Mono Amino Oxidase (MAO) inhibitor therapy :
explanation: Aged cheeses, red wines, and certain chocolates contain tyramine, which can precipitate a severe hypertensive crisis when combined with MAO inhibitors.

question_text: The following are the signs and symptoms of tuberculosis excepts :
explanation: Morning stiffness is a classic sign of inflammatory joint diseases like rheumatoid arthritis rather than tuberculosis.

question_text: The World Health Organization (WHO) programme for International Adverse Drug Reaction Monitoring is a worldwide collaboration of more than 150 countries whose aims are the safer use of medicines for patients everywhere and building a global culture of patient safety. The monitoring centre is situated at
explanation: The WHO Collaborating Centre for International Drug Monitoring (the Uppsala Monitoring Centre) is located in Uppsala, Sweden.

question_text: Chemical composition of asbestos:
explanation: Asbestos is a group of naturally occurring silicate minerals composed of thin, fibrous crystals known chemically as aluminosilicates.

question_text: Which among the following is classified as folate antagonist:
explanation: Methotrexate is a well-known antimetabolite and antifolate drug used in cancer chemotherapy and autoimmune diseases.

question_text: Gynaecomastia may be the possible side effects of one of the following drug:
explanation: Ketoconazole inhibits steroidogenesis, including testosterone synthesis, which can lead to gynecomastia as a side effect.

question_text: When at least $51\%$ shares of business organisation are in the hands of government it is called:
explanation: A government company is defined as any company in which not less than $51\%$ of the paid-up share capital is held by the government.

question_text: Myristicin is a chemical constituent of:
explanation: Myristicin is a naturally occurring organic compound found in nutmeg essential oil.

question_text: A cationic surfactant is:
explanation: Cetrimide is a cationic surfactant commonly used as an antiseptic and disinfectant.

question_text: Which type of mill is used for grinding sulphonamide drug?
explanation: Fluid energy mills (jet mills) are used for ultra-fine grinding of heat-sensitive substances like certain sulfonamides.

question_text: Mail order business is:
explanation: Mail order business is a form of retailing where goods are sold through the mail or postal service.

question_text: Which drug is used for the detection of boric acid?
explanation: Turmeric paper contains curcumin, which reacts with boric acid to form a reddish-brown complex (rosocyanin), used in detection.

question_text: A strong dog poison is:
explanation: Strychnine is an extremely toxic alkaloid traditionally used as a pesticide, notably against vertebrates such as stray dogs.

question_text: The ability of the firm to meet its current liability is measured by:
explanation: Liquidity ratios measure a company's ability to pay off its short-term debts and current liabilities.

question_text: Drugs which increases respiratory tract fluid is called:
explanation: Expectorants are pharmacological agents that increase bronchial secretion and respiratory tract fluid.

question_text: Precursor glycoside of digitoxin:
explanation: Purpurea glycoside A is the primary biosynthetic precursor to digitoxin found in Digitalis purpurea.

question_text: Storage condition for dried plasma:
explanation: Dried human plasma is typically stored at temperatures not exceeding $25^{\circ}\text{C}$ to maintain stability.

question_text: Aloe contain barbaloin which is a:
explanation: Barbaloin (aloin) is an anthraquinone derivative containing a C-glycosidic bond.

question_text: An example of cholinomimetic alkaloid is:
explanation: Pilocarpine is a naturally occurring plant alkaloid that acts as a direct-acting cholinomimetic.

question_text: Beta blocker with membrane stabilizing activity:
explanation: Propranolol possesses intrinsic local anesthetic or membrane-stabilizing activity among beta-blockers.

question_text: A journal is a book of:
explanation: A journal is known as a book of original entry where financial transactions are first recorded.

question_text: A resin of animal origin:
explanation: Shellac is a natural resin secreted by the female lac insect.

question_text: All the particles passes through a sieve No. 44 and not more than $40\%$ through a sieve No. 85 called as:
explanation: Moderately fine powder standards require all particles to pass through sieve No. 44 and not more than $40\%$ through sieve No. 85.

question_text: Vein Islet number of Digitalis Purpurea:
explanation: The vein islet number for Digitalis purpurea typically ranges from 15 to 26.

question_text: Plant constituent used in the preparation of mosquito coils:
explanation: Pyrethrins extracted from Pyrethrum flowers are widely used as natural insecticides in mosquito coils.

question_text: Richest source of Lecithin:
explanation: Egg yolk and soybeans are well-known rich natural sources of lecithin (phosphatidylcholine).

question_text: Mevalonic acid formation is catalysed by the enzyme:
explanation: HMG-CoA reductase catalyzes the rate-limiting step in cholesterol biosynthesis, reducing HMG-CoA to mevalonate.

question_text: Enzyme referred as spreading factor:
explanation: Hyaluronidase is known as the spreading factor because it degrades hyaluronic acid, increasing tissue permeability.

question_text: The ex-officio member of Pharmacy Council of India is:
explanation: The Director of the Central Drugs Laboratory (CDL) serves as an ex-officio member of the Pharmacy Council of India.

question_text: Casein is an example of:
explanation: Casein is a major phosphoprotein found in mammalian milk.

question_text: Immunoglobulin found on lymphocyte surface of new born:
explanation: IgM and IgD are typically expressed on the surface of mature B lymphocytes.

question_text: Antigenic preparations made from extra cellular toxins:
explanation: Toxoids are modified bacterial exotoxins that have been detoxified while retaining their antigenicity.

question_text: Enzyme which is used in the treatment of leukaemia:
explanation: L-asparaginase is utilized in chemotherapy to treat acute lymphoblastic leukemia by depleting circulating asparagine.

question_text: One tea spoon full is:
explanation: Traditionally, a standard metric teaspoonful in pharmacy corresponds to approximately $4\text{ ml}$ or $5\text{ ml}$ ($4\text{ ml}$ is common in classic British/Indian pharmacopoeial equivalence tables).

question_text: A drug consist, in full or in whole or in part, of any filthy, putrid or decomposed substance:
explanation: Under drug regulations, a drug containing filthy, putrid, or decomposed substances is legally classified as adulterated.

question_text: Standards of disinfectant fluid comes under:
explanation: Schedule O of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act outlines standards for disinfectant fluids.

question_text: Which vitamin is known as antisterility factor?
explanation: Vitamin E is historically known as the anti-sterility factor because deficiency was found to cause reproductive failure in rats.

question_text: Sodium chloride injection IP contains:
explanation: Normal saline (Sodium Chloride Injection IP) is an isotonic solution containing $0.9\%\text{ w/v}$ of sodium chloride.

question_text: An opaque covering agent used in bleaches:
explanation: Titanium dioxide is a widely used opacifying agent in cosmetic and pharmaceutical formulations.

question_text: Which one of the following dryer is known as Lyophiliser?
explanation: A freeze dryer is also known as a lyophiliser, which removes water by sublimation under vacuum.

question_text: Autoclaving of ampoules in a dye bath as:
explanation: The dye bath test involving autoclaving is a standard method for leaker testing of sealed ampoules.

question_text: High count of WBC's is an indication of:
explanation: Leukemia is characterized by a significant, uncontrolled increase in the count of white blood cells (WBCs).

question_text: Example of an antioxidant:
explanation: Gallic acid and its derivatives are well-known phenolic antioxidants.

question_text: Isotonic vehicle used to prepare ophthalmic solution:
explanation: $1.9\%$ Boric acid solution is isotonic with tear fluid and serves as an ophthalmic vehicle and buffer.

question_text: Repeated administration of drug results in cell receptor blockage. This is known as:
explanation: Tolerance describes the gradual decrease in responsiveness to a drug following repeated administration.

question_text: Sterilization by autoclaving:
explanation: Autoclaving uses steam under pressure, which is classified as moist heat sterilization.

question_text: Keller-Killiani test is the identification test for:
explanation: Keller-Killiani test is used to detect deoxysugars characteristic of cardiac glycosides present in Digitalis.

question_text: THC is a constituent found in the plant:
explanation: Tetrahydrocannabinol (THC) is the principal psychoactive constituent of the Cannabis plant.

question_text: Which is the highly perfused organ in the body?
explanation: The liver receives dual blood supply and is among the most highly perfused organs in the human body.

question_text: Diatomaceous earth is the other name of:
explanation: Diatomaceous earth is also known as kieselguhr and is used as a filtering aid.

question_text: Cotton consists of epidermal trichomes of species:
explanation: Purified cotton consists of epidermal trichomes of seeds of Gossypium species such as Gossypium herbaceum.

question_text: The working principle of hammer mill:
explanation: A hammer mill primarily operates on the principle of impact to reduce particle size.

question_text: Partial or complete removal of top or bottom of a tablet is known as:
explanation: Capping is the partial or complete separation of the top or bottom crowns of a tablet from the main body.

question_text: Mother clove is an adulterant of:
explanation: Mother cloves (ripe fruits of the clove tree) are commonly used as an adulterant for genuine clove flower buds.

question_text: Tablets are designed to exert local effect in throat:
explanation: Lozenges are solid preparations designed to dissolve slowly in the mouth to release medication for a local effect in the throat.

question_text: A plant drug which lowers blood pressure:
explanation: Rauwolfia serpentina contains reserpine, a well-known alkaloid used as an antihypertensive agent.

question_text: The minimum required area to open a retail drug store is:
explanation: According to pharmacy regulations in many jurisdictions (such as India), the minimum area required for a retail drug store is 10 square meters.

question_text: Enteric coated tablets are designed to release medicament in:
explanation: Enteric coatings are acid-resistant and designed to prevent release in the stomach, releasing the drug in the alkaline environment of the small intestine.

question_text: Dryer used for the production of milk powder:
explanation: Spray drying is the standard industrial method used for producing milk powder from liquid milk due to rapid evaporation.

question_text: Vapaside is an insecticide which is formulated from:
explanation: Pyrethrum is widely used as a natural botanical insecticide.

question_text: Jesuit's bark is the synonym of:
explanation: Cinchona bark is historically known as Jesuit's bark because it was introduced to Europe by Jesuit missionaries.

question_text: Renin a proteolytic enzyme which is produced in:
explanation: Renin is an aspartic protease synthesized, stored, and secreted by the juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney.

question_text: An example of potassium sparing diuretics:
explanation: Triamterene is a potassium-sparing diuretic that acts directly on the renal distal tubules.

question_text: Alkylating agent used as antineoplastic drug:
explanation: Nitrogen mustard is a classic alkylating antineoplastic agent.

question_text: Abrasive agent used in dentifrices:
explanation: Calcium carbonate is commonly used as a polishing and abrasive agent in toothpaste formulations.

question_text: First line agent used in Tuberculosis:
explanation: Isoniazid is a primary first-line medication for the treatment of tuberculosis.

question_text: Reagent used for the identification of cellulose:
explanation: Chlorzinc iodine (sometimes referred to as van Urk's or similar specific identification reagents) or specialized iodine tests are used, but among choices, Vanurk's or equivalent is selected; typically chlorzinc iodine turns cellulose blue/violet.

question_text: Drug used in uterine inertia:
explanation: Oxytocin is used to stimulate uterine contractions in uterine inertia during labor.

question_text: Dimethicone is the other name of:
explanation: Dimethicone is polymerized siloxane, commonly known as medical grade silicone oil.

question_text: Drug used in ulcerative colitis:
explanation: Sulfasalazine is a standard anti-inflammatory drug used in the management of ulcerative colitis.

question_text: Drug that act by lowering the plasma LDL level:
explanation: Fibrates like clofibrate are lipid-lowering agents that reduce plasma triglyceride and LDL levels.

question_text: Other name of regenerated cellulose:
explanation: Rayon is a manufactured fiber composed of regenerated cellulose.

question_text: An example of rapidly acting anticoagulant:
explanation: Heparin acts rapidly as an injectable anticoagulant, unlike oral anticoagulants such as warfarin.

question_text: Water soluble constituent of Ergot:
explanation: Ergometrine (ergonovine) is uniquely water-soluble among the principal ergot alkaloids.

question_text: Yeast is the richest source of:
explanation: Yeast is well-known as an exceptionally rich natural source of B-complex vitamins.

question_text: Drug used to test gastric acid secretion:
explanation: Histamine (or pentagastrin) is historically used as a stimulant to test gastric acid secretory capacity.

question_text: Shick test is performed to test the degree of immunity against:
explanation: The Schick test is a clinical skin test used to determine whether a person is susceptible to diphtheria.

question_text: Example of ultra short acting barbiturates:
explanation: Thiopental sodium is an ultra-short-acting barbiturate used for induction of anesthesia.

question_text: Rasping method is used to prepare:
explanation: Lemon oil and other citrus oils are traditionally obtained by the rasping (or ecuelle) method from the fruit peel.

question_text: Chemical name of plaster of paris:
explanation: Plaster of Paris is calcium sulfate hemihydrate ($CaSO_4 \cdot \frac{1}{2}H_2O$).

question_text: Which one of the following is a beta-lactamase inhibitor?
explanation: Sulbactam is a beta-lactamase inhibitor given in combination with beta-lactam antibiotics.

question_text: Oxytocin is the hormone released from:
explanation: Oxytocin is synthesized in the hypothalamus and released from the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland.

question_text: Scurvy is the deficiency symptom of vitamin:
explanation: Scurvy is caused by a deficiency of vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

question_text: Millipore filters are examples of which type of filters used in sterilization :
explanation: Millipore filters are well-known membrane filters utilized for sterile filtration.

question_text: Enhanced sterilizing action of moist heat is mainly due to :
explanation: Moist heat kills microorganisms primarily by coagulating and denaturing cellular proteins and protoplasm.

question_text: Which of the following is true about disinfection?

options.A: Destroys all viable forms of microorganisms
options.B: Done by physical and chemical methods
options.C: Cannot be used for producing sterile products

explanation: Disinfection reduces pathogenic microorganisms but does not necessarily eliminate all microbial forms, hence it cannot guarantee absolute sterility.

question_text: Sieve number used for wet screening of granules in moist granulation process of tablet manufacturing :
explanation: Sieve No. 10 is commonly used for wet screening of damp granules in conventional wet granulation.

question_text: Super disintegrants used as tablet excipients :

options.C: are mainly modified starches and cellulose

explanation: Super disintegrants are effective at low concentrations, act by rapid swelling/disruption, and are typically modified celluloses and starches.

question_text: Inadequate removal of air from granules in the die cavity before and during compression of tablets leads to :
explanation: Entrapped air in granules during compression expands upon ejection, causing the top or bottom crown of the tablet to separate, known as capping.

question_text: Disintegration test for uncoated tablets is carried out using which of the following immersion liquid at $37\pm2^{\circ}$ :
explanation: Water is typically used as the standard immersion liquid for the disintegration test of ordinary uncoated tablets.

question_text: Film forming polymer commonly used in film coating of tablets :
explanation: Hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC) is the most widely used water-soluble polymer for conventional tablet film coating.

question_text: Most suitable capsule number used for filling 450 mg of a powder fill :
explanation: Size 0 hard gelatin capsules typically hold approximately 500 mg depending on bulk density, making size 0 suitable for 450 mg.

question_text: Which of the following is not a Quality control test for capsules?
explanation: Friability test is performed exclusively on compressed tablets, not on capsules.

question_text: In the formulation of suspension which of the following is the use of non-ionic surfactant :
explanation: Surfactants are commonly employed in suspensions to reduce interfacial tension and act as wetting or flocculating agents.

question_text: The HLB value of Sorbitan monoleate is :
explanation: Sorbitan monooleate (Span 80) has a standard HLB value of approximately 4.3.

question_text: Resinous drugs containing preparations fall into which category of suspension :
explanation: Resinous matter does not readily wet or diffuse uniformly, making them indiffusible solids requiring a suspending agent.

question_text: Preservative used in the formulation of emulsion :
explanation: Benzoic acid and its derivatives (like parabens) are classical antimicrobial preservatives used in aqueous emulsion phases.

question_text: Humectant used in the formulation of dental preparations :
explanation: Propylene glycol (along with glycerin and sorbitol) is commonly used as a humectant in toothpastes to prevent moisture loss.

question_text: Materials used to impart lustre to the hair and keep hair in place :
explanation: Brilliantines are hair grooming preparations used to impart shine and keep hair in place.

question_text: Dye used for leaker test for the evaluation of parenteral products :
explanation: Methylene blue dye solution is standardly used in dye immersion tests to detect container-closure leaks in ampoules.

question_text: Which among the following is an example of water miscible non aqueous solvent used in the preparation parenteral preparations?
explanation: Polyethylene glycol 400 (PEG 400) is a water-miscible co-solvent used in parenteral formulations.

question_text: The bactericide used in ophthalmic preparation must be rapidly effective against wide range of microorganisms particularly :
explanation: Pseudomonas aeruginosa is notoriously hazardous in eye infections, making rapid bactericidal activity against it mandatory for ophthalmic preservatives.

question_text: Eye drops are sterilised by :
explanation: Depending on the formulation stability, eye drops can be sterilized via autoclaving, heating with a bactericide, or membrane filtration.

question_text: The available iodine in povidone-iodine, calculated on dry basis, is :
explanation: According to pharmacopeial standards, povidone-iodine contains between 9.0% and 12.0% available iodine on a dry basis.

question_text: Which of the following statement about Boric acid is correct?

options.C: Having a very low dissociation constant

explanation: Boric acid is a very weak monobasic Lewis acid with a very low dissociation constant ($K_a \approx 5.8 \times 10^{-10}$), making it weaker than carbonic acid.

question_text: The emulsifying action of borax on oils is due to the presence of free alkali formed by :
explanation: Borax undergoes hydrolysis in water to yield sodium hydroxide (free alkali), which reacts with fatty acids in oils to form natural soaps acting as emulsifiers.

question_text: The pellets of sodium hydroxide should be kept in well-closed bottles because it is :

options.B: Highly deliquescent and absorbs carbon dioxide from the air
options.C: Highly hygroscopic and absorbs oxygen from the air

explanation: Sodium hydroxide is deliquescent and reacts readily with atmospheric carbon dioxide to form sodium carbonate.

question_text: Which of the following statement about mild silver protein is not correct?

options.C: Silver rendered colloidal by combination with protein
options.D: Contains less amount of silver than strong silver protein

explanation: Mild silver protein actually contains a higher percentage of silver (approx 19-23%) compared to strong silver protein (7-8%), making statement D incorrect.

question_text: The suitable calcium salt as a stabilizer used in the official calcium gluconate intravenous injection is :
explanation: Calcium D-saccharate is added as a stabilizing agent to official calcium gluconate injections to prevent supersaturation and precipitation.

question_text: Which of the following drug is effective in treating severe metabolic alkalosis when administered intravenously?
explanation: Ammonium chloride IV injection is used to acidify the extracellular fluid and treat severe metabolic alkalosis.

question_text: “Tartar emetic” is chemically known as :
explanation: Tartar emetic is the traditional name for potassium antimonyl tartrate or antimony potassium tartrate.

question_text: All of the following are official compounds of Iron EXCEPT :
explanation: Ferric sulfate is an astringent/hemostatic reagent and not an official therapeutic iron supplement compound like the others.

question_text: All of the following statements about Lugol’s solution are correct EXCEPT :

options.B: Contains more amount of potassium iodide than iodine
options.C: Otherwise called aqueous solution of iodine

explanation: Lugol's solution (aqueous iodine solution) can indeed be taken by mouth (e.g., for thyroid storm preparation), making statement D incorrect.

question_text: All of the following statements regarding Benzalkonium chloride are true EXCEPT :
explanation: Benzalkonium chloride is readily soluble in water and alcohol, making option C false.

question_text: All of the following compounds exhibit amphoteric properties EXCEPT :
explanation: Benzyl penicillin contains a carboxylic acid group but lacks a basic amino group that confers true amphoteric properties, unlike the others.

question_text: All of the following are anti-tubercular antibiotics EXCEPT :
explanation: Erythromycin is a macrolide antibiotic primarily used for gram-positive respiratory infections, not tuberculosis.

question_text: An aromatic nitro compound, used as a broad spectrum antibiotic :
explanation: Chloramphenicol features a characteristic p-nitrophenyl aromatic nitro group and is a broad-spectrum antibiotic.

question_text: Which of the following statement about chloroquine is correct?

options.B: Used for both prophylaxis and treatment of malaria
options.C: For the treatment of extra intestinal amoebiasis

explanation: Chloroquine is a 4-aminoquinoline used for malaria prophylaxis and treatment, and also for extraintestinal amebiasis like liver abscess.

question_text: A drug which belongs to fluorobutyrophenone with antipsychotic activity :
explanation: Haloperidol is a classical butyrophenone antipsychotic containing a fluorophenyl group.

question_text: Diazepam is used :
explanation: Diazepam is a benzodiazepine widely used as an anxiolytic, anticonvulsant, and skeletal muscle relaxant in spasticity.

question_text: Adrenaline is light sensitive and easily oxidised on exposure to air because of the moiety in adrenaline :
explanation: The ortho-diphenol (catechol) ring system in adrenaline is readily oxidized to quinone derivatives upon exposure to light and air.

question_text: The most widely used anticholinesterase agent for treating myasthenia gravis :
explanation: Pyridostigmine is a carbamate acetylcholinesterase inhibitor that serves as the standard chronic oral treatment for myasthenia gravis.

question_text: Most of the anti-neoplastic alkylating agents contain :
explanation: Alkylating agents act by generating reactive electrophilic species that form covalent adducts with cellular nucleophiles like DNA.

question_text: Which of the following plant is commonly known as Henbane?
explanation: Hyoscyamus niger is commonly known as henbane.

question_text: Meconic acid is a dibasic acid found in :
explanation: Meconic acid is a characteristic organic acid found exclusively in opium (Papaver somniferum).

question_text: Hallucinogenic drug LSD is prepared from :
explanation: Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) is semisynthetically produced from lysergic acid derived from ergot alkaloids (Claviceps purpurea).

question_text: Cinnamon is the dried inner bark of the coppiced shoots of Cinnamomum zeylanicum Nees., belonging to family Lauraceae. Coppicing means :
explanation: Coppicing is the practice of cutting woody plants close to the ground level to stimulate vigorous shoot growth.

question_text: Cardamom consists of the dried ripe seeds of Elettaria cardamomum Maton., belonging to family :
explanation: Cardamom belongs to the ginger family, Zingiberaceae.

question_text: Guggal is a gum resin obtained by incision of the bark of :
explanation: Guggul gum resin is tapped from the plant species Commiphora mukul.

question_text: Hydnocarpic acid is a constituent of :
explanation: Chaulmoogra oil contains cyclopentenyl fatty acids, notably hydnocarpic acid and chaulmoogric acid, historically used for leprosy.

question_text: In Fiehe’s test for honey, on addition of which reagent gives a transient red colour for natural honey :
explanation: Fiehe's test utilizes resorcinol (in hydrochloric acid) to detect adulteration with commercial invert sugar in honey.

question_text: Narcotic effect of Nutmeg is due to the presence of :
explanation: Myristicin is the primary phenylpropene constituent responsible for the psychoactive and narcotic effects of nutmeg.

question_text: Epidermis with thick-waved, bent and twisted lignified covering trichomes are characteristic feature of :
explanation: Ephedra species are characterized by thick-waved, bent, and twisted lignified covering trichomes on their epidermis.

question_text: Weight gain can be a side effect of the following anticonvulsants :
explanation: Valproic acid is well-known to cause weight gain and increased appetite as a common adverse metabolic effect.

question_text: Dipivefrine is an :
explanation: Dipivefrine is a prodrug formed by the diesterification of epinephrine and pivalic acid, used to treat glaucoma.

question_text: Timolol has the following features except :
explanation: Timolol is a non-selective beta-blocker (blocking both beta-1 and beta-2 receptors), making option D incorrect.

question_text: Therapeutic index of digitalis is :
explanation: Digitalis (digoxin) has a narrow margin of safety, meaning its therapeutic index is low.

question_text: Sulfonamides are not effective in the presence of pus because they are rich in :
explanation: Pus contains breakdown products of cellular debris, particularly para-aminobenzoic acid (PABA), which competitively inhibits sulfonamides.

question_text: Diacetylmorphine is :
explanation: Diacetylmorphine is the chemical IUPAC-derived name for heroin.

question_text: Which endogenous substance depletion potentiates paracetamol toxicity?
explanation: Depletion of hepatic glutathione leads to accumulation of toxic NAPQI metabolite, causing paracetamol-induced hepatotoxicity.

question_text: Select the long-acting semisynthetic tetracycline :
explanation: Minocycline and doxycycline are long-acting tetracyclines derived semisynthetically.

question_text: Doxapram is :
explanation: Doxapram is a central nervous system stimulant that primarily acts as a respiratory stimulant.

question_text: Which of the following is not an intravenous anesthetic?
explanation: Sevoflurane is an inhaled volatile general anesthetic, not an intravenous one.

question_text: The life period of polio vaccine when stored at minus 20°C is :
explanation: Oral polio vaccine (OPV) stored at -20°C typically maintains its potency for 24 months.

question_text: As per Drugs and Cosmetic act 1940 and Rules 1945, "Cool Place" means place having a temperature between :
explanation: Under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, a cool place is defined as a place with temperatures between 8°C and 25°C.

question_text: The flowering or fruiting tops of the cannabis plant (excluding the seeds and leaves when not accompanied by the tops), by whatever name they may be known or designated is known as :
explanation: Ganja is legally defined as the flowering or fruiting tops of the cannabis plant.

question_text: Who among the following is not the member of Central council of Pharmacy council of India?

options.A: Representative of the University Grants Commission
options.B: Representative of the All India Council for Technical Education
options.C: Representative of Indian Council of Medical research

explanation: ICMR representative is typically not a designated member of the PCI under the Pharmacy Act.

question_text: "If the label or container bears the name of an individual or company purporting to be the manufacturer of the drug, which individual or company is fictitious or does not exist" it belongs to :
explanation: Drugs with fictitious manufacturing names are classified as spurious drugs under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act.

question_text: The nominated member of Pharmacy Council of India shall hold office for a term of how many years from the date of his : (I) 5 years (II) 3 years (III) 6 years (IV) Until his successor has been duly nominated
explanation: Nominated members of the PCI hold office for 5 years and continue until their successor is nominated (I and IV).

question_text: Which among the following conditions, in which their advertisements are prohibited?
explanation: Under the Drugs and Magic Remedies Act, advertisements for all these conditions are strictly prohibited.

question_text: Any product of opium by any series of operations designed to transform opium an extract suitable for smoking and the dross or other residue remaining after opium is smoked is :
explanation: Prepared opium is legally defined as any product of opium obtained through operations to make it suitable for smoking.

question_text: The pack size of Albendazole suspension :
explanation: Standard paediatric single-dose packs of Albendazole oral suspension are typically formulated in 10 ml bottles.

question_text: Application for grant of a licence to sell, stock, exhibit or offer for sale, or distribute drugs other than those specified in Schedule X by wholesale is in :
explanation: Form 19AA is the application form for wholesale licenses of drugs other than Schedule X drugs.

question_text: The upsurge in prices for goods and services is called :
explanation: An ongoing rise in the general price level of goods and services in an economy is defined as inflation.

question_text: Which among the following comes under current liability?
explanation: Bank overdraft is a short-term obligation categorized as a current liability.

question_text: Incentives are a part of :
explanation: Trade promotions frequently utilize monetary and non-monetary incentives to encourage distributors and retailers.

question_text: Which among the following is a constraint of sole proprietorship?

options.A: No sharing of profit and loss

explanation: A major disadvantage or constraint of a sole proprietorship is the unlimited (infinite) personal liability of the owner.

question_text: Request indicator refers to :
explanation: Reorder level serves as the indicator that triggers a request or replenishment order.

question_text: The term capital refers to :
explanation: Capital (owner's equity) is calculated mathematically as total assets minus total liabilities.

question_text: Aisle interrupter is a part of :
explanation: An aisle interrupter is a retail point-of-sale display used as a sales promotion tool.

question_text: Which among the following committee was constituted by Govt. of India to rationalize the price structure of drugs?
explanation: The Hathi Committee was appointed by the Government of India in 1974 to review and rationalize drug prices and the pharmaceutical industry.

question_text: When a given event affects both revenue and expenses, the effect on each should be recognized in the same period is a part of?
explanation: The matching concept requires that expenses be matched with revenues generated in the same accounting period.

question_text: The salary of staff is entered in which among the following account :
explanation: Salary is an expense, and all expenses and incomes are recorded under nominal accounts.

question_text: Which among the following is NOT a primary source of information?
explanation: Textbooks are classified as tertiary literature sources, not primary sources.

question_text: Inventory control method ABC Analysis is based on which principle :
explanation: ABC analysis relies on Pareto's 80/20 principle where a small portion of items account for the majority of inventory value.

question_text: Identify factors influencing the selection of drugs in a hospital formulary : (1) Efficacy (2) Safety (3) Cost (4) Restricted use
explanation: All listed factors—efficacy, safety, cost, and restrictions on use—are critical considerations in a hospital formulary.

question_text: Average time duration between placing the order and the receipt of item is known as :
explanation: Lead time is the time elapsed between placing an order and receiving the delivered goods.

question_text: Surgical instrument with long handles and angulated blades, not having rachette and is used for picking sterile instruments and swabs at the time of surgery :
explanation: Cheetle's forceps are long-handled, angulated, ratchet-free forceps specifically used for handling sterile instruments.

question_text: All inpatient drugs are dispensed in unit doses and all the drugs are stored in main pharmacy and dispensed at the time the dose is due to be given to the patient. This system is known as :

options.A: Decentralized unit dose drug distribution system
options.C: Centralized unit dose drug distribution system

explanation: Storing and dispensing unit doses directly from a central pharmacy location describes a centralized unit dose system.

question_text: The most vital committee in a hospital which is having both advisory and educational role :
explanation: The Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee serves an advisory and educational role regarding drug therapy in hospitals.

question_text: "Clean room area" an atmosphere free from small particles of size less than 0.5 mm is given a distinct colour code :
explanation: Clean room zones and environments are traditionally designated with white color coding.

question_text: The day today assessment of all operations from receipt of raw materials to the distribution of finished products with analysis and testing of finished product is :
explanation: Quality control involves day-to-day sampling, testing, and inspection of raw materials and finished products.

question_text: Bandage which is a union fabric with more than 60% wool content with warp cotton and weft is wool :
explanation: Domette bandage is a union fabric containing over 60% wool with cotton warp and wool weft.

question_text: Glucose 6 phosphate dehydrogenase enzyme deficient persons are at risk of developing haemolytic crisis with which of the following drug group :
explanation: Sulphonamides, antimalarials, and certain other drugs precipitate hemolytic crisis in G6PD deficient patients.

question_text: In rheumatoid arthritis hypertrophy of the synovium due to sustained inflammation leads to the formation of a structure which spreads over the joint surface causing erosive destruction of cartilage and bone is :
explanation: Pannus is the abnormal layer of fibrovascular tissue that invades and destroys joint cartilage and bone in rheumatoid arthritis.

question_text: Slow acetylators are at increased risk of developing which ADR :
explanation: Type B adverse drug reactions are idiosyncratic and genetically determined, such as toxicity in slow acetylators.

question_text: Which of the following is NOT an ingredient of universal antidote?
explanation: Universal antidote consists of activated charcoal, magnesium oxide, and tannic acid; penicillamine is a chelating agent, not part of it.

question_text: In disease conditions high ESR value is observed than normal. The reason is :
explanation: Elevated acute-phase proteins (like fibrinogen and globulins) increase erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR).

question_text: The causative organism of peptic ulcer in susceptible individuals :
explanation: Helicobacter pylori is the primary bacterial causative agent responsible for peptic ulcer disease.

question_text: Faecal oral route is the mode of transmission of :
explanation: Hepatitis A and E are primarily transmitted via the fecal-oral route, unlike B, C, and D which are blood-borne.

question_text: Ingestion of alcohol along with the use of sulphonyl ureas can cause :
explanation: Alcohol can potentiate the hypoglycemic effects of sulfonylureas, sometimes leading to severe hypoglycemia.

question_text: Identify the drug which can induce hypertension in susceptible individuals :
explanation: Cyclosporine is a well-known immunosuppressant that frequently causes hypertension as an adverse effect.

question_text: A patient receiving ACE inhibitor and potassium sparing diuretic is at risk of developing :
explanation: Both ACE inhibitors and potassium-sparing diuretics retain potassium, synergistically increasing the risk of hyperkalemia.

question_text: Which of the following statements is not true for dry heat method of sterilisation?

options.A: Usually sterilisation is done by heating at a temperature of $160^\circ\text{C}$ for two hours
options.B: Destruction of microorganism is effected by oxidation of essential cell constituents
options.C: This method is not suitable for powders and oily materials
options.D: This method is not suitable for surgical dressings

explanation: Dry heat is actually very suitable for heat-stable powders and oily materials.

question_text: Enteric coating is given to tablets in order to

options.A: Protect the medicament from atmospheric effects
options.B: Ensure highest concentration of drug in the intestine
options.C: Separate chemical or physical incompatible ingredients
options.D: Prolong the duration of action of medicaments

explanation: Enteric coating resists gastric fluid and disintegrates in the intestine, ensuring drug release there.

question_text: If a capsule is numbered as 000 which means

options.A: It is the smallest sized capsule with a capacity of 100 mg
options.B: It is for the inclusion of ophthalmic ointments only
options.C: The shape of the capsule is oval
options.D: It is the largest sized and for veterinary purpose only

explanation: 000 is the largest standard capsule size used mainly for veterinary or bulk filling purposes.

question_text: Which one of the following is a correct statement regarding soft gelatin capsule?

options.A: Soft gelatin shells may contain methyl and propyl parabens as preservative
options.B: Not suitable for use as suppositories
options.D: The manufacturing and filling of medicaments are done in separate operations

explanation: Preservatives like methyl and propyl parabens are commonly added to soft gelatin shell formulations to prevent microbial growth.

question_text: For the evaluation of tablet, a test used to measure the amount of time required for the drug substance in tablet to go into solution under specified condition is known as
explanation: Dissolution test measures the rate and extent of drug substance going into solution.

question_text: Unequal distribution of colour on a tablet with light and dark areas standing out in a uniform surface is known as
explanation: Mottling is the term for unequal color distribution on a tablet surface.

question_text: Mechanism of killing microorganisms by gaseous sterilisation is
explanation: Gaseous sterilizing agents like ethylene oxide act via alkylation of cellular proteins and nucleic acids.

question_text: Role of Glycerin or sorbitol in the manufacturing of capsule shell as
explanation: Glycerin and sorbitol act as plasticizers to render the gelatin shell flexible and elastic.

question_text: Sterilisation by heating with a bactericide

options.A: Can be used safely for intrathecal injections
options.B: Not suitable for intravenous injection when single dose exceeds 15 ml
options.C: Is performed before the preparation is transferred into the final container

explanation: Heating with a bactericide is restricted for large volume intravenous injections (exceeding 15 ml) due to toxicity risks from the bactericide.

question_text: During the formulation of tablet the purpose of adding magnesium stearate as
explanation: Magnesium stearate is widely used as a tablet and capsule lubricant to prevent adhesion to compression equipment.

question_text: Lugol's solution is
explanation: Lugol's solution is an aqueous solution of iodine and potassium iodide.

question_text: Which one of the following is a common ingredient in ear drops as dewaxing agent?
explanation: Hydrogen peroxide releases oxygen and helps soften and loosen earwax.

question_text: Penicillamine is an antidote used in the poisoning of
explanation: Penicillamine is a chelating agent used to treat copper (Wilson's disease) and lead poisoning.

question_text: An oxidative antimicrobial agent is
explanation: Sodium hypochlorite exerts its antimicrobial effect primarily through oxidation.

question_text: Which of the following is an incorrect statement regarding ammonium chloride?

options.A: It is an irritating expectorant and used as an ingredient in cough mixtures
options.B: Given to aid easy elimination in lead poisoning
options.C: In the liver it is metabolised into urea
options.D: It is used as a systemic alkaliniser

explanation: Ammonium chloride is an acidifying agent, not an alkaliniser, as it dissociates into hydrogen and chloride ions.

question_text: which one of the following is used for the treatment of schistosomiasis (Kala-azar) and administered intravenously?
explanation: Antimony potassium tartrate (tartar emetic) has historically been used for schistosomiasis.

question_text: A sulphur compound which is a common ingredient in shampoos and lotions for the treatment of dandruff and seborrhoeic dermatitis
explanation: Selenium sulfide is widely used in anti-dandruff shampoos.

question_text: Green vitriol is
explanation: Green vitriol is the common name for hydrated ferrous sulfate.

question_text: Prolonged use of silver preparation may lead to a condition known as
explanation: Argyria is a condition caused by prolonged exposure to silver preparations, characterized by blue-gray skin discoloration.

question_text: An organic mercury compound which is commonly used as antiseptic/antifungal agent is
explanation: Thiomersal (thimerosal) is an organomercury compound used as an antiseptic and antifungal agent.

question_text: Viscosity builders used in Ophthalmic formulation
explanation: Carboxymethyl cellulose is commonly used as a viscosity-imparting agent in eye drops to increase retention time.

question_text: Thickening of a shampoo may be carried by addition of
explanation: Carboxy vinyl polymers (carbomers) are widely used thickening agents in cosmetics and shampoos.

question_text: Eye Ointment base should melt at
explanation: Eye ointment bases must melt or soften at body temperature to ensure proper drug release and avoid irritation.

question_text: For preparation of emulsions using fixed oil the ratio of oil: water : Gum
explanation: The standard primary emulsion ratio for fixed oils using gum acacia is 4:2:1 (Oil:Water:Gum).

question_text: Suspensions are biphasic liquid dosage form of medicament in which the finely divided solid particles ranging from
explanation: Suspended solid particles in pharmaceutical suspensions typically range between 0.5 to 5.0 microns.

question_text: Example for semi-synthetic thickening agents in suspension
explanation: Microcrystalline cellulose is a semi-synthetic cellulose derivative used as a suspending and thickening agent.

question_text: Which among the ingredients is used for the preparation of concentrated Haemodialysis fluid B.P.C.?
explanation: Sodium acetate is commonly used as a buffer source in haemodialysis fluids.

question_text: Examples of liquid Anti perspirants
explanation: Aluminium chlorohydrate is widely used as an active antiperspirant ingredient.

question_text: Hair remover is otherwise called
explanation: Chemical hair removers are known as depilatories.

question_text: Rubber closures are washed with hot solution of
explanation: Rubber closures are typically washed with a 0.2% sodium pyrophosphate solution to remove surface impurities.

question_text: Vasaka contains _________ % w/w of vasicine calculated on the dried basis
explanation: Vasaka (Adhatoda vasica) contains not less than 0.5% vasicine on a dried basis according to pharmacopeial standards.

question_text: Tulsi comes under category
explanation: Ocimum sanctum (Tulsi) is well known for its immunomodulatory properties.

question_text: Peppermint oil is obtained by
explanation: Volatile oils like peppermint oil are typically extracted using steam distillation.

question_text: Powdered ergot when treated with ________ solution develops strong odour of trimethylamine
explanation: Treatment of ergot with sodium hydroxide releases free trimethylamine, producing a characteristic strong fishy odor.

question_text: Terminalia Arjuna is used as
explanation: Terminalia arjuna bark is traditionally used in indigenous systems of medicine for cardiovascular diseases and liver disorders including jaundice.

question_text: Active constituent of Rhubarb
explanation: Rhubarb contains anthraquinone derivatives such as rhein, emodin, and chrysophanol.

question_text: Anti-sweetening agent in Gymnema sylvestre
explanation: Gymnemic acids are the active anti-sweetening principles found in the leaves of Gymnema sylvestre.

question_text: Ergotoxine test gives __________ colour
explanation: Ergot alkaloids give a characteristic deep purple or blue-violet color with p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde (Van Urk's reagent).

question_text: Triphala and chyavanprash contain
explanation: Amla (Emblica officinalis) is a primary ingredient in both Triphala and Chyavanprash.

question_text: Main triglycerides in castor oil
explanation: Castor oil consists mainly of tricinolein, which is the triglyceride of ricinoleic acid.

question_text: The antiseptic which is an acridine derivative
explanation: Proflavine is an antiseptic acridine dye derivative.
