question_text: In Quantitative T.L.C. radioactive material can be studied by
explanation: Radioactive materials on TLC plates are quantified using radiation detectors such as a Geiger counter or scintillation counters.

question_text: One of the following ingredients which improves the flow property of granules is:
explanation: Glidants are added to powder formulations to improve flow properties by reducing interparticle friction.

question_text: The wavelength source in N.M.R. spectrometer is
explanation: Nuclear Magnetic Resonance (NMR) spectroscopy utilizes radiofrequency radiation generated by an RF oscillator.

question_text: One of the following materials is used for the preparation of master grating. Identify
explanation: Master diffraction gratings are typically ruled on aluminum-coated surfaces or blanks due to its reflective properties and ductility.

question_text: Benzathine penicillin is

options.A: An equimolecular composition of Amoxicillin + N.N dibenzyl ethylene diamine
options.B: A molecular complexation of Benzyl penicillin+ N.N dibenzyl ethylene diamine
options.C: A molecular complexation of Cloxacillin + ethylene diamine
options.D: Equimolecular proportion of Amoxicillin + ethylene diamine

explanation: Benzathine penicillin G is formed by the salt formation/complexation of benzyl penicillin with N,N'-dibenzylethylenediamine.

question_text: Schick test is performed to ascertain susceptibility to
explanation: The Schick test is a clinical skin test used to determine whether a person is susceptible to diphtheria.

question_text: Which of the following commonly available large volume dextrose solution for intravenous use is isotonic?
explanation: A $5\% \text{ w/v}$ dextrose solution in water is considered isotonic with human body fluids.

question_text: The term bioavailability refers to the

options.A: Relationship between the physical and chemical properties of a drug and the systemic absorption of the drug
options.B: Measurement of the rate and amount of therapeutically active drug that reaches the systemic circulation
options.C: Movement of drug into the body tissues over time
options.D: Dissolution of a drug in the gastrointestinal tract

explanation: Bioavailability is defined as the rate and extent to which the active ingredient is absorbed from a drug product and becomes available at the site of action.

question_text: Among the propellants used in aerosols one of the following is used for topical pharmaceutical aerosols.
explanation: Trichloromonofluoromethane (Propellant 11) and Dichlorodifluoromethane (Propellant 12) are standard chlorofluorocarbon propellants historically used in aerosols.

question_text: The principal structural component of the cell wall in bacteria is made up of
explanation: Bacterial cell walls are primarily composed of peptidoglycan (murein), a polymer consisting of sugars and amino acids.

question_text: Which of the following has the highest degree of ionization in an aqueous solution?
explanation: A lower $\text{pK}_a$ value for a weak acid indicates a stronger acid, which ionizes to a greater extent at a given pH.

question_text: Tetracyclines are avoided during pregnancy because

options.B: It may affect the bone growth of foetus
options.C: It causes discolouration of mothers teeth

explanation: Tetracyclines bind to calcium in developing teeth and bones, leading to dental staining and inhibition of bone growth in the fetus.

question_text: The Xenobiotics that does not cause nephrotoxicity is
explanation: Isoniazid is primarily metabolized by the liver (acetylation) and is not typically associated with direct nephrotoxicity like cisplatin, aminoglycosides, or streptozocin.

question_text: Which of the following function of OPIOID receptors?
explanation: Opioid receptor activation inhibits presynaptic calcium channels and opens potassium channels, leading to a decrease in the release of neurotransmitters such as norepinephrine.

question_text: Assume that a typical type of Cancer is susceptible to an individual drug. Listed below are some therapeutic combination of anti-cancer drugs which are rationale except one. Identify.
explanation: Chlorambucil and Melphalan are both alkylating agents with similar mechanisms and overlapping toxicities, making their combination irrational.

question_text: One of the following emissions from the decay of Radio nuclides is commonly used in sterilization. Identify
explanation: Gamma rays (typically from Cobalt-60) have high penetration power and are widely used for industrial radiation sterilization.

question_text: Clinically available anticancer agents have one of the underlying mechanism of action, they act by

options.C: Receptor site blockade of cancer cell content

explanation: Anticancer agents function primarily by inhibiting cell growth, proliferation, and inducing apoptosis in rapidly dividing cells.

question_text: Listed below are some of the common Radio nuclides used in Nuclear Pharmacy which one is generator produced?
explanation: Technetium-99m ($^{99m}\text{Tc}$) is obtained commercially using a Molybdenum-99/Technetium-99m generator.

question_text: Smallpox Vaccine contains
explanation: The smallpox vaccine contains live vaccinia virus, which is closely related to the smallpox virus.

question_text: The solution strength of $\text{Ca}^{++}$ in terms of $\text{mg/L}$ for a Calcium injection which contains $5\text{ mEq. Calcium}$ ($\text{Ca}^{++}$) per $100\text{ ml}$ is given below. Identify the correct one. [At $40\text{ wt} - \text{Ca}^{++} = 40$].
explanation: Calculation: $5\text{ mEq/100 mL} = 50\text{ mEq/L}$. Equivalent weight of $\text{Ca}^{++} = 40 / 2 = 20\text{ g/Eq} = 20\text{ mg/mEq}$. $\text{Concentration} = 50\text{ mEq/L} \times 20\text{ mg/mEq} = 1000\text{ mg/L}$.

question_text: Listed below are some of the drug intermediates. Choose the correct one for the synthesis of Procainamide.

options.A: p-nitro benzyl chloride and Diethyl amino ethylamine
options.B: p-nitro benzyl chloride and ethyl amino ethylamine
options.C: p-nitro cinnamoyl chloride and Diethyl amino ethylamine
options.D: p-nitro benzene and Diethyl amino ethylamine

explanation: Procainamide is synthesized by reacting p-nitrobenzoyl chloride with diethylaminoethylamine, followed by reduction of the nitro group.

question_text: Choose the correct name for Digitoxigenin.
explanation: Digitoxigenin is a cardenolide steroid aglycone possessing two hydroxyl groups at the $3\beta$ and $14\beta$ positions.

question_text: 2, 6-dimethyl aniline and chloro acetyl chloride are the starting compounds for the synthesis of one of the following drugs. Choose the correct one.
explanation: Lidocaine is synthesized by the reaction of 2,6-dimethylaniline with chloroacetyl chloride, followed by diethylamine displacement.

question_text: Choose the correct geneva name for TRANYL CYPROMINE.
explanation: Tranylcypromine is marketed as a racemic mixture of trans-2-phenylcyclopropylamine.

question_text: In take of which of the following should be avoided by a patient taking on oral anticoagulant?
explanation: Menadione (Vitamin K3) promotes blood clotting and antagonizes the effects of oral anticoagulants like warfarin.

question_text: Ellipsoidal schizolysigenous oil glands are important diagnostic of
explanation: Clove flower buds exhibit characteristic ellipsoidal schizolysigenous oil glands under microscopic examination.

question_text: Catecholamines act by

options.A: Decrease the amount of glucose released into the blood
options.B: Increase the utilization of glucose by muscle
options.C: Increase the amount of glucose released into the blood
options.D: Decrease the amount of glucose in the muscle.

explanation: Catecholamines (such as epinephrine) stimulate glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis, increasing blood glucose levels.

question_text: Hyoscyamine an alkaloid obtained from Atropa belladonna

options.A: Readily racemises to atropine with ethanolic alkali. Atropine is (\pm) Hyoscyamine
options.B: Readily disintegrates into atropine with acid solution. Atropine is (-) Hyoscyamine
options.C: Readily rearranges into atropine with acid solution. Atropine is (+) Hyoscyamine
options.D: Readily racemise to atropine with ethanolic alkali. Atropine is (+)...

explanation: Hyoscyamine is the levorotatory isomer, and treatment with dilute alkali readily racemizes it into racemic DL-hyoscyamine, known as atropine.

question_text: Identify the correct molecule which controls the biosynthesis of proteins in living organisms
explanation: DNA stores the master genetic code which ultimately controls protein biosynthesis via transcription and translation.

explanation: Opium alkaloids naturally occur in the plant complexed as salts of meconic acid.

options.A: One RE represents the biological activity in $1 \mu g$ of all trans retinol
options.B: One RE represents the biological activity of $30 \text{ mg}$ of all trans retinol
options.C: One RE represents the biological activity of $0.334 \text{ } \mu \text{g}$ of all trans retinol

explanation: One retinol equivalent (RE) corresponds to $1 \mu \text{g}$ of all-trans-retinol.

question_text: Which of the antineoplastic agent is metabolised by xanthine oxidase?
explanation: Mercaptopurine is inactivated by xanthine oxidase, which is why allopurinol interacts with it.

question_text: The energy of a photon is given by the relationship $E = h\nu$, where

options.A: $E$ is energy of photon in kilo-calories
options.B: $E$ is energy of photon in cycles/sec
options.C: $E$ is the energy of photon in joules
options.D: $E$ is the energy of photon in ergs

explanation: In standard SI units for Planck's relation, energy $E$ is measured in joules.

question_text: Gas chromatographic technique can be used for
explanation: Gas chromatography is widely used for both qualitative identification (via retention time) and quantitative determination.

question_text: Reference compound widely used in NMR spectroscopy for proton spectra in non-aqueous medium is:
explanation: Tetramethylsilane (TMS) is the universal reference standard for $^1\text{H}$ NMR in non-aqueous organic solvents.

question_text: Liposomes are

options.A: Uni or multilayered vesicles of phospholipids

explanation: Liposomes consist of phospholipid bilayers forming spherical vesicles.

question_text: The gonadal hormones like Estrogens, Androgens and Progestins bind with

options.B: Receptors located in the nucleus of the cell
options.C: Receptors located in the contractile vacuoles

explanation: Steroid hormone receptors primarily function as nuclear receptors.

question_text: A highly sensitive semi quantitative method of detecting microbial antigens in biological fluid is:
explanation: Counterimmunoelectrophoresis is commonly employed for rapid detection of microbial antigens.

question_text: Polyene antibiotics such as Amphotericin - B are most likely to

options.D: React with sterols in the membrane

explanation: Amphotericin B binds to ergosterol in fungal cell membranes, creating pores that lead to cell death.

question_text: Among the following statements one of them is most appropriate for $\gamma$ - Interferon. Identify.

options.A: They are virus specific substances and not host specific, naturally occurring glycol-proteins.
options.B: They are not virus specific substances, however, they are naturally occurring glycol-proteins.
options.C: They are not virus specific substances, however they are not host specific either. They are naturally occurring glycol-proteins.
options.D: They are virus specific and host specific naturally occurring glycoproteins.

explanation: Interferons are host-specific, non-virus-specific glycoproteins with antiviral and immunomodulatory activities.

question_text: The tear secretion contains an antibacterial enzyme known as
explanation: Lysozyme is an antimicrobial enzyme found in tears and other bodily secretions.

question_text: A list of ACE inhibition is given below. One of them is not a Prodrug. Identify.
explanation: Captopril is an active drug and does not require ester hydrolysis unlike most other ACE inhibitors.

question_text: Which one of the following is not a pharmacological effect of MORPHINE?
explanation: Morphine causes constipation, not diarrhoea, due to decreased gastrointestinal motility.

question_text: Half life equation for First order reaction is:
explanation: The half-life for a first-order reaction is independent of initial concentration and equals $0.693/K$.

question_text: Which one of the following is true for alkaloidal bases?

options.A: Water solubility and organic solvent insolubility.
options.B: Water insolubility and organic solvent insolubility.
options.C: Water solubility and organic solvent solubility
options.D: Water insolubility and organic solvent solubility

explanation: Free alkaloidal bases are typically insoluble in water but soluble in organic solvents.

question_text: The conductivity of the solution of an electrolysis is:
explanation: Electrolytic conductivity varies significantly with temperature due to changes in ion mobility and viscosity.

question_text: One of the materials listed below is most commonly used in film coating of tablets. Identify.
explanation: HPMC is the industry standard polymer used for pharmaceutical film coating.

question_text: Lamination is:

options.A: Separation of a tablet into two or more distinct layers
options.B: Partial and complete separation of the top and bottom crowns from the main body of the tablet

explanation: Lamination refers to the separation of a tablet into two or more distinct horizontal layers.

question_text: Among the four OPIOIDS given below one of them is equipotent on $\mu$, $\delta$, $k_1$ and $k_3$ receptor types. Identify.
explanation: Morphine acts across various opioid receptor subtypes.

question_text: An amperometric titrations which one of the following is kept constant?
explanation: In amperometry, a constant potential is applied to the indicator electrode while measuring current.

question_text: Disposable syringes are made up of
explanation: Polypropylene is widely used for manufacturing medical-grade disposable syringes.

question_text: Typhoid vaccine IP is a sterile suspension or a freeze dried solid prepared from
explanation: Typhoid vaccines are prepared from killed or attenuated Salmonella typhi.

question_text: In the microbiological assay of bacitracin \ce{IP} the test organism used is
explanation: Micrococcus luteus is typically used as the test organism for bacitracin microbiological assays.
