explanation: Sulfacetamide (N-sulfanilylacetamide) is synthesized through such routes and is widely used as its sodium salt in ophthalmic anti-infective drops.

question_text: Two of the following compounds give 3 signals in NMR spectroscopy. Choose the correct combination: (P) $CH_3-COOH$, (Q) $CH_3-CH_2-NH_2$, (R) $CH_3-OH$, (S) $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Cl$
explanation: $CH_3-COOH$ and $CH_3-OH$ both give exactly two distinct proton environments (signals) in standard ${}^1\text{H}$ NMR, but wait, let us re-evaluate: $CH_3-COOH$ has 2 signals, $CH_3-OH$ has 2 signals. Let's check $CH_3-CH_2-NH_2$ (3 signals) and $CH_3-CH_2-CH_2Cl$ (3 signals). Therefore, Q and S give 3 signals.

question_text: Conductance cells for conductivity measurements can be made from two of the following metals: (P) Mercury, (Q) Sodium, (R) Platinum, (S) Stainless steel
explanation: Platinum (platinized platinum) and stainless steel are standard inert/stable electrode materials used for conductance cells, whereas sodium and mercury are chemically unsuitable.

question_text: In aldehydes, the $-C=O$ stretch and the $-C-H$ stretch are approximately: (P) $1725\text{ cm}^{-1}$, (Q) $1660\text{ cm}^{-1}$, (R) $2750\text{ cm}^{-1}$, (S) $3300\text{ cm}^{-1}$
explanation: Aliphatic aldehyde carbonyl stretch typically occurs near $1725\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (P) and the characteristic Fermi doublet for the aldehyde C-H stretch appears around $2750\text{ cm}^{-1}$ (R).

question_text: Schedule 'C' and Schedule 'N' as per the Drugs and Cosmetics Act deal with the following: (P) Standards for cosmetics, (Q) Biological and special products, (R) Life period of drugs, (S) List of minimum equipments for the efficient running of a pharmacy
explanation: Schedule C deals with biological and special products (Q), and Schedule N specifies the list of minimum equipment for running a pharmacy (S).

question_text: Abrasive and humectant compounds used in the formulation of toothpaste are: (P) Dicalcium phosphate, (Q) Sodium lauryl sulphate, (R) Sorbitol syrup, (S) Tragacanth
explanation: Dicalcium phosphate functions as an abrasive agent, and sorbitol syrup functions as a humectant in toothpaste formulations.

question_text: Two of the following types of techniques are used for depot formulation: (P) Dissolution controlled, (Q) Encapsulation type, (R) Solubilization, (S) Parenteral suspensions
explanation: Dissolution controlled release systems and parenteral suspensions are common classical techniques used to achieve depot drug delivery.

question_text: GABA, an important transmitter in the brain: (P) Is an inhibitory transmitter, (Q) Is an excitatory transmitter, (R) Increases chloride conductance, (S) Is antagonized by Naloxone
explanation: GABA is the primary inhibitory neurotransmitter in the central nervous system (P) and exerts its action via $GABA_A$ receptors by increasing chloride ion conductance (R).

question_text: Atovaquone when combined with proguanil: (P) Is highly effective and well tolerated, (Q) Is not well tolerated, (R) Antagonism is observed, (S) Resistance is reduced
explanation: The combination of atovaquone and proguanil (Malarone) is highly effective, well tolerated (P), and synergistically reduces the development of parasite resistance (S).

question_text: G-CSF a myeloid growth factor: (P) Exhibits action similar to that of folic acid, (Q) Has a remarkable ability to mobilize hemopoietic stem cells, (R) Is activated by t-PA, (S) Activates a phagocytic activity of mature neutrophils and prolongs their survival of circulation
explanation: Granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) mobilizes hematopoietic stem cells (Q) and activates phagocytic activity while prolonging mature neutrophil survival (S).

question_text: Microscopical characters of cardamom are: (P) Very thin membranous arillus enveloping the seed and composed of several layers of collapsed cells, yellow in colour containing oil, (Q) Presence of anomocytic stomata on the epidermis of pericarp and mesocarp and containing lignifiedreticulate parenchyma, (R) Vittae, the secretory canals contain volatile oil and are brown in colour, (S) Inner epidermis of the pericarp are made up of polygonal tubular cells. Mesocarp includes few Brown to yellow coloured resinous cells
explanation: Cardamom microscopy features a thin membranous arillus (P) and an inner epidermis of the pericarp with polygonal tubular cells along with resinous cells (S).

question_text: Two of the following attributes are characteristic to a natural drug obtained from Syzygium aromaticum: (P) Qadrangular stalked portion- the hypanthium, surmounted by four divergent lobes of sepals which surround a globular head, (Q) Powdered drug shows fragments of hypantium showing the epidermis and the parenchyma containing large oil glands, singly occurring short fibres, cluster crystals of calcium oxalate, (R) Aromatic, pungent, globular berries, remains of stigma at the apex. Kernel white and hollow at the centre, consists of perisperm and endosperm, (S) Tubular epidermal cells, followed by thin walled parenchymatous hypodermis with rectangular stone cells. Pericarp and perisperm containing oil glands, abundant starch grains
explanation: Syzygium aromaticum (clove) flower buds possess a quadrangular stalked hypanthium with four sepals (P) and microscopic features showing hypanthium fragments with large oil glands and calcium oxalate cluster crystals (Q).

question_text: Two metabolites that could transiently accumulate as a result of inhibition of squalene synthase are: (P) Dimethylallyl pyrophosphate, (Q) Cholesterol, (R) Farnesylpyrophosphate, (S) Prednisolone
explanation: Squalene synthase catalyzes the reductive dimerization of two molecules of farnesyl pyrophosphate (R) to form squalene, which is synthesized upstream via intermediates like dimethylallyl pyrophosphate (P).

question_text: Two possible targets against which inhibitors can be designed for use in diabetes treatment are: (P) Carbonic anhydrase, (Q) Insulin, (R) Glycogenphosphorylase, (S) Glucose-6-phosphatase
explanation: Inhibiting glycogen phosphorylase (R) and glucose-6-phosphatase (S) helps reduce hepatic glucose output, making them targets for type 2 diabetes treatment.

question_text: Two important advantages of using micro-organisms for bio-transformations in drug synthesis are: (P) Having been produced from micro-organisms, they are certain to have antibacterial properties, (Q) They are abundant in nature and hence reduce the processing cost significantly, (R) They produce the specific stereoisomer only, (S) They are highly selective and therefore yield products with high purity
explanation: Microbial bio-transformations offer high chemo-, regio-, and stereoselectivity (R, S), ensuring high purity and enantiomeric excess.

question_text: Aminotransferases are directly involved in the biosynthesis of: (P) Aspartate, (Q) Alanine, (R) Oleate, (S) 3-phosphoglycerate
explanation: Aminotransferases catalyze the interconversion of amino acids and alpha-keto acids, directly synthesizing amino acids such as aspartate (from oxaloacetate) and alanine (from pyruvate).

question_text: Match the reactions in GROUP I with their names in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) p-nitrobenzaldehyde and acetone to form 1-(4-nitrophenyl-3-oxo-butene), (Q) Isobutyl benzene is treated with acetyl chloride and anhydrous $AlCl_3$, (R) Pregnelone acetate is saponified and then treated with an aluminium alcoholate to yield progesterone, (S) Benzalacetone and 4-hydroxy coumarin in presence of pyridine. GROUP II: (1) Claisen-Schmidt condensation, (2) Michael condensation, (3) Friedel-Crafts acylation, (4) Oppenauer oxidation
explanation: P corresponds to Claisen-Schmidt condensation (1), Q corresponds to Friedel-Crafts acylation (3), R corresponds to Oppenauer oxidation (4), and S corresponds to Michael addition/condensation (2).

question_text: Match N-substitution of 4-phenylpiperidine-4-ethyl-carboxylate derivatives in GROUP I with analgesics in GROUP II. GROUP I (Substitution at N): (P) $-CH_3$, (Q) $-CH_2-CH_2-(C_6H_4)-NH_2$, (R) $-CH_2-CH_2-C-(C_6H_5)_2-CN$, (S) $-CH_2-CH_2-C_6H_5$. GROUP II (Analgesics): (1) Fentanyl, (2) Diphenoxylate, (3) Pethidine, (4) Anileridine
explanation: P ($CH_3$) gives Pethidine (3); Q gives Anileridines (4); R gives Diphenoxylate (2); S gives Fentanyl derivative/related analog (1).

question_text: Match drugs in GROUP I with nature and function in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Colestipolhydrochloride, (Q) Clebopride, (R) Cilazapril, (S) Mentone. GROUP II: (1) Piradizino-diazepine derivative, angiotensin Converting enzyme inhibitor, (2) Benzylpiperidine derivative, antiemetic, (3) Benzophenone derivative, topical sun screening Substance, (4) Granular copolymer of tetra ethylene and Epichlorohydrin, hypolipidemic
explanation: Colestipol is a hypolipidemic polymer (P-4), Clebopride is an antiemetic benzylpiperidine derivative (Q-2), Cilazapril is an ACE inhibitor (R-1), and Menthone/Benzophenone derivative relates to sun screening/topical use (S-3).

question_text: Match principles involved in GROUP I with instrument used in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Excitation of electrons, (Q) Electron impact bombardment, (R) Molecular vibration, (S) Splitting of electron's magnetic energy. GROUP II: (1) ESR spectrometer, (2) IR spectrometer, (3) Mass spectrometer, (4) UV spectrometer
explanation: Electron excitation corresponds to UV (P-4), electron impact corresponds to Mass spec (Q-3), molecular vibration corresponds to IR (R-2), and electron spin splitting corresponds to ESR (S-1).

question_text: Match drug in GROUP I with reagent for assay in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Albendazole, (Q) Isoniazid, (R) Sulfacetamide sodium, (S) Paracetamol. GROUP II: (1) Cerric ammonium sulphate, (2) Sodium nitrite, (3) Per chloric acid, (4) Potassium bromate
explanation: Albendazole is assayed with perchloric acid (P-3), Isoniazid with potassium bromate (Q-4), Sulfacetamide with sodium nitrite diazotization (R-2), and Paracetamol with ceric ammonium sulphate (S-1).

question_text: Match method adopted in GROUP I with physical state of sample used in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Gas chromatography, (Q) Infra-red, (R) HPLC, (S) X-Ray diffraction. GROUP II: (1) Solution, (2) Crystal, (3) Solid, liquid or gas, (4) Liquid or gas
explanation: Gas chromatography uses liquid or gas samples (P-4), IR can use solid, liquid, or gas (Q-3), HPLC uses solution samples (R-1), and X-Ray diffraction uses crystals (S-2).

question_text: Match film defects in GROUP I with explanation in GROUP II. GROUP I: (P) Orange peel effect, (Q) Blistering, (R) Cracking, (S) Bloom. GROUP II: (1) Inadequate spreading of the coating solution before Drying causes a bumping effect on the coating, (2) It is the result of drying coated tablets in ovens, due to too Rapid evaporation of the solvent from the core and the Effect of high temperature on the film, (3) Occurs due to processing temperature used is too high for a particular formulation, (4) Occurs if internal stress in the film exceed the tensile Strength of the film
explanation: Orange peel relates to inadequate spreading/bumping (P-1), blistering relates to rapid solvent evaporation in ovens (Q-2), cracking occurs when internal stress exceeds tensile strength (R-4), and bloom relates to high temperature effects/migration (S-3).

question_text: Match Group-I (term) with Group-II (example). GROUP I: (P) Hydrophilic suppository Base, (Q) Polymorphism, (R) Film former used in the Formation of nail lacquer, (S) Opaquant extender. GROUP II: (1) Nitrocellulose, (2) Titanium dioxide, (3) Cocoa butter, (4) Polyethylene glycol
explanation: Hydrophilic suppository base is polyethylene glycol (P-4), polymorphism is exhibited by cocoa butter (Q-3), nail lacquer film former is nitrocellulose (R-1), and opaquant extender is titanium dioxide (S-2).

question_text: Match Group-I (Drug) with Group-II (Type of action). GROUP I: (P) Toremlifene, (Q) Flutamide, (R) Ketaconazole, (S) Miglitol. GROUP II: (1) Inhibitor of adrenal and gonadal steroidogenesis, (2) \alpha-glucosidase inhibitor, (3) Androgen receptor antagonist, (4) Selective estrogen receptor modulator
explanation: Toremifene is a SERM (P-4), flutamide is an androgen receptor antagonist (Q-3), ketoconazole inhibits steroidogenesis (R-1/2 contextually mapped to 2/1, let's check: Miglitol is alpha-glucosidase inhibitor S-2, Ketoconazole is 1). Thus P-4, Q-3, R-1, S-2.

question_text: The activities of certain object drugs are increased by certain precipitant drug choose the correct combination. GROUP I (Object drug): (P) Amines in foods, (Q) Alcohol, (R) Cefoxitin, (S) Azathioprine. GROUP II (Precipitant Drugs): (1) Allopurinol, (2) MAO inhibitor, (3) Disulfiram, (4) Probenecid
explanation: MAO inhibitors increase pressor amines in foods (P-2), Disulfiram increases alcohol toxicity (Q-3), Probenecid increases antibiotic levels like cefoxitin/penicillins (R-4), Allopurinol increases azathioprine toxicity (S-1). Wait, let's match option D or corresponding pairs properly.

question_text: Match GROUP I (Drug) with GROUP II (Mechanism). GROUP I: (P) Amines in foods, (Q) Alcohol, (R) Cefoxitin, (S) Azathioprine. GROUP II (Mechanism): (1) Allopurinol, (2) MAO inhibitor, (3) Disulfiram, (4) Probenecid
explanation: P matches MAO inhibitor (2), Q matches Disulfiram (3), R matches Probenecid (4), and S matches Allopurinol (1).

question_text: Match GROUP I (Plant Hormone Type) with GROUP II (Chemical Substance). GROUP I: (P) Auxin, (Q) Gibberellin, (R) Cytokinin, (S) Growth inhibitor. GROUP II: (1) Absicic acid, (2) NAA, (3) GA3, (4) 6-furfuryl amine
explanation: Auxin corresponds to NAA (P-2), Gibberellin corresponds to GA3 (Q-3), Cytokinin corresponds to 6-furfuryl amine/kinetin (R-4), and Growth inhibitor corresponds to Abscisic acid (S-1).

question_text: Match GROUP I (Crude Drugs) with GROUP II (Chemical Test). GROUP I: (P) Etoposide, (Q) Sumatra benzoin, (R) Ergot Powar, (S) Papaverine. GROUP II (Chemical Test): (1) Add a solution of potassium permanganate and warm; yield an odour of benzaldehyde, (2) To an alcoholic solution, add a solution of p-dimethylamino Benzaldehyde, (3) A solution in HCl acid when treated with k- ferriccyanide; Yield and yellow color, (4) Alcoholic solution of the drug is treated with strong copper Solution; gives a brown precipitate
explanation: Benzoin gives benzaldehyde odor with KMnO4 (Q-1), Ergot alkaloids react with p-dimethylaminobenzaldehyde (Van Urk's test) (R-2), Papaverine gives yellow color with ferricyanide (S-3).

question_text: The chief constituent of the seeds Strophanthus gratus or woods of Acokantheraschimiperi belonging to the family Apocynaceae is G-strophanthin. On hydrolysis, it gives
explanation: G-strophanthin is also known as ouabain, which upon hydrolysis yields ouabagenin and rhamnose.

question_text: The duration of action of sublingual nitroglycerin tablet is
explanation: Sublingual nitroglycerin has a rapid onset and a short duration of action, typically lasting about 10 to 30 minutes.

question_text: Identify the adrenergic receptor, whose agonists can be missed used by sportsmen for anabolic effects.
explanation: Beta-2 ($\beta_2$) agonists like clenbuterol are sometimes misused by athletes for their anabolic and fat-reducing properties.

question_text: When the urinary pH becomes 8.0, significant increase in the excretion of the drugs takes place
explanation: Aspirin is a weak acid; in an alkaline urine (pH 8.0), it becomes ionized and its renal excretion is significantly increased due to ion trapping.

question_text: Condensation of 6-hydroxy-2,4,5-triaminopyridine with 1,1,3-trichloro acetone and N-(4-aminobenzoyl) glutamic acid at pH 4 to 5, in the presence of sodium bisulphate gives
explanation: Pteroyl glutamic acid (Folic acid) can be synthesized by the condensation of these specified precursors.

question_text: The common structural feature of iodoxamic acid, iotalamic acid, diatrizoic acid and iocarmic acid is
explanation: These agents are radiocontrast media that share a 2,4,6-triiodobenzoic acid core structure.

question_text: Tranykypromine, a psychonanaleptic and antidepressant drug is synthesized from
explanation: Tranylcypromine synthesis typically involves cyclization starting from precursors like ethyl phenylcyclopropanecarboxylate.

question_text: List of diseases and ailments which a drug may not purport to prevent or cure or make claims to prevent or cure under the Drugs and Cosmetics Rule 1945 is given under
explanation: Schedule J of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules lists diseases and ailments that cannot be prevented or cured by drugs.

question_text: Annatto consists of the dried seeds of Bixa orellana L. Family Bixaceae. The chief constituent is
explanation: Annatto contains carotenoid pigments, specifically bixin and norbixin, located in the resinous aril.

question_text: 'Cresol with soap solution' is a preparation, in which soap is incorporated to

options.B: Improve mutual miscibility of cresol and water by reducing critical solution temperature of Cresol water system
options.C: Sustain the germicidal action of cresol

explanation: Soap acts as an emulsifying agent that lowers the critical solution temperature, making cresol completely miscible with water in all proportions (Lysol).

question_text: When stoichiometric amount of $CaCl_2$ is added to an emulsion stabilized with sodium alginate, it will

options.B: Change the nature from w/o to o/w
options.C: Change the nature from o/w to w/o
options.D: Accelerate the phenomenon of Ostwald ripening

explanation: Calcium ions cross-link sodium alginate to form insoluble calcium alginate, destroying the stabilizing film and causing the emulsion to crack.

question_text: Chlorine and bromine substitution in aromatic compounds
explanation: Heavy atoms like chlorine and bromine promote intersystem crossing due to the heavy atom effect, which quenches fluorescence.

question_text: Solvent programming, also called gradient elution, involves

options.C: Using the mobile phase is unchanged

explanation: Gradient elution or solvent programming refers to continuously changing the mobile phase composition during chromatographic separation.

question_text: Calibration of the cell constant of conductance cell is carried out by using a solution
explanation: Potassium chloride ($KCl$) solutions of known concentration (typically $0.1\text{ M}$ or $1\text{ M}$) are standard reference solutions used to determine the cell constant of a conductivity cell.

question_text: Hybridoma technology is widely used for producing
explanation: Hybridoma technology fuses antibody-producing B cells with myeloma cells to produce large quantities of monoclonal antibodies.

question_text: 'Gene therapy' refers to the process of

options.A: Identifying disease causing genes and activating them for therapeutic benefits
options.B: Increasing the expression levels of the set of genes involved in a given disease in affected cells through selective modulating agents
options.C: Transfer of new genetic material to the cells of an individual for therapeutic benefit
options.D: Removal of the protein corresponding to the disease causing genes from the cells of the affected individual

explanation: Gene therapy involves introducing genetic material into a patient's cells to treat or prevent disease.

question_text: A technician is attempting to sterilize a plug of cotton in hermetically sealed condition in a glass bottle by autoclaving. Which of the following statement is correct

options.A: It should be sterilized at 115-118° C for 30 minutes
options.B: It should be sterilized at 121 to 124° C for 15 minutes at 15 lbs/sq. inch pressure
options.D: It should be autoclaved at 126-129° C with saturated steam for 10 minutes

explanation: Steam cannot penetrate a hermetically sealed glass bottle containing a cotton plug, rendering autoclave sterilization ineffective in this condition.

question_text: Hyperuricaemia is associated with the abnormal metabolism of
explanation: Hyperuricemia (elevated uric acid) results from abnormal purine metabolism, leading to conditions like gout.

question_text: What is the concentration of NaCl required making 1% solution of cocaine HCl Isotonic with blood plasma? Freezing point of 1% w/v solution of NaCl is -0.576°C and freezing point of 1% w/v cocaine HCl is -0.09°C
explanation: Using sodium chloride equivalent formula: $W = (0.52 - a) / b$, yielding approximately $0.746 \% \text{ w/v}$.

question_text: Arillode is

options.A: Warty out-growth from microphyl, eg., castor
options.B: Succulent growth from hilum covering the entire seed, eg., nutmeg
options.C: Outgrowth originating from micropyle and covering the seeds, eg., cardamom

explanation: An arillode (aril) in cardamom is a fleshy outgrowth originating from the region of the micropyle covering the seed.

question_text: Cinnamon consists of the dried inner bark of the shoots of coppiced tree of Cinnamomum zeylanicum Nees. The typical microscopic charaters of the bark are

options.A: Biseriate medullary rays, secretory cavities containing volatile oil and mucilage and few starch grains in cortical parenchyma and calcium oxalate in parenchymatous cells.
options.B: 2-5 layers of cork cells containing oil globules. Presence of schizogenous canal
options.C: Medullary rays multiseriate, the periderm portion cork has both tangentially and radially elongated cells, stone cells present and no phloem fibers
options.D: Exo-foliated cork, non-lignified with 2-4 layers of phellogens. 15-20 rows of phelloderm. Prominent vascular tissue.

explanation: Cinnamon bark microscopy is characterized by biseriate medullary rays, oil/mucilage cavities, starch, and calcium oxalate needles.

question_text: An essential ingredient in the general preparation of plant tissue culture media is
explanation: Carbon source such as sucrose or glucose is an essential ingredient in all plant tissue culture media to provide energy.

question_text: The mefloquine, proguanil and primaquine can be effectively used in diseases produced by
explanation: Mefloquine, proguanil, and primaquine are antimalarial drugs, which are protozoan parasites.

question_text: Identify the receptor which demonstrates the fastest onset of response, when stimulated
explanation: Ionotropic receptors (ligand-gated ion channels) mediate rapid responses within milliseconds.

question_text: One of the following drugs is converted to the corresponding deoxy nucleotide, which shows cytotoxicity
explanation: 5-Fluorouracil is converted intracellularly to active deoxynucleotide metabolites (like FdUMP) that inhibit thymidylate synthase.

question_text: The compounds 2-Methyl-3-phytyl-1, 4-naphthoquinone and 2-methyl1-3-all-trans faenesylgeranylgeranyl-1, 4-napthoquinone are commonly known as:
explanation: These chemical structures correspond to phylloquinone (Vitamin $K_1$) and menaquinone (Vitamin $K_2$).

question_text: (Z)-5-Fluoro-2-methyl-1-{[p-(methyl-sulpinyl)phenyl]methylene}-1H indene-3-acetic acid, reaches peak blood levels within 2-4 hours and undergoes a complication reversible metabolism to become active. Active metabolite has the group.
explanation: Sulindac undergoes reversible reduction to its active sulfide metabolite.

question_text: An intermediate for the synthesis of benzodiazepine derivatives can be prepared by treating 4-chloroaniline with benzoyl chloride in the presence of zinc chloride as a catalyst. Identify the intermediate.
explanation: Friedel-Crafts acylation of 4-chloroaniline with benzoyl chloride yields the corresponding benzophenone derivative.

question_text: Find the product X in the reaction involving a substituted benzophenone and methyl N-cyano-N'-[2-(methylthio)ethyl]carbamimidothioate or similar reagent.
explanation: This reaction sequence is part of the synthesis of specific fused heterocyclic systems like quinazoline or benzodiazepine analogs.

question_text: In the preparation of ointments, macrogels are used as used as
explanation: Macrogols (polyethylene glycols) form water-soluble ointment bases.

question_text: An antioxidant commonly used in the formulation of a non-aqueous parenteral preparation is
explanation: Butylated hydroxytoluene (BHT) is lipophilic and suitable as an antioxidant for non-aqueous (oily) parenteral preparations.

question_text: Phosphatidic acid and its derivatives from liposomes because

options.A: In a fully hydrated condition, they are conical in shape
options.B: In a fully hydrated condition, they are cylindrical in shape
options.C: They contain only non-polar moieties in their structures
options.D: Their saponification values are unusually low.

explanation: Molecules with inverted cone shapes or specific packing parameters tend to form non-lamellar structures, whereas cylinder shapes form bilayers.

question_text: With regard to the standards for sterile water for injection, IP, the 'residue on evaporation' limit is

options.A: Higher than water for injection, IP
options.B: Lower than water for injection, IP
options.C: Same as that of the water for injection, IP
options.D: No such standard is prescribed in the monograph

question_text: The number of peaks given by the $^{1}\text{H NMR}$ spectrum of 2-methyl-1-pentene is
explanation: 2-Methyl-1-pentene ($CH_2=C(CH_3)CH_2CH_2CH_3$) has 4 chemically non-equivalent sets of protons.

question_text: In HPLC, the analytical performance improves when

options.C: Coarser particles are paired with shorter columns

explanation: Reducing particle diameter in HPLC decreases plate height (improves column efficiency and resolution according to the Van Deemter equation).

question_text: Increase in the extent of conjugation of a double bonded system results in
explanation: Increasing conjugation decreases the HOMO-LUMO gap, shifting absorption to longer wavelengths (bathochromic or red shift).

question_text: Alkaloids derived from ornithine are (P) Cocaine (Q) Colchicine (R) Hyoscyamine (S) Emetine
explanation: Cocaine and hyoscyamine (tropane alkaloids) are derived from ornithine/proline.

question_text: Aloe barbadensis has two of following characters: (P) The drug obtained is white in color and has a bitter taste (Q) The drugs is opaque, yellowish brown to chocolate brown and breaks with a waxy fracture (R) The drug has a pungent odour and is amorphous under the microscope (S) Under in the microscope, acicular crystals are visible.
explanation: Aloe has a characteristic waxy fracture and shows numerous acicular crystals of aloin under the microscope.

question_text: Tacrolimus is a macrolide antibiotic, which bears the following attributes: (P) Produced from Streptomyces hygroscopicus and is chemically related to cyclosporine (Q) Binds with cytoplasmic peptidyl-propyl-isomerase and can be useful in liver and kidney transplant (R) Produced from Streptomyces tsukubaensis and is chemically, unrelated to cyclosporine (S) An inhibitor of pyrimidine synthesis, used in rheumatoid arthritis
explanation: Tacrolimus is produced by Streptomyces tsukubaensis, is chemically unrelated to cyclosporine, binds FKBP (immunophilin), and is used in transplants.

question_text: Metformin acts by two mechanisms: (P) Increasing insulin secretion (Q) Inhibiting a-glucosidase (R) Decreasing hepatic glucose production (S) Increasing insulin action in muscle and fat
explanation: Metformin reduces hepatic glucose production and increases peripheral insulin sensitivity.

question_text: Metabolic oxidation of carbon -nitrogen, carbon oxygen and carbon - sulphur systems principally involves two basic types of bio-transformation processes: (P) Hydroxylation of the a-carbon atom attached directly to the heteroatom (Q) Mixed function oxidase system also oxidizes carbon atom adjacent to carbonyl and imino functions (R) Hydroxylation of the hetero-atom only (S) Microsomal hydroxylation at allylic carbonatom
explanation: Oxidation of C-N, C-O, and C-S systems typically proceeds via alpha-carbon hydroxylation and heteroatom oxidation.

question_text: The silver salt sulphadiaziane, SILVADENE, is an effective topical antimicrobial agent in burns because of its two important attributes: (P) Board spectrum of activity (Q) Active against pseudomonas spp. (R) The salt is only very slightly soluble and its does not penetrate the wall, instead it acts on the structure (S) The salt is highly soluble and hence it is rapidly absorbed
explanation: Silver sulfadiazine is active against Pseudomonas spp. and has low solubility, releasing silver ions slowly at the burn site.

question_text: In the synthesis of chlorpheniramine, two important ingredients required are: (P) 4-chloro benzyl cyanide (Q) 4-chloro pyridine (R) 2-chloro benzyl cyanide (S) 2-chloro pyridine
explanation: Chlorpheniramine synthesis involves 4-chlorophenylacetonitrile and 2-halopyridine derivatives.

question_text: Zeta potential: (P) Is the difference in potential between the surface of the tightly bound layer and the electroneutral region (Q) Is the potential at the solid surface of the suspended particle (R) Can be positive, zero negative (S) Is the electronanotherodynamic potential
explanation: Zeta potential is the electrokinetic potential at the shear plane and can be positive, zero, or negative.

question_text: Two of official standards for uncoated tablets as per IP are: (P) Shape (Q) Friability (R) Disintegration time (S) Uniformity of weight
explanation: Disintegration time and weight uniformity are mandatory official IP quality control standards for uncoated tablets.

question_text: As per schedule 'O' of the Drugs and Cosmetics Rules 1945, the minimum Rider walker coefficients for Grade 1 and 3 Black disinfectant fluids are: (P) 18 (Q) 10 (R) 5 (S) 14
explanation: Grade 1 black disinfectant fluids have a minimum Rideal-Walker coefficient of 18, and Grade 3 has a coefficient of 5.

question_text: The IR spectrum of an organic liquid can be taken by placing it between a pair of polished plates made of
explanation: Sodium chloride (NaCl) and Potassium bromide (KBr) plates are transparent to infrared radiation, making them standard materials for IR liquid films.

question_text: In gas choromatography, derivatisation is desirable to
explanation: Derivatization in GC is used to improve thermal stability of polar compounds and enable suitable interaction with the carrier gas or column.

question_text: Neutral thioaliphatic amino acid found in proteins are
explanation: Methionine contains a thioether group and Cysteine contains a thiol group, both being sulfur-containing (thioaliphatic) amino acids.

question_text: Diazoxide, a benzothiazide derivative produces
explanation: Diazoxide acts as a K+ channel opener, causing vasodilation, and inhibits insulin secretion by hyperpolarizing pancreatic beta cells.

question_text: The principle of ELISA is based on these two observations
explanation: ELISA relies on antibodies and antigens attaching to solid supports while retaining immunological activity, and being coupled to enzymes without losing function.

question_text: Which of the following are likely to be good targets for designing antihypertensive drugs?
explanation: H2 histamine receptors are not typical antihypertensive targets, whereas H2 blockers lower acid, but Calcium channel proteins and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors are classic targets for treating high blood pressure.

question_text: The characteristic of the sabin vaccine administered orally for prevention of polio
explanation: The Sabin vaccine (OPV) consists of live attenuated strains and carries a rare risk of reverting to neurovirulence, causing vaccine-associated paralytic poliomyelitis.

explanation: Matching the anatomical origin of mucilages yields cell wall of seed epidermis in linseed (P-4), endodermis in fenugreek (Q-1), etc.

explanation: Jaborandi contains pilocarpine (imidazole), Ergot contains ergot alkaloids (indole), Kurchi contains steroidal alkaloids, and Pterocarpus contains tannins.

question_text: Match Common reagents used in pharmacognosy (Group I) with Uses (Group II)

question_text: Match Name of enzyme (Group I) with Description (Group II)
explanation: Sutilains are proteolytic enzymes from Bacillus subtilis (P-4), Urokinase from human kidneys (Q-3), Alteplase is rt-PA (R-2), and Bromelains from pineapples (S-1).

question_text: Match Physical form of substances (Group I) with Rheological properties (Group II)
explanation: Castor oil shows Newtonian flow (P-4), concentrated flocculated suspensions show pseudoplastic flow (Q-2), methylcellulose dispersion shows plastic/pseudoplastic, pastes show plastic flow.

question_text: Match concepts/scales (Group I) with their corresponding theoretical frameworks (Group II)
explanation: Crystal growth relates to Ostwald ripening (P-4), pH scale to Sorensen (Q-2), HLB scale to Griffin (R-1), and interparticular forces to DLVO theory (S-3).

question_text: Match Method of purification (Group I) with Effect on water quality (Group II)

question_text: Match Drugs (Group I) with Mechanism (Group II)
explanation: Rifabutin inhibits mycobacterial RNA polymerase (P-2), Penciclovir inhibits viral DNA synthesis (Q-1), Imiquimod is an immunomodulator (R-4), and Amprenavir is a protease inhibitor (S-3).

question_text: Match Reponses/Incidents (Group I) with Bioactive substances (Group II)
explanation: False transmitter involves methyldopa (P-2), St. Anthony's fire involves ergot alkaloids (Q-4), triple response involves histamine (R-1), and Straub phenomenon involves morphine (S-3).

question_text: Match Adverse effects (Group I) with Drugs (Group II)
explanation: Reye's syndrome is associated with aspirin (P-3), hypertrichosis with minoxidil (Q-4), grey baby syndrome with chloramphenicol (R-1), and pinpoint pupil with morphine (S-2).

question_text: Match Technique used (Group I) with Analytical method of evaluation (Group II)
explanation: Polarography involves current-potential measurements, Potentiometry involves potential-volume, Conductometry involves conductance-volume, and Amperometry involves current-volume curves.

question_text: Match Type of Radiation (Group I) with Wave length (Group II)
explanation: Radio frequency has wavelengths > 100 mm (P-1), UV is 200-380 nm (Q-4), X-ray is 10 pm-10 nm (R-3), and Mid-IR is 2.5-50 um (S-2).

question_text: Match Spraying reagents used in Chromatographic methods (Group I) with Type of substance (Group II)
explanation: SbCl3 in CHCl3 detects steroids (P-3), bromocresol green detects carboxylic acids (Q-1), aniline phthalate detects sugars (R-4), and 2,4-DNP detects aldehydes/ketones (S-2).

question_text: Match Antibiotics (Group I) with Test organism for microbiological assay IP (Group II)
explanation: Erythromycin uses Micrococcus luteus (P-4), Doxycycline uses Staphylococcus aureus (Q-1), Carbenicillin uses Pseudomonas aeruginosa (R-2), and Amphotericin B uses Saccharomyces cerevisiae (S-3).

question_text: Match Hormone (Group I) with Action (Group II)
explanation: Vasopressin modulates extensive vasodilation/water balance (P-1), Oxytocin responds to suckling reflex (Q-3), etc.

question_text: The alkaloid concentration in coca leaves vary from
explanation: Dried coca leaves typically contain around 0.7% to 1.5% total alkaloids, predominantly cocaine.

question_text: Cocaine, the alkaloid derived from coca leaves acts by
explanation: Cocaine blocks the reuptake of monoamine neurotransmitters like noradrenaline, dopamine, and serotonin.

question_text: Chlorambucil is derivative of
explanation: Chlorambucil is an aromatic nitrogen mustard derived from phenylbutyric acid.

explanation: Chlorambucil contains a carboxylic acid group and is assayed by direct alkalimetry using standard sodium hydroxide solution.

explanation: Picrocrocin is the bitter glycoside responsible for the taste of saffron (Crocus sativus).

explanation: Hydrolysis of picrocrocin yields safranal, which is the main volatile compound responsible for saffron's characteristic aroma.

options.A: Lowering the affinity for free plasminogen
options.D: Antagonizing co-factor function of vitamin K

explanation: Heparin binds to antithrombin III, greatly accelerating its inhibition of thrombin and factor Xa.

explanation: Chlorination of 2,4-dihydroxy compound followed by substitution gives 2-amino-4-chloro-6,7-dimethoxyquinazoline as intermediate X.

options.A: Decrease of glucose uptake in muscles

explanation: Pioglitazone is a thiazolidinedione that acts as an agonist at PPAR-gamma receptors, thereby increasing insulin sensitivity in peripheral tissues.

question_text: An angiotensin-II receptor blocker useful in treating hypertension is

options.B: Interaction due to change in drug transport
options.C: Interaction due to disturbances in electrolyte balance

explanation: NSAIDs displace warfarin from plasma protein binding sites or inhibit platelet aggregation, leading to additive or synergistic bleeding risks.

explanation: Alginic acid and its salts (alginates) are commercially extracted from brown seaweeds such as Laminaria and Kelp.

explanation: Urginea indica (Indian squill) microscopy typically reveals raphides of calcium oxalate.

question_text: Streptomycin is a

options.A: Di-acidic base possessing an aldehydic carbonyl group
options.B: Tri-acidic base possessing an aldehydic carbonyl group
options.C: Neutral compound possessing a ketonic group
options.D: Acid compound possessing a carboxyl group

explanation: Streptomycin is an aminoglycoside antibiotic containing two strongly basic guanidino groups and one N-methyl-L-glucosamine amino group making it a tri-acidic base, along with a formyl (aldehydic) group.

question_text: The antihistaminic with diphenyl methyl group is

explanation: Pilocarpine contains an imidazole ring and a dihydrofuran-2-one (lactone) ring.

question_text: The most important microbial virulence factor in etiology of meningitis is
explanation: Encapsulated pathogens like Neisseria meningitidis and Streptococcus pneumoniae rely heavily on their polysaccharide capsule to resist phagocytosis and cause meningitis.

question_text: Commonly used tetanus vaccine is produced by

options.A: Treatment of the causative organism with heat or UV light and finally obtaining the toxoid
options.C: Artificially generating antibodies to viral glycoproteins
options.D: Isolating the antigenicity genes from the causative organism

explanation: Tetanus vaccine is a toxoid prepared by detoxifying the toxin produced by Clostridium tetani, typically using formaldehyde.

question_text: Which of the following equations is valid for standard B-DNA

question_text: Clinical jaundice, typified by yellowing of the tissues is associated with elevated levels of
explanation: Jaundice is clinically defined by hyperbilirubinemia, leading to the yellow coloration of skin and sclera.

question_text: In NMR spectrometry, the chemical shift (\delta) is expressed in
explanation: Chemical shift in NMR spectroscopy is dimensionless and typically expressed in parts per million (ppm).

question_text: In chromatographic separation, the different species in the sample, undergo the process of
explanation: Chromatographic separation relies on the differential partitioning of sample components between stationary and mobile phases.

question_text: A target material used in the production of X-rays is
explanation: Copper and tungsten are standard high-melting-point materials used as targets/anodes in X-ray tubes.

question_text: The requirement and guidelines for clinical trials, import and manufacture of new drugs as per the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules is given under Schedule
explanation: Schedule Y of the Drugs & Cosmetics Rules outlines the requirements and guidelines for clinical trials and new drug approval in India.

question_text: The growth of large particles at the expense of smaller ones, as a result of a difference in the solubility of the particles of varying sizes, is termed as
explanation: Ostwald ripening describes the dissolution of small particles and redeposition onto larger particles driven by differences in solubility.

question_text: Cyclic oligomers of glucose that form water soluble inclusion complexes, which are biocompatible and improve the bioavailability of drugs
explanation: Cyclodextrins are cyclic oligosaccharides capable of forming inclusion complexes with hydrophobic drugs to enhance solubility and bioavailability.

question_text: 'Draves test' is associated with measuring the efficiency of
explanation: The Draves test is a standard method used to evaluate the efficiency of wetting agents.

question_text: Effect of fibrates on blood lipids are mediated by

options.A: Inhibiting both synthesis and esterification of fatty acids
options.B: Their interaction with peroxime proliferator-activated receptors (PPARs)
options.C: Reducing the conversion of HMG-CoA to mevalonate

explanation: Fibrates lower triglycerides and increase HDL by acting as agonists for peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor alpha (PPAR-alpha).

question_text: A cardioselective beta blocker with vasodilating properties is
explanation: Nebivolol is a beta-1 selective blocker that also induces vasodilation via L-arginine/nitric oxide pathway.

question_text: Choose the correct option: C1=CC=CC=C1CH=CH-COOH is the precursor for the biosynthesis of
explanation: Cinnamic acid (shown as C1=CC=CC=C1CH=CH-COOH) serves as the primary precursor for the biosynthesis of coumarins (benz-alpha-pyrone structures).

question_text: (-)-Hyscyamine is

options.A: 15-20 times more active as a mydriatic than (+)-hyoscyamine
options.C: 3-5 times less active as a mydriatic than (+)-hyoscyamine
options.D: 100 times more active as a mydriatic than (+)-hyoscyamine

explanation: The naturally occurring (-)-isomer of hyoscyamine is significantly more potent pharmacologically than the (+)-isomer.

question_text: The reaction shown in the diagram involving the tricyclic compound and Grignard-like reagent is known as
explanation: The reaction involves an organomagnesium halide (Grignard reagent) adding to a carbonyl group, which is a classic Grignard reaction.

question_text: In thiazole diuretics, the position 7 is very important and is occupied by a
explanation: In thiazide diuretics, an unsubstituted/free sulfamoyl group at position 7 is essential for diuretic activity.

explanation: The condensation of 4-hydroxycoumarin with benzalacetone yields Warfarin.

question_text: A mass spectrum is obtained by plotting

options.C: Concentration versus degree of deflection of ions
options.D: Abundance of ions versus their m/e ratio

explanation: Mass spectrometry plots relative abundance (ion intensity) against the mass-to-charge ratio (m/z or m/e).

question_text: Aldehydes can be distinguished from other C=O containing compounds by IR, due to

options.A: The low frequency of absorption of aldehydes
options.B: The alkyl or group is attached to >C=O
options.D: The doublet at the C-H-stretching region

explanation: Aldehydes exhibit characteristic Fermi resonance resulting in a distinct doublet in the C-H stretching region around 2830 and 2720 cm^-1.

question_text: A super disintegrant in tablet formulation is
explanation: Sodium starch glycolate is widely used as a superdisintegrant in tablet manufacturing.

question_text: A drug was administered to 30 subjects as a tablet (30 mg), an oral aqueous solution (30 mg) and as an intravenous (0.3 mg). Mean AUC's (ng.hr/mL), dose normalized to 1 mg, for tablet, oral solution and IV were 0.91, 0.87 and 103.0 respectively. Calculate the relative bioavailability of the drug in table compared to the solution.
explanation: Relative bioavailability = (AUC_tablet / AUC_solution) * 100 = (0.91 / 0.87) * 100 = 104.6%.

question_text: When ammonium chloride is gradually and slowly incorporates in to an emulsion stabilized with ammonium oleate,

options.B: It will invert from o/w to w/o type
options.C: It will invert from w/o to o/w type
options.D: There will be no impact on its physical stability

explanation: Adding an electrolyte like ammonium chloride changes the surfactant property, leading to phase inversion of the o/w emulsion stabilized by soap.

question_text: A prescription requires 4 mEq/liter of hydrogen phosphate ion $HPO_4^{-2}$. How many milligrams of dibasic potassium phosphate, $K_2HPO_4$ (molecular weight 174) will be required?
explanation: Equivalent weight = MW / valence = 174 / 2 = 87 g/Eq. For 4 mEq, mass = 4 * 10^-3 Eq * 87 g/Eq = 0.348 g = 348 mg.

question_text: Gram positive bacterial typically contain

options.B: Repeating units arabinogalactan and mycolates in their cellwalls
options.C: Peptidoglycan muramic acid and D-amino acids in their cell walls
options.D: Cell walls containing predominantly polysaccharides and glycoproteins

explanation: Gram-positive bacterial cell walls are characterized by a thick peptidoglycan layer containing muramic acid and unique D-amino acids.

question_text: Quartenary structure of a protein molecule refers to

options.A: Specific association to two or more copies of a polypeptide chain to result in a biologically active molecule
options.B: Regular seen local structure within a polypeptide chain
options.C: The portion of the polypeptide chain that comes into contact with another protein molecule
options.D: The portion of the structure that gets stabilized upon binding to nucleic acid

explanation: Quaternary protein structure describes the assembly and spatial arrangement of multiple folded polypeptide subunits into a multi-subunit complex.

question_text: A blood sample is treated with alkaline phosphotungstic acid to from tungsten blue, which is estimated colorimetrically to give a positive reaction. The sample contains
explanation: Uric acid reduces phosphotungstic acid in an alkaline medium to form tungsten blue.

question_text: Two important steps for plant regeneration by organogenesis are: (P) Establishment of callus cultures, (Q) Initiation of somatic embryogenesis, (R) Germination of seeds, (S) Initiation of cell suspensions
explanation: Plant organogenesis and micropropagation typically start with establishment of callus cultures (P) and initiation of cell suspensions (S) or similar tissue culture steps.

question_text: Two tests for ephedrine are: (P) A solution in dilute HCl, treated with copper sulphate and sodium hydroxide gives a violet colour, (Q) An alcoholic solution gives a red colour with FeCl3, (R) On shaking with solvent ether, the organic layer shows purple while the aqueous layer becomes blue, (S) A solution of vanillin gives a violet-red colour
explanation: Ephedrine responds positively to the copper-reduction test (Biuret-like copper complex giving a violet color) and the vanillin test.

question_text: Dried fruits of sweet fennel has two the following properties: (P) $80\%$ of E-anethole, $10\%$ of methyl chavicol and $5\%$ (+)-fenchone as constituents, (Q) 65-75 % (+) Linalool as a constituent, (R) The fruit is a diankene, almost cylinder and surrounded bylarge stylopod, (S) The fruit is elongated and surrounded by cayculus
explanation: Fennel fruits contain anethole and fenchone as major components and have typical schizocarpic cremocarp morphology with distinct stylopods.

question_text: Dihydroxy acetone phosphate is involved in the biosyntheses of two of the following: (P) Serotonin, (Q) Triacylglycerol, (R) Pyruvate, (S) Methionine
explanation: Dihydroxyacetone phosphate (DHAP) is a glycolysis intermediate that gives rise to glycerol-3-phosphate for triacylglycerols and converts towards pyruvate via glycolysis.

question_text: The virus responsible for SARS can be described by two of the following features: (P) It contains double-standards DNA and requires two complementary strands to be synthesized to serve as mRNA, (Q) It has distinctive club shaped particles projecting from the surface, appearing like a crown, (R) It contains plus-strand RNA that can serve directly as mRNA, (S) It is a retrovirus and requires extracellular DNA for replication
explanation: SARS-CoV is a coronavirus characterized by club-like spike projections resembling a crown (corona) and a positive-sense single-stranded RNA genome acting directly as mRNA.

question_text: Two of the following facts are associated with Ethylene oxide gas: (P) It is non toxic and non inflammable and used for sterilization, (Q) It is a colourless inflammable gas. Toxic in nature and used for sterilization, (R) It is diluted with CO2, (S) It cannot penetrated plastic and paper packaging
explanation: Ethylene oxide is a colorless, highly flammable, and toxic gas used for gaseous sterilization, typically blended with carbon dioxide to reduce flammability hazards.

question_text: Examine the chemical structure of Mestranol or ethinylestradiol derivative and identify its properties from the list: (P) Is active parenterally, (Q) Shows greater activity orally than parenterally, (R) Is orally inactive, (S) Has no parenteral activity
explanation: Ethinylated steroids like ethinylestradiol and mestranol have high oral bioavailability and show greater activity orally due to protection from first-pass metabolism by the 17-alpha ethynyl group.

question_text: Tranexamic acid is: (P) Trans-4-amino methyl cyclohexane carbolic acid, (Q) A polypeptide, (R) An inhibitor of proteolytic enzymes including plasmin, (S) Used for the prophylaxis of hemorrhage associated with excessive fibrinolysis
explanation: Tranexamic acid is an antifibrinolytic agent that inhibits plasminogen activation, useful in preventing hemorrhage due to hyperfibrinolysis.

question_text: Prostaglandins are derivatives of: (P) C25 acid, (Q) 7-(2 cyclohexyl) pentenoic acid, (R) C20 prostanoic acid, (S) 7-(2 octyl cyclopentyl) heptanoic acid
explanation: Prostaglandins are C20 fatty acid derivatives based structurally on prostanoic acid.

question_text: Two ex-officio members of the Drugs Technical Advisory Board under Drugs and Cosmetic Act are (P) The Drugs Controller General of India (Q) The President, Medical Council of India (R) The Secretary, Pharmacy Council of India (S) The Director, National Institute of Pharmaceutical Education and Research, India
explanation: The Drugs Controller General of India and the Secretary of the Pharmacy Council of India are official ex-officio members of the DTAB.

explanation: Calfactant (P) is a sterile non-pyrogenic lung surfactant for intratracheal instillation and (S) is an extract of natural surfactant from calf lungs.

explanation: Kaolin is hydrated magnesium silicate/aluminum silicate, Keiselguhr is diatomaceous earth, Calamine contains zinc oxide, and Talc is magnesium silicate.

explanation: Seal coating uses shellac/gelatin, sub coating builds up tablet shape with bulking agents, polishing uses waxes like carnauba wax, and film coating uses polymers like HPMC.

question_text: Match interacting drugs in Group I with pharmacological effects in Group II: (P) Verapamil and Atenolol, (Q) Clozapine and Co-trimoxazole, (R) Alcohol and Flunitrazepam, (S) Ramipril and amiloride.
explanation: Verapamil and atenolol cause severe bradycardia/asystole, clozapine and co-trimoxazole increase bone marrow suppression risk, alcohol and flunitrazepam cause severe CNS depression, and ramipril with amiloride increases hyperkalemia risk.

question_text: Match receptors in Group I with agonists in Group II: (P) beta-adrenergic (Type 2), (Q) alpha-adrenergic (Type 1), (R) Dopaminergic (Type 2), (S) 5-hydroxytryptamine (Type 1A).
explanation: Ritodrine is a beta-2 agonist, phenylephrine is an alpha-1 agonist, bromocriptine is a dopamine D2 agonist, and buspirone is a 5-HT1A agonist.

question_text: Match drugs in Group I with mechanisms in Group II: (P) Terbinafine, (Q) Cidofovir, (R) Imatinib, (S) Stavudine.
explanation: Terbinafine inhibits squalene epoxidase, cidofovir inhibits DNA polymerase, imatinib is a tyrosine kinase inhibitor, and stavudine inhibits reverse transcriptase.

question_text: Match materials used in Group I with instrumental techniques in Group II: (P) Sodium chloride, (Q) Glass, (R) Quartz, (S) Potassium hydrogen phthalate.
explanation: NaCl crystals are used in IR optics/spectrophotometry, glass in colorimetry, quartz in UV spectrophotometry, and potassium hydrogen phthalate as standard.

question_text: Match drugs in Group I with B.P. Assay methods in Group II: (P) Iopanoic acid, (Q) Cyclizine hydrochloride, (R) Chlorothiazide, (S) Chlorambucil.
explanation: Matches standard British Pharmacopoeia assay procedures for each compound.

question_text: Match techniques in Group I with related equations in Group II: (P) Potentiometry, (Q) Polarography, (R) Colorimetry, (S) Column chromatography.
explanation: Potentiometry uses Nernst equation, polarography uses Ilkovic equation, colorimetry uses Beer-Lambert law ($A=ebc$).

question_text: Match tests in Group I with principles in Group II: (P) Direct agglutination test, (Q) Passive agglutination, (R) Haemagglutination inhibition test, (S) Coomb's test.
explanation: Direct agglutination involves particulate antigens, passive uses inert particles coated with soluble antigens, and Coomb's test detects incomplete or blocking antibodies.

question_text: Match enzymes in Group I with functions in Group II: (P) Na+-K+ ATPase, (Q) Cytochrome c oxidase, (R) Malate dehydrogenase, (S) Tyrosine kinase.
explanation: Na+-K+ ATPase generates electrochemical gradients, cytochrome c oxidase functions in electron transport, malate dehydrogenase is part of the TCA/malate-aspartate pathway, and tyrosine kinase handles signal transduction.

explanation: HDL is known as 'good cholesterol' because it helps remove other forms of cholesterol from your bloodstream; low levels increase heart disease risk.

explanation: Lithium (as lithium carbonate) is the classic mood-stabilizing inorganic ion used for the prophylaxis and treatment of bipolar disorder.

explanation: Cyclodextrins are produced by the action of cyclodextrin glycosyltransferase (derived from bacteria such as Bacillus macerans) on starch.

explanation: A Florentine receiver separates immiscible liquids of different densities, such as volatile oils from water in steam distillation.

question_text: The official dissolution test apparatus contains cylindrical vessel and lower edge of the blade is positioned from inside bottom vessel at
explanation: According to USP guidelines for dissolution apparatus 2 (paddle), the distance between the blade and the inside bottom of the vessel is $25 \pm 2 \text{ mm}$ ($23$ to $27 \text{ mm}$).

question_text: As per Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules, the Good Manufacturing Practice is included under schedule
explanation: Schedule M of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act covers GMP requirements for pharmaceutical manufacturing.

question_text: A substance used for modification of silica gel for reversed-phase TLC is
explanation: Impregnating silica gel with silicone oil or paraffin creates a reversed-phase thin-layer chromatographic plate.

question_text: In IR spectrum, the functional group region is from
explanation: The functional group region in an infrared (IR) spectrum typically spans from $4000 \text{ cm}^{-1}$ to $1400 \text{ cm}^{-1}$.

question_text: The equation $E = E^0 + \frac{RT}{nF} \ln a_{M^{n+}}$ is used to measure the
explanation: The Nernst equation calculates the cell potential or electrode potential difference.

question_text: Intermediates in the biosynthesis of cholesterol are
explanation: Mevalonate and isopentenyl pyrophosphate (IPP) are key intermediates in the mevalonate pathway leading to cholesterol biosynthesis.

question_text: A naturally occurring amino acid which does not have a chiral centre is
explanation: Glycine has two hydrogen atoms attached to its alpha carbon, making it achiral.

question_text: A given Gram-positive bacterium is differentiated from Gram-negative by Gram staining. This is because its cell wall contains
explanation: Gram-positive cell walls contain a thick peptidoglycan layer associated with teichoic acids, which helps retain the crystal violet-iodine complex.

question_text: The drug which increases the plasma concentration of digoxin by a pharmacokinetic mechanism is
explanation: Quinidine displaces digoxin from tissue binding sites and reduces its renal clearance, significantly increasing plasma digoxin concentration.

question_text: Microscopic characters of ginger rhizome are

options.B: Cluster crystals of calcium oxalate and sclereids
options.C: Non-lignified vessels and sac shaped starch grains

explanation: Ginger rhizome histology typically shows abundant starch grains, oil cells, and non-lignified fibers, alongside cluster crystals of calcium oxalate and occasional sclereids.

question_text: Klunge's test is for the identification of
explanation: Klunge's test is a specific chemical test used to identify isobarbaloin in aloes.

question_text: 3,4 Benzpyrene present in cigarette smoke reduces the therapeutic activity of Diazepam by

options.D: Increasing the activity of liver microsomal enzymes

explanation: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons like 3,4-benzpyrene induce hepatic CYP enzymes (such as CYP1A2), increasing the metabolism and reducing the effectiveness of drugs like diazepam.

question_text: An NMDA antagonist introduced for treatment of Alzheimer's disease is
explanation: Memantine is a low-affinity uncompetitive NMDA receptor antagonist used for moderate-to-severe Alzheimer's disease.

question_text: Reaction: 2,4-dichloroquinazoline + Hydrazine hydrate (< 20°C for 1 hr in pyridine) -> Resulting product treated with NaOH at 100°C for 1 hr gave an effective product for the treatment of Gout. Identity

explanation: The conversion of a phenyl ester into an ortho- and/or para-hydroxyketone in the presence of a Lewis acid like AlCl3 is the Fries rearrangement.

explanation: Mass of alcohol = $240 \text{ ml} \times 0.816 \text{ g/ml} = 195.84 \text{ g}$. For a 2% w/w solution, mass of drug = $195.84 \times 0.02 / 0.98 \approx 4.0 \text{ g}$ or directly taking $2\% \times 240 \times 0.816 = 3.918 \text{ g}$ close to $4 \text{ g}$.

explanation: Saturated hydrocarbons like cyclohexane absorb only in the vacuum UV region (below $200 \text{ nm}$) due to high-energy $\sigma - \sigma^*$ transitions, making them transparent in the near-UV range.

question_text: Quaternary structure in protein molecules refers to the

options.A: Arrangement of multiple domains in a single polypeptide chain

question_text: Phase I clinical studies of a drug under development is generally carried out on

options.C: A small group of 20-100 healthy male and female volunteers
options.D: Reliable in-vitro cell-lines derived from people suffering with the disease

explanation: Phase I clinical trials primarily evaluate safety, pharmacokinetics, and tolerability in a small group of healthy volunteers (usually 20-100).

explanation: Aspirin-induced asthma occurs because COX inhibition shunts arachidonic acid down the lipoxygenase pathway, leading to an overproduction of bronchoconstrictive leukotrienes (e.g., LTC4/LTD4).

question_text: The vitamin essential in tissue culture medium is
explanation: Thiamine (Vitamin B1) is a vital component often required in plant and animal tissue culture media for cell growth and metabolism.

question_text: Ginkgo biloba is used for its
explanation: Ginkgo biloba contains ginkgolides which act as potent platelet-activating factor (PAF) receptor antagonists.

question_text: The amount of barbaloin present in Aloe vera is
explanation: Aloe vera typically contains about 2 to 2.5% of barbaloin, a key anthraquinone glycoside.

question_text: Sildenafil is used for treatment of one of the following Disorders:
explanation: Sildenafil is a PDE5 inhibitor that is approved for the treatment of pulmonary arterial hypertension.

question_text: Cardiac glycosides have the following configuration in the aglycone part of the steroid nucleus
explanation: Naturally occurring cardiac glycosides possess a $5\beta, 14\beta$-cis-trans-cis steroid nucleus configuration between rings A/B and C/D.

question_text: Quassia wood is adulterated with
explanation: Brucea antidysentrica is a common adulterant of Quassia wood due to similar bitter principles and appearance.

question_text: Eugenol is present in
explanation: Eugenol is the major phenolic constituent found in Tulsi (Ocimum sanctum) and clove oil.

question_text: Which one of the following drugs is prescribed for the treatment of Philadelphia chromosome positive patients with chronic myeloid leukemia?
explanation: Imatinib is a targeted tyrosine kinase inhibitor specifically designed to treat Philadelphia chromosome-positive CML.

question_text: Which of the following monoclonal antibodies is prescribed for patients with non-Hodgkin's Lymphoma
explanation: Rituximab is an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody used widely in non-Hodgkin's lymphoma treatment.

question_text: Identify the drug which is NOT used in the treatment of malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum:
explanation: Primaquine is used to clear liver hypnozoites in P. vivax and P. ovale, not as a primary treatment for acute P. falciparum blood-stage malaria.

question_text: Which one of the following drugs does NOT act through G-Protein coupled receptors
explanation: Insulin acts via a receptor tyrosine kinase, whereas epinephrine, dopamine, and TSH act via GPCRs.

question_text: Which one of the following drugs is most effective in preventing transmission of HIV virus from the mother to the foetus
explanation: Zidovudine (AZT) was historically and remains standard in protocols for reducing mother-to-child vertical transmission of HIV.

question_text: Improvement of memory in Alzheimer's disease is brought about by drugs which increase transmission in
explanation: Alzheimer's disease is associated with a deficit in central cholinergic transmission, treated with acetylcholinesterase inhibitors.

question_text: Which of the following non-opioid analgesic is a prodrug
explanation: Nabumetone is a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory prodrug that is metabolized in vivo to its active acidic form, 6-methoxy-2-naphthylacetic acid.

question_text: Which one of the following drugs is NOT a typical anti-psychotic agent
explanation: Risperidone is an atypical antipsychotic (second-generation), whereas chlorpromazine, haloperidol, and flupentixol are typical (first-generation).

question_text: Which one of the followings is a plasminogen activator
explanation: Streptokinase acts as a thrombolytic by directly activating plasminogen into plasmin.

question_text: Myasthenia gravis is diagnosed with improved neuromuscular function by using
explanation: Edrophonium is a short-acting acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used in the Tensilon test to diagnose myasthenia gravis.

question_text: Which one of the following drugs specifically inhibits calcineurin in the activated T-Lymphocytes
explanation: Tacrolimus (and cyclosporine) binds to immunophilins to inhibit calcineurin, whereas sirolimus inhibits mTOR.

question_text: The chemical behaviour of morphine alkaloid is
explanation: Morphine is amphoteric due to the presence of a basic tertiary amino group and an acidic phenolic hydroxyl group.

question_text: At physiological pH the following compound would be MOSTLY in the structure: CC(C)C1C(N2C1(S)CC2=O)C(=O)O
explanation: Penicillins have a carboxylic acid group with a pKa around 2.5-3.0, meaning at physiological pH (~7.4) they exist predominantly as anions.

question_text: Which one of the followings is used as a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder and also in certain epileptic convulsions?
explanation: Sodium valproate is widely used both as an anticonvulsant and as a mood stabilizer for bipolar disorder.

question_text: An isosteric replacement for carboxylic acid group is
explanation: Tetrazole is a classic acidic bioisostere for the carboxylic acid group, sharing similar pKa and planar properties.

question_text: The given antibiotic is an example of ansamycins
explanation: Rifampicin belongs to the ansamycin class of antibiotics characterized by an ansa structure (an aromatic ring bridged by an aliphatic chain).

question_text: For glyburide, all of the following metabolic reactions are logical EXCEPT
explanation: Glyburide is mainly metabolized via aromatic oxidation of its cyclohexyl ring and O-demethylation of the methoxy group, not amide hydrolysis.

question_text: The effects observed following systemic administration of levodopa in the treatment of Parkinsonism has been attributed to its catabolism to dopamine. Carbidopa, can markedly increase the proportion of levodopa that crosses the bloodbrain barrier by

options.A: Increasing penetration of levodopa through BBB by complexation with it
options.C: Decreasing metabolism of levodopa in the CNS
options.D: Decreasing clearance of levodopa from the CNS

explanation: Carbidopa is a peripheral aromatic L-amino acid decarboxylase inhibitor, reducing peripheral conversion of levodopa to dopamine.

question_text: Ethambutol molecule has
explanation: Ethambutol has two identical chiral carbons, giving rise to 3 stereoisomers (d, l, and meso forms).

question_text: A compound will be sensitive towards IR radiation only when one of the following properties undergo transition on
explanation: A molecular vibration is infrared active only if it causes a net change in the dipole moment of the molecule.

question_text: X-ray crystallographic analysis of an optically active compound determines its
explanation: Single-crystal X-ray diffraction with anomalous dispersion can determine the absolute three-dimensional configuration of chiral molecules.

question_text: Which one of the following statements is WRONG

options.A: A singlet or triplet state may result when one of the electrons from the HOMO is excited to higher energy levels
options.B: In an excited singlet state, the spin of the electron in the higher energy orbital is paired with the electron in the ground state orbital
options.C: Triplet excited state is more stable than the singlet excited state
options.D: When the electron from the singlet excited state returns to ground state, the molecule always shows fluorescence phenomenon.

explanation: Deactivation of a singlet excited state can occur via non-radiative pathways (like heat dissipation or intersystem crossing) as well as fluorescence.

question_text: Aminotransferases usually require the following for their activity
explanation: Pyridoxal phosphate (PLP, the active form of Vitamin B6) is the essential coenzyme for all aminotransferase (transaminase) reactions.

question_text: Purity of water can be assessed by determining one of its following properties instrumentally
explanation: Electrical conductivity is a direct, highly sensitive instrumental measure of ionic impurities and purity in water.

question_text: Which one of the following statements is WRONG

options.A: Carbon NMR is less sensitive than proton NMR
options.C: Both 13C and 1H have same spin quantum numbers
options.D: The gyromagnetic ratio of 1H is lesser than that of 12C

explanation: The gyromagnetic ratio of 1H is actually much larger than that of 13C, and 12C has zero spin.

question_text: In the TCA cycle, at which of the following enzyme-catalyzed steps, incorporation of elements of water into an intermediate of the cycle takes place
explanation: Aconitase catalyzes the reversible hydration-dehydration steps interconverting citrate, cis-aconitate, and isocitrate.

question_text: Humectants added in cosmetic preparations generally act by
explanation: Humectants (like glycerin and propylene glycol) attract and retain moisture through strong hydrogen bonding with water molecules.

question_text: In the mixing of thymol and menthol the following type of incompatibility occurs
explanation: Mixing thymol and menthol results in eutectic formation, leading to liquefaction (a physical incompatibility).

question_text: Bloom strength is used to check the quality of
explanation: Bloom strength is the standard measure of the gel strength and quality of gelatin.

question_text: The characteristic of non-linear pharmacokinetics include

options.A: Area under the curve is proportional to the dose
options.C: Area under the curve is not proportional to the dose
options.D: Amount of drug excreted through remains constant

explanation: Under non-linear (capacity-limited) pharmacokinetics, AUC is not directly proportional to the administered dose.

question_text: In the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules, the Schedule relating to GMP is
explanation: Schedule M of the Indian Drugs and Cosmetics Rules outlines Good Manufacturing Practices (GMP) for pharmaceutical products.

question_text: Thioglycolic acid-like compounds have applications in following type of cosmetic formulations
explanation: Thioglycolic acid and its salts are widely used in chemical depilatories to break disulfide bonds in hair keratin.

question_text: Which one of the following is a flocculating agent for a negatively charged drug
explanation: Multivalent cations such as aluminium chloride are used as flocculating agents to reduce the zeta potential of negatively charged suspensions.

question_text: The healing agent used in hand creams is
explanation: Urea is commonly incorporated into hand creams and ointments for its keratolytic and moisturizing/healing properties.

question_text: Measurement of inulin renal clearance is a measure for
explanation: Inulin clearance is the gold standard clinical measurement for determining the glomerular filtration rate (GFR).

question_text: Highly branched three dimensional macromolecules with controlled structures with all bonds originating from a central core are known as
explanation: Dendrimers are radially symmetric, highly branched, treelike nanoscale macromolecules emanating from a central core.

question_text: Which one of the following is the commonly used bulking agent in the formulation of freeze dried low dose drug products?
explanation: Mannitol is widely used as a bulking and crystalline matrix-forming agent in lyophilized (freeze-dried) parenteral products.

question_text: The applicability of Noyes-Whitney equation is to describe
explanation: The Noyes-Whitney equation quantitatively describes the rate of dissolution of solid particles in a liquid medium.

question_text: Which filler can NOT be used for the preparation of tablets for amine containing basic drugs to avoid discoloration of the tablets?
explanation: Lactose contains a reducing sugar group that undergoes Maillard browning reactions with primary and secondary amines, causing discoloration.

question_text: The ability of human eye using illuminated area to detect a particle is limited to
explanation: Under normal visual inspection with good illumination, the human eye can typically resolve particles down to about 40-50 microns.

question_text: What quantities of $95\%\text{ v/v}$ and $45\%\text{ v/v}$ alcohols are to be mixed to make $800\text{ mL}$ of $65\%\text{ v/v}$ alcohol?

options.A: $480\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $320\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol
options.B: $320\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $480\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol
options.C: $440\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $360\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol
options.D: $360\text{ mL}$ of $95\%$ and $440\text{ mL}$ of $45\%$ alcohol

explanation: Using alligation: parts of 95% = 65-45 = 20; parts of 45% = 95-65 = 30. Ratio is 2:3. Thus, 2/5 of 800 = 320 mL (45%) and 3/5 of 800 = 480 mL (95%).

question_text: The role of borax in cold creams is

options.B: To provide fine particles to polish skin

explanation: Borax reacts with free fatty acids in beeswax to form sodium soaps in-situ, acting as an emulsifying agent in cold creams.

question_text: Choose the right combination

options.D: Palmitic acid, salicylic acid, fatty acids

explanation: Reserpine is a classic indole alkaloid possessing antihypertensive properties.

question_text: Triterpenoids are active constituents of
explanation: Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri) contains active triterpenoid saponins known as bacosides.

question_text: Alkaloids are NOT precipitated by
explanation: Millon's reagent is a specific test for proteins and phenolic compounds (like tyrosine), not a general alkaloidal precipitating reagent.

question_text: Anisocytic stomata are present in
explanation: Belladonna leaves typically feature anisocytic (cruciferous) stomata surrounded by three subsidiary cells of unequal size.

question_text: Bacopa monnieri plant belongs to the family
explanation: Bacopa monnieri belongs to the family Scrophulariaceae (or Plantaginaceae in newer APG systems, but classically Scrophulariaceae).

question_text: Tropane alkaloids are NOT present in
explanation: Lobelia inflata contains piperidine alkaloids (such as lobeline), whereas Datura, Duboisia, and Erythroxylum contain tropane alkaloids.

question_text: Guggul lipids are obtained from
explanation: Guggul is the oleo-gum resin obtained from the plant Commiphora wightii.

question_text: An example of N-glycoside is
explanation: Adenosine is a nucleoside featuring a glycosidic bond between a sugar and a nitrogen atom of adenine (N-glycoside).

question_text: One mg of Lycopodium spores used in quantitative microscopy contains an average of
explanation: One milligram of powdered Lycopodium spores contains an average constant of approximately 90,000 spores used in quantitative microscopy.

question_text: Select the correct combination of drugs for the treatment of patients suffering from Hepatitis C
explanation: Combination therapy of pegylated interferon alfa and ribavirin has been a foundational treatment protocol for chronic Hepatitis C.

question_text: ALISKIREN acts by

options.A: Inhibiting the conversion of Angiotensin I to II
options.C: Inhibiting the binding of Angiotensin II to the receptor

explanation: Aliskiren is a direct renin inhibitor, preventing the enzymatic cleavage of angiotensinogen to angiotensin I.

question_text: Digitalis toxicity is enhanced by co-administration of
explanation: Quinidine displaces digitalis from tissue binding sites and reduces its renal clearance, significantly enhancing digitalis toxicity.

question_text: The rate limiting step in cholesterol biosynthesis is one of the followings:
explanation: The reduction of HMG-CoA to mevalonic acid by HMG-CoA reductase is the rate-limiting step in cholesterol biosynthesis.

question_text: Which one of the following drugs is withdrawn from the market due to torsade de pointes
explanation: Astemizole was withdrawn or severely restricted globally due to its potential to cause QT prolongation and fatal torsades de pointes.

question_text: Ganciclovir is mainly used for the treatment of infection caused by
explanation: Ganciclovir is an antiviral agent specifically indicated for serious cytomegalovirus (CMV) infections.

question_text: Identify the one rational combination which has clinical benefit:
explanation: Amoxicillin combined with clavulanic acid is a classic rational combination where clavulanate protects amoxicillin from beta-lactamase degradation.

question_text: Stevens Johnson syndrome is the most common adverse effect associated with ofthe following category of drugs
explanation: Sulfonamides are well known for causing severe cutaneous adverse reactions such as Stevens-Johnson syndrome.

question_text: Amitriptyline is synthesized from the following starting material
explanation: Although multiple routes exist, phthalic anhydride derivatives or related multi-step aromatic precursors are classically taught in foundational synthesis pathways for tricyclics.

question_text: The common structural feature amongst the three categories of anti-convulsant drugs Barbiturates, succinimides and hydantoins is
explanation: Barbiturates, succinimides, and hydantoins all share a cyclic ureide (acylurea) core structure responsible for their anticonvulsant activity.

question_text: Nicotinic action of acetylcholine is blocked by the drug
explanation: d-Tubocurarine is a classic competitive neuromuscular blocker that blocks nicotinic receptors at the skeletal neuromuscular junction.

question_text: Chemical nomenclature of procaine is
explanation: Procaine chemically is the ester of 4-aminobenzoic acid and 2-diethylaminoethanol, named 2-diethylaminoethyl 4-aminobenzoate.
