question_text: In which of the following techniques the sample is kept below triple point

A glycoalkaloid [P] Contains sulphur in addition to nitrogen in its molecule [Q] Is glycosidic in nature. [R] Can be hydrolysed to an alkaloid. [S] Always contains endocyclic nitrogen in its molecule.
explanation: Glycoalkaloids are glycosidic compounds containing a sugar moiety attached to an alkaloid aglycone, which can be liberated upon hydrolysis.

question_text: Which of the following statements are true for ginseng root [P] It is among the most traded plant material of Brazil [Q] It is obtained from Panax ginseng and Panax quinquefolium [R] It is obtained from young plants of six months to one year age [S] It contains derivatives of protopanaxadiol
explanation: Ginseng is obtained from Panax species and contains ginsenosides which are derivatives of protopanaxadiol and protopanaxatriol.

question_text: Which of the following drugs is a triterpenoid containing root?
explanation: Shatavari contains steroidal saponins and triterpenoid roots.

question_text: Which of the following alkaloids is derived from tyrosine
explanation: Morphine is a benzylisoquinoline alkaloid derived biosynthetically from tyrosine.

question_text: The following options carry the name of the plant, part used and its family. Find a wrong combination.

options.C: Glycyrrhiza glabra, root and stolon & Leguminosae

explanation: Strophanthus gratus belongs to the family Apocynaceae, not Scrophulariaceae.

question_text: Anomocytic stomata, trichomes with collapsed cell and absence of calcium oxalate crystals are some of the microscopic features of which plant
explanation: Hyoscyamus leaves possess anomocytic stomata and glandular trichomes with multicellular stalks and collapsed heads.

question_text: Each of the following options lists the name of the drug, its class, pharmacological action and plant source. Choose an option showing a wrong combination.
explanation: Myrrh is obtained from Commiphora molmol or Commiphora abyssinica, whereas Commiphora wightii yields guggul.

question_text: Quinoline alkaloids are biosynthesized via which one of the following pathways
explanation: Quinoline alkaloids like quinine are derived from tryptophan and secologanin via the strictosidine pathway.

question_text: Which of the following ergot alkaloids is water soluble and shows blue fluorescence
explanation: Ergometrine (ergobasine) is the only water-soluble ergot alkaloid and exhibits blue fluorescence in solution.

question_text: Khellin is an active constituent of which one of the following plants
explanation: Khellin is a furanochromone obtained from the fruits of Ammi visnaga.

question_text: Goldbeater's skin test is used to detect the presence of which one of the following classes of compounds
explanation: Goldbeater's skin test is a standard qualitative assay for the detection of tannins.

question_text: Which one of the following compounds is useful for the stimulation of cell division and release of lateral bud dormancy?
explanation: Zeatin is a naturally occurring cytokinin that promotes cell division and breaks bud dormancy.

question_text: Phenylethylisoquinoline is the precursor of which of the following alkaloids
explanation: Colchicine is biosynthetically derived from phenylethylisoquinoline precursors.

question_text: A powdered drug has the following microscopic characters: Anther cells, parenchyma, pollen grains, phloem fibers, volatile oil cells and stone cells. The powder is obtained from which of the followings?
explanation: Phloem fibers and stone cells are characteristic of clove stalks, which contaminate clove bud powder when mixed.

question_text: Arrange the following fatty acids in decreasing order of their unsaturation (highest to lowest) [P] Stearic [Q] Oleic acid [R] Linolenic acid [S] Linoleic acid
explanation: Linolenic acid has 3 double bonds, linoleic has 2, oleic has 1, and stearic acid is saturated (0 double bonds).

question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]: Assertion (a): Tannins are polyphenolic substances occurring in plant cell sap. Hydrolysable and condensed tannins are differentiated by match stick test. Reason (r): The condensed tannins are resistant to acid hydrolysis therefore stain the lignin present in matchstick.

options.A: Both (a) and (r) are true, and (r) is a correct reason for (a)
options.B: Both (a) and (r) are true, but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)
options.C: (a) is true but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)

explanation: Condensed tannins react with phloroglucinol-HCl in the matchstick test to produce a red color due to their reaction with lignin/phlobaphenes.

question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]: Assertion (a): Castor oil is soluble in alcohol and is used as purgative. Reason (r): The oil contains ricinoleic acid having a hydroxyl group at C-12 position which is responsible for its solubility in alcohol and its purgative action.

options.A: Both (a) and (r) are true but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)
options.B: (a) is true but (r) is NOT the correct reason for (a)
options.C: Both (a) and (r) are true and (r) is the correct reason for (a)

explanation: The presence of the free hydroxyl group in ricinoleic acid imparts polarity, making castor oil soluble in alcohol and driving its irritant purgative action.

question_text: In acetate mevalonate pathway geranyl pyrophosphate leads to formation of monoterpenes, the major constituents of volatile oils. [P] Geranyl pyrophosphate contains two isoprene units [Q] Monoterpenes have 15 carbon atoms [R] The two isoprene units condense in head to tail fashion to give Monoterpenes [S] Isoprene unit has molecular formula of $C_5H_8$. which one of the given statements is correct?

options.A: P is true, Q is false, R is true, S is false
options.B: P is false, Q is true, R is true, S is false
options.C: P is true, Q is true, R is false, S is true
options.D: P is true, Q is false, R is true, S is true

explanation: Monoterpenes contain 10 carbons (two C5 units), so statement Q is false, while P, R, and S are correct.

question_text: Two genetic types of Cannabis i.e. drug type and Hemp types are cultivated. [P] Drug type cannabis is rich in (-)$9$-trans-tetrahydrocannabinol [Q] Hemp type cannabis is rich in cannabidiol [R] Drug type cannabis is rich in cannabidiol [S] Hemp type cannabis contains elongated bast fibres which one of the given statements is correct?

options.A: P is true, Q is true, R is true, S is true
options.B: P is true, Q is true, R is false, S is true
options.C: P is true, Q is true, R is false, S is false
options.D: P is false, Q is true, R is false, S is true

explanation: Drug-type cannabis is rich in psychoactive THC, whereas hemp-type is cultivated for fiber and is rich in CBD.

question_text: Each of the following options lists a phytoconstituent, its phytochemical grouping, pharmacological activity and corresponding semisynthetic analogue. Find a MISMATCHING option
explanation: Sinigrin is a glucosinolate found in mustard, not a semisynthetic analogue of sennoside.

question_text: Inhibition/induction of which of the following Cytochrome P450 enzyme system ismost likely to be involved in important drug-drug interactions
explanation: CYP3A4 is the most abundant hepatic CYP450 enzyme and metabolizes the largest share of clinically used drugs, making it primary for interactions.

question_text: Which of the following mechanisms is NOT related to platelet aggregation inhibitory action
explanation: Prostacyclin inhibits platelet aggregation; thus, prostacyclin inhibition would promote, not inhibit, platelet aggregation.

question_text: Choose the correct statement about the given four diseases? [P] Cardiomyopathy [Q] Rheumatoid arthritis [R] Myasthenia gravis [S] Ulcerative colitis

options.C: P & R are not autoimmune disorders
options.D: R & S are not autoimmune disorders

explanation: Rheumatoid arthritis and ulcerative colitis are well-known autoimmune disorders.

question_text: Which of the following species is being inactivated by the enzyme Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4
explanation: DPP-4 is the enzyme responsible for the rapid degradation of incretin hormones like GLP-1 and GIP.

question_text: Patients taking isosorbide mononitrate or nitroglycerine should be advised not to take Sildenafil. This drug- drug interaction causes which of the following actions
explanation: Combining nitrates with PDE5 inhibitors causes a synergistic rise in cGMP leading to profound, potentially fatal hypotension.

question_text: Which of the following drugs does NOT induce mydriasis?
explanation: Phentolamine is an alpha blocker that causes miosis rather than mydriasis.

question_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE for angiotensin-II

options.B: Decreases the action of sympathetic nervous system
options.D: Decreases the synthesis and release of aldosterone

explanation: Angiotensin II promotes vascular and cardiac remodeling, including myocyte hypertrophy.

question_text: Which of the following beta blockers has been shown clinically to reduce mortality in patients of symptomatic heart failure
explanation: Carvedilol, metoprolol succinate, and bisoprolol are proven to reduce mortality in heart failure.

question_text: All of the given four drugs cause vasodilatation. Choose the correct statement about them. [P] Bradykinin [Q] Minoxidil [R] Acetylcholine [S] Hydralazine

options.A: P & Q cause release of nitric oxide
options.B: Q & R do not cause release of nitric oxide
options.C: R & S cause release of nitric oxide
options.D: P & S do not cause release of nitric oxide

explanation: Bradykinin and minoxidil or endothelial-dependent pathways involve nitric oxide release for vasodilation.

question_text: Rhabdomyolysis is the side effect associated with which of the following classes of drugs
explanation: Statins are well-known to cause myopathy and rhabdomyolysis as a severe adverse effect.

question_text: Blood level monitoring of HbA1c is important in which of the given diseased states
explanation: HbA1c reflects average blood glucose over the past 3 months and is the standard metric for monitoring diabetes mellitus.

question_text: Most of the emergency contraceptives have which of the following active ingredients
explanation: Levonorgestrel is the standard progestin used in emergency contraceptive pills (e.g., Plan B).

question_text: Which of the following antibiotics produces concentration dependent bactericidal action and also possesses post-antibiotic effect
explanation: Aminoglycosides like amikacin exhibit concentration-dependent killing and a significant post-antibiotic effect.

question_text: Antiretroviral Raltegravir is unique, because of which of its following actions
explanation: Raltegravir was the first HIV integrase strand transfer inhibitor approved for clinical use.

question_text: What is chemotaxis
explanation: Chemotaxis refers to the directional movement of cells (such as leucocytes) in response to chemical gradients during inflammation.

question_text: Which one of the followings is NOT an example of G-protein coupled receptor?
explanation: Nicotinic cholinergic receptors are ligand-gated ion channels, not G-protein coupled receptors.

question_text: Which of the followings used in the treatment of rheumatoid arthritis is NOT a biologic response modifier
explanation: Leflunomide is a conventional synthetic DMARD, whereas the others are biologic DMARDs.

question_text: Which of the following statements is FALSE for artemisinin?

options.A: It is a sesquiterpene lactone endoperoxide
options.B: It is a drug of choice in prophylaxis of malaria
options.C: It does not cure relapsing malaria
options.D: It is useful in treatment of cerebral falciparum malaria

explanation: Artemisinins are not used for malaria prophylaxis due to their short half-life and to prevent resistance development.

question_text: Which of the followings is a noncompetitive inhibitor of the enzyme reverse transcriptase in HIV
explanation: Nevirapine is a non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitor (NNRTI), which acts as a noncompetitive inhibitor.

question_text: Which of the followings is the most effective monotherapy for raising HDL cholesterol
explanation: Niacin (nicotinic acid) remains the most effective pharmacologic agent for increasing HDL cholesterol levels.

question_text: Which of the following parameters from plasma concentration time profile study gives indication of the rate of drug absorption?
explanation: T_max is the time required to reach peak plasma concentration and reflects the rate of drug absorption.

question_text: Which of the following pairs has high binding affinity for 5\alpha -reductase
explanation: Finasteride is a competitive inhibitor of 5-alpha-reductase, and testosterone is the natural substrate with high affinity.

question_text: Which of the following skeletal muscle relaxants acts directly on the contractile mechanism of the muscle fibers
explanation: Dantrolene acts directly on skeletal muscle by blocking ryanodine receptors (RyR1), inhibiting calcium release from the sarcoplasmic reticulum.

question_text: Which is the molecular target for the vinca alkaloids as anticancer agents
explanation: Vinca alkaloids bind to tubulin and inhibit the formation of microtubules, arresting cells in metaphase.

question_text: Choose the correct pair of the neurodegenerative disorders from those given below.
explanation: Both Parkinson's and Alzheimer's are characterized by progressive neurodegeneration.

question_text: A 64 year old woman with a history of Type II diabetes is diagnosed with heart failure. Which of the followings would be a Poor choice in controlling her diabetes
explanation: Thiazolidinediones like pioglitazone cause fluid retention and worsen or precipitate heart failure, making them contraindicated.

question_text: Mifepristone and gemeprost combination is used for medical termination of pregnancy. The action is caused due to which of the following mechanisms

options.A: Mifepristone is an antiestrogen while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor agonist
options.B: Mifepristone is an antiprogestin while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor agonist
options.C: Mifepristone is an antiandrogen while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor agonist
options.D: Mifepristone is an antiprogestin while gemeprost is a prostaglandin E receptor antagonist

explanation: Mifepristone is a progesterone receptor antagonist (antiprogestin) and gemeprost is a PGE1 analogue that contracts the uterus.

question_text: Which one of the following is a $\beta$ lactamase inhibitor
explanation: Clavulanic acid is a well-known mechanism-based inhibitor of beta-lactamase enzymes.

question_text: All of the followings are indications for use of ACE inhibitors Except for one. Identify that
explanation: Pheochromocytoma is managed using alpha blockers (e.g., phenoxybenzamine), not ACE inhibitors.

question_text: Neural tube defects may occur by which one of the following anti-seizure drugs
explanation: Valproic acid is strongly associated with a high incidence of neural tube defects (like spina bifida) when taken during pregnancy.

question_text: Which water is used for hand washing in a change room of pharmaceutical manufacturing plant?
explanation: Potable (drinking) water is standard for washing hands prior to entering pharmaceutical processing areas.

question_text: Which one of the following drying methods is commonly used in Pharma industry for dryingof soft shell capsules?
explanation: Fluid bed drying is extensively used for the rapid and uniform drying of soft gelatin capsules.

question_text: Which one of the followings does NOT afford a macromolecular inclusion compound
explanation: Cyclodextrins form molecular inclusion complexes, whereas zeolites and dextrins/gels form larger channel or network lattices.

question_text: If C is the concentration of dissolved drug and Cs is the saturation concentration. In which case the sink conditions are said to be maintained?
explanation: Sink conditions are generally maintained when the concentration of the solute in the bulk solution is kept well below saturation, typically below 10% to 20% of Cs (often cited as < 10%-20% with < 10% being the stricter definition).

question_text: Which condition does not apply as per Indian law while conducting single dose bioavailability study of an immediate release product

options.A: Sampling period should be at least three t_1/2 el
options.B: Sampling should represent pre-exposure, peak exposure and post-exposure phases
options.C: There should be at least four sampling points during elimination phase
options.D: Sampling should be continued till measured AUC is at least equal to 80% of AUC

explanation: Typically, at least 3 to 4 points are needed in the terminal elimination phase, but specific regulatory guidance requires AUC truncation rules rather than exactly four points in elimination.

question_text: Upon standing sometimes gel system shrinks a bit and little liquid is pressed out. What is this phenomenon, known as
explanation: Syneresis is the contraction of a gel upon standing, with the consequent squeezing out of liquid.

question_text: Which of the following routes of administration of drugs is associated with Phlebitis
explanation: Phlebitis is inflammation of a vein, commonly associated with intravenous catheterization and IV drug administration.

question_text: Study the following two statements and choose the correct answer: [P] Antibodies are serum proteins providing immunity. [Q] IgG provides immunity to new born babies while IgM is the first generated antibody.

options.A: P is correct and Q is incorrect
options.B: P is incorrect and Q is correct
options.C: Both P and Q are correct
options.D: Both P and Q are incorrect

explanation: Both statements are immunologically accurate regarding antibody classes and functions.

question_text: Which microbe is used for validation of sterilization by filtration process
explanation: Pseudomonas diminuta (ATCC 19146) is the standard challenge microorganism used for membrane filter validation due to its small size (0.3 um).

question_text: Non-linear pharmacokinetics can be expected due to [P] Enzyme induction [Q] Active secretion Choose the correct answer

options.A: Both P and Q are true
options.B: P is true, Q is false
options.C: Q is true, P is false
options.D: Both P and Q are false

explanation: Both enzyme induction and active transport/secretion processes are known causes of non-linear (dose-dependent) pharmacokinetics.

question_text: Which wavelength of the UV light provides maximum germicidal action
explanation: Germicidal UV lamps typically emit around $253.7\text{ nm}$, which corresponds to the peak absorption of nucleic acids.

question_text: Which of the following statements is INCORRECT

options.A: Chick Martin test uses organic matter in media
options.B: The organism in Rideal-walker test is S. typhi
options.C: Rideal-walker test uses organic matter in media
options.D: The organism in Chick Martin test is S. typhi

explanation: Unlike the Chick Martin test, the Rideal-Walker test does not use organic matter in the testing medium.

question_text: Which of the following forces contribute to stability of charge-transfer complexes

options.C: Dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces

explanation: Charge-transfer complex stability involves resonance structures of the complex as well as London dispersion forces.

question_text: Which of the following isotherms are produced when the heat of condensation of successive layers is more than the heat of adsorption of first layer
explanation: Type III and V isotherms occur when adsorbate-adsorbate interactions are greater than adsorbent-adsorbate interactions.

question_text: Which of the followings act as a non-ionic emulsifying agent
explanation: Polysorbates (polyoxyethylene sorbitan fatty acid esters) are classic non-ionic surfactants.

question_text: The minimal effective flow rate of air in laminar flow hood should be not less than how many cubic feet per minute
explanation: Standard laminar airflow hoods require a velocity delivering approximately $100\text{ ft}^3/\text{min}$ ($\pm 20\%$) to maintain sterility.

question_text: Which of the following Schedules include shelf life of drugs
explanation: Schedule P of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act prescribes the life period (shelf-life) of drugs.

question_text: Which of the following pumps is used in handling of corrosive liquids
explanation: Peristaltic pumps isolate the fluid inside the tubing, making them ideal for corrosive or sterile liquids without pump contamination.

question_text: By addition of which of the followings the shells of soft gelatin capsules may be made elastic
explanation: Plasticizers such as sorbitol and glycerol are added to gelatin to impart flexibility and elasticity.

question_text: Convert $90\%\text{ v/v}$ akohol to Proof strength. Choose the correct answer.
explanation: Proof strength $= (\% \text{v/v} \times 1.753) - 100$. For $90\%$, $(90 \times 1.753) - 100 = 157.77 - 100 = 57.77^{\circ}$ over proof.

question_text: Department of Transport Test (DOT) is performed for which of the followings
explanation: The Department of Transportation (DOT) leak test and pressure test are standard evaluations for aerosol containers.

question_text: What is the Heat of vaporization of water at $100^{\circ}\text{C}$?

question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]: Assertion[a]: For a pharmaceutical powder true density is greater than the granule density. question_text: Define Plasmapheresis. Choose the correct answer

question_text: Choose the correct sequence of Moisture vapor Transmission Rate in packaging materials?

question_text: How many $\text{mL}$ of $50\%\text{ (w/v)}$ dextrose solution and how many $\text{mL}$ of $5\%\text{ (w/v)}$ dextrose solution are required to prepare $4500\text{ mL}$ of a $10\%\text{ (w/v)}$ solution?

question_text: A drug is administered to a $65\text{ Kg}$ patient as $500\text{ mg}$ tablets every $4\text{ hours}$. Half-life of the drug is $3\text{ h}$, volume of distribution is $2\text{ liter/Kg}$ and oral bioavailability of the drug is $0.85$. Calculate the steady state concentration of the drug
explanation: Css = $(F \times Dose) / (Cl \times \tau)$. Calculation yields approximately $5.05\text{ mcg/ml}$.

question_text: P-Glycoprotein pump is responsible for which one of the followings

options.C: Transporting the drugs from oral mucosa into blood capillaries

question_text: The first stage of wetting on addition of a granulating agent to the powders is characterized by which one of the followings?

question_text: Larger values of Ky in the Heckel Plot indicate formation of what quality of tablets?
explanation: A larger Heckel constant $k$ (or $K_y$) reflects higher plasticity and lower yield strength, often corresponding to softer or more readily deformable materials.

question_text: The degree of flocculation of a suspension is $1.5$ and the sedimentation volume is $0.75$. What will be the ultimate volume of deflocculated suspension
explanation: Degree of flocculation $\beta = F / F_\infty$. Thus $F_\infty = 0.75 / 1.5 = 0.5$.

question_text: What will be the time required for a drug exhibiting first order rate constant of $4.6/\text{hr}$ to be degraded from initial concentration of $100\text{ mg/ml}$ to $10\text{ mg/ml}$?
What will be the dose required maintaining therapeutic concentration of $20\text{ }\mu\text{gm/ml}$ for $24\text{ hr}$ of a drug exhibiting total clearance of $2\text{ L/hr}$?
explanation: Total Dose = $C_p \times Cl \times t = 20\text{ }\mu\text{g/mL} \times 2000\text{ mL/hr} \times 24\text{ hr} = 960,000\text{ }\mu\text{g} = 960\text{ mg}$.

question_text: What will be the urine to plasma ratio of a weakly acidic drug having pKa of $5$? [urine $(\text{pH} : 5)$ plasma $(\text{pH} : 7)$]
explanation: For a weak acid, $U/P = (1 + 10^{\text{pH}_u - \text{pKa}}) / (1 + 10^{\text{pH}_p - \text{pKa}}) = (1 + 10^{5-5}) / (1 + 10^{7-5}) = 2 / 101 \approx 1:50.5$ or closer to $1:101$ derivation based on ionized fractions.

question_text: The Reynolds number widely used to classify flow behavior of fluids is the ratio of which one of the followings:
explanation: Reynolds number is the ratio of inertial forces to viscous forces within a fluid.

question_text: If the distillation graph using McCabe Thiele method is parallel to x-axis, then the feed is which one of the followings?
explanation: In McCabe-Thiele analysis, a feed line slope of zero (q = 0, parallel to x-axis) represents a saturated vapor feed.

question_text: What for the baffles are provided in a shell and tube heat exchanger?
explanation: Baffles direct fluid flow across the tube bundle, increasing turbulence and heat transfer efficiency.

question_text: SOS means which one of the followings

question_text: Which statement is FALSE for Association Colloids
explanation: Association colloids (micelles) form via hydrophobic association and are typically solvated at their hydrophilic outer shells, making 'partial solvation' an inaccurate distinguishing false statement.

question_text: Which of the followings is NOT a reciprocating pump

question_text: A drug whose solubility is $1\text{ g/L}$ in water; when given orally at a dose of $500\text{ mg}$ is absorbed up to $95\%$ of the administered dose. The drug belongs to which class according to the BCS classification?
explanation: Dose = $500\text{ mg} = 0.5\text{ g}$. Solubility = $1\text{ g/L}$, so volume required to dissolve dose is $500\text{ mL}$ ($< 250\text{ mL}$ threshold is high solubility if dose/solubility volume $\le 250\text{ mL}$). Since absorption is $95\%$, it is high permeability, placing it in BCS Class I.

question_text: Arrange the following Lowry-Bronsted acids into their decreasing order of acidity (highest to lowest) [P] $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}$ [Q] $\text{H}_3\text{C}-\text{C}\equiv\text{CH}$ [R] $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ [S] $\text{CH}_3\text{NH}_2$

question_text: Pyridine is more basic than pyrrole. This is due to which of the following facts
