explanation: 1,4-Dimethylcyclohexane possesses high symmetry leading to four unique carbon and proton environments.

question_text: Out of the four given compounds choose the one which is aromatic.
explanation: Azulene is a non-benzenoid aromatic hydrocarbon satisfying Hückel's rule with 10 $\pi$-electrons.

question_text: Quantification of minute quantity of a drug from a complex matrix, without prior separation can be done using one of the following techniques. Identify that.
explanation: Radioimmunoassay (RIA) provides extreme sensitivity and specificity for measuring trace analytes directly in complex biological fluids without prior extraction.

question_text: Which one of the following fragmentation pathways involves a double bond and hydrogen in mass spectrometry
explanation: McLafferty rearrangement is a characteristic mass spectral fragmentation involving a six-membered transition state with transfer of a $\gamma$-hydrogen to a double bond heteroatom/carbonyl.

question_text:
Read the following statements carefully about non-aqueous titrations:
[P]: Acetate ion is the strongest base capable of existence in acetic acid.
[Q]: Mixtures of bases of different strengths can be analyzed by selecting a differentiating solvent for the bases.
[R]: Acetic acid acts as a leveling solvent for various acids like perchloric and hydrochloric acids.
[S]: Mixtures of bases of different strengths can be analyzed by selecting a leveling solvent for the bases.
Choose the correct answer.

options.A: P and Q are true and R and S are false
options.B: P and S are true and R and Q are false
options.C: R and Q are true and P and S are false
options.D: R and S are true and P and Q are false

explanation: Acetic acid levels strong acids, but acetate is its strongest base (leveling effect), and differentiating solvents are used to resolve bases of different strengths.

question_text:
Read the following statements carefully about Volhards method:
[P]: In Volhard's titration, silver ions are titrated with thiocyanates in acidic solution
[Q]: Ferric ions act as indicator in Volhard's method, yielding reddish brown ferric thiocyanate
[R]: Volhard's method is used to determine halides
[S]: Volhard's method is a direct titration
Choose the correct set of answers.

options.A: P, Q and R are true and S is false
options.B: Q, R and S are true and P is false
options.C: R, S and P true and Q is false
options.D: P, Q, R and S all are true

explanation: Volhard's method is an indirect (residual) titration, making statement S false while P, Q, and R are correct.

question_text: Identify the group of enzymes that utilizes NADP or NAD as coenzymes and catalyzes biochemical reactions by the transfer of electrons from one molecule to another.
explanation: Oxidoreductases catalyze oxidation-reduction reactions involving electron transfer, often using NAD+/NADP+ coenzymes.

question_text: Glucose is the only source of energy for one of the followings. Identify that.
explanation: Mature red blood cells lack mitochondria and rely exclusively on anaerobic glycolysis of glucose for energy.

question_text:
Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and Reason [r]: Assertion [a] : Halogens are unusual in their effect on electrophilic aromatic substitution; they are deactivating yet ortho-, para - directing. Reason [r] : In electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions, reactivity is controlled by stronger inductive effect while orientation is controlled by the stronger hyperconjugation effect.
Choose the correct statement.

options.B: Both [a] and [r] are true and [r] is the correct reason for [a]
options.D: Both [a] and [r] are true but [r] is NOT the correct reason

explanation: Assertion is true due to inductive withdrawal (deactivation) and resonance donation (ortho/para orientation), making the reason false.

question_text:
Given are the four statements about dehydration of alcohols to give alkenes:
[P]: Ease of dehydration of alcohols takes place in the order $3^\circ > 2^\circ > 1^\circ$.
[Q]: Dehydration is acid catalyzed.
[R]: Orientation of the alkene formed is strongly Saytzeff.
[S]: Dehydration is irreversible.
Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P and Q are correct while R and S are not
options.B: P, Q and R all three are correct but S is not
options.C: P, Q, R and S all are correct
options.D: P, Q and S all are correct but R is not

explanation: Dehydration is an equilibrium reaction (reversible), making statement S false, while P, Q, and R are correct.

question_text: Choose the correct statement regarding the synthesis of phenyl n-propyl ether.

options.A: Phenyl n-propyl ether is prepared from n-propyl bromide and sodium phenoxide
options.B: Phenyl n-propyl ether is prepared from bromobenzene and sodium n-propoxide
options.C: Phenyl n-propyl ether can be prepared by either of the two methods
options.D: Both (a) and (b) are not the correct methods for the synthesis of phenyl n-propyl ether

explanation: Williamson ether synthesis works best with unhindered alkyl halides (n-propyl bromide) and phenoxide nucleophiles, as aryl halides are unreactive to nucleophilic substitution.

question_text:
Read the following statements about SN1 reactions:
[P]: They proceed with complete inversion (Walden inversion).
[Q]: They proceed with racemization plus some net inversion.
[R]: They are characterized by rearrangements.
[S]: They are characterized by the reactivity sequence, $CH_3 > 1^\circ > 2^\circ > 3^\circ$.
Choose the correct combination?

options.A: P and Q are true while R and S are false
options.B: P and R are true while S and Q are false
options.C: Q and R are true while P and S are false
options.D: R and S are true while P and Q are false

explanation: SN1 reactions involve carbocation intermediates leading to racemization with partial inversion and carbocation rearrangements (Q and R are correct).

question_text:
Read the following statements carefully:
[P]: Pyrrole and thiophene undergo electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions much faster than benzene
[Q]: Pyrrole and thiophene undergo Diels Alder addition reaction very fast
[R]: Pyrrole and thiophene undergo nucleophilic aromatic substitution reaction faster than benzene
[S]: Pyrrole is a pie excessive system while thiophene is a pie deficient system

options.A: Q only is true while P, R and S are false
options.B: R and S are true while P and Q are false
options.C: P and R are true while Q and S are false
options.D: P only is true white Q, R and S are false

explanation: Pyrrole and thiophene are pi-excessive heterocycles that undergo rapid electrophilic aromatic substitution compared to benzene (P is true; both are pi-excessive, making S false).

question_text: Among the followings which one is not only a non-reducing sugar but also does not exhibit mutarotation?
explanation: Sucrose has both anomeric carbons involved in the glycosidic bond, making it a non-reducing sugar that cannot open to form a free aldehyde/ketone, hence no mutarotation.

question_text: Choose the most basic heterocyclic compound among the followings.
explanation: Pyrrolidine is a saturated secondary amine heterocycle with a high pKa (~11.3), making it significantly more basic than aromatic heterocycles or pyrrole.

question_text:
Followings are some drug derivatives used to increase/decrease the water solubility of the parent drugs:
[P]: Rolitetracycline
[Q]: Erythromycin lactobionate
[R]: Chloramphenicol succinate
[S]: Erythromycin stearate
Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: Q and R are used to increase water solubility while P and S are used to decrease it
options.B: P, Q and R are used to increase water solubility while S is used to decrease it
options.C: Q, S and R are used to increase water solubility while P is used to decrease it
options.D: Q and S are used to increase water solubility and R are used to decrease it

explanation: Rolitetracycline, erythromycin lactobionate, and chloramphenicol succinate are prodrugs/salts designed to enhance water solubility, whereas erythromycin stearate decreases water solubility for taste masking or sustained release.

question_text:
Study the following statements on prevention of crystalluria. By the given approaches crystalluria can be prevented
[P]: By co-administration of sulfadiazine, sulfamerazine and sulfamethazine
[Q]: By increasing the pH of urine
[R]: By co-administration of sulphanilamide, sulphamethoxazole and folic acid
[S]: By administration of co-trimoxazole
Choose the correct combination of statements.
explanation: Multiple sulfonamides can be combined to reduce individual saturation (triple sulfa) and alkalinization of urine increases ionization and solubility.

question_text:
Progesterone is obtained from diosgenin through the following sequence of chemical reactions:
[P]: Acetylation, $CrO_3$ (oxidation), Acetolysis, $H_2/Pd$, Hydrolysis and Oppenauer oxidation
[Q]: Oppenauer oxidation, Acetylation, $CrO_3$ (oxidation), Acetolysis, $H_2/Pd$ and Hydrolysis
[R]: $CrO_3$ (oxidation), Acetolysis, Acetytation, Oppenauer oxidation, Hydrolysis and $H_2/Pd$
[S]: Acetylation, $H_2/Pd$, Hydrolysis, $CrO_3$ (oxidation), Oppenauer oxidation and Acetolysis
Choose the correct sequence of reactions.
explanation: The standard industrial conversion of diosgenin to progesterone starts with acetylation followed by oxidation and subsequent steps represented in sequence P.

question_text:
Following statements are given for local anaesthetic drug lidocaine:
[P]: It contains a xylidine moiety
[Q]: It can be used as antiarrhythmic agent on oral administration.
[R]: When administered along with adrenaline its toxicity is reduced and its effect is prolonged
[S]: Chemically it is 2-diethylamino-2',6'-dimethylphenyl acetamide
Choose the correct combination of statements.
explanation: Lidocaine undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism so it is not given orally as an antiarrhythmic (making Q false); P, R, and S are correct.

question_text:
One of the following ring systems can be used as the bioisosteric replacement for benzene ring in drug design:
[P]: Thiophene
[Q]: Cyclohexa-1,3-diene
[R]: Pyrrolidine
[S]: Imidazoline
Identify the correct answer.
explanation: Thiophene is a classic classical/non-classical bioisostere for a benzene ring due to similar aromatic stabilization and spatial properties.

question_text:
Some of the following statements describe the properties of Dropping Mercury Electrode (DME) correctly:
[P]: Constant renewal of electrode surface eliminates poisoning effects.
[Q]: Mercury makes many metal ions easily reducible.
[R]: Mercury has large hydrogen over-voltage.
[S]: The electrode can get oxidised with ease.
Identify the correct combination.

options.A: All statements P, Q, R and S are correct
options.B: Statements P, Q and R only are correct
options.C: Statements P, R and S only are correct
options.D: Statements P, Q and S only are correct

explanation: Mercury resists oxidation at negative potentials (making S incorrect, as it is difficult to oxidize compared to other metals). Thus P, Q, and R are correct.

question_text:
Penicillin ring system is derived from two of the following amino acids:
[P]: Alanine and methionine
[Q]: Cysteine and valine
[R]: Glycine and cysteine
[S]: Methionine and leucine
Choose the correct pair.
explanation: Biosynthetically, the core of penicillins is assembled from L-cysteine and L-valine.

question_text: For the management of which disease the given drug tacrine is used? Identify. (Tacrine structure shown with acridine ring)
explanation: Tacrine is a centrally acting reversible acetylcholinesterase inhibitor used for treating Alzheimer's disease.

question_text: Low dose aspirin acts as anti-platelet aggregating agent by which one of the following mechanisms? Find the correct answer

options.A: It acts as a suicide substrate for COX-1 enzyme present in platelets
options.B: It acts as a transition state analog for COX-2 enzyme present in the platelets
options.C: It acts as a reversible inhibitor of lipoxygenase present in the platelets
options.D: It acts as an affinity label of oxidoreductases present in the platelets

explanation: Aspirin irreversibly acetylates serine-530 of COX-1 in platelets, acting as a suicide substrate to block thromboxane A2 synthesis.

question_text: Some statements are given for clavulanic acid, sulbactam and tazobactam: [P] : All three lack the 6-acylamino side chain [Q] : All are potent inhibitors of the enzyme $\beta$-lactamase [R] : All are prodrugs of penicillin [S] : All have weak antibacterial activity Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P, Q and R are true while S is false
options.B: Q, R and S are true while P is false
options.C: P, R and S are true while Q is false
options.D: P, Q and S are true while R is false

explanation: Clavulanic acid, sulbactam, and tazobactam lack the 6-acylamino side chain (or equivalent structural modification), are potent beta-lactamase inhibitors with weak intrinsic antibacterial activity, but they are not prodrugs of penicillin themselves.

question_text: Electrophilic aromatic substitution reactions in indole give one of the following products preferably. Identify that.
explanation: Electrophilic aromatic substitution in indole preferentially occurs at the C-3 position because the resulting intermediate maintains an intact benzene ring and has a more stable resonance-stabilized intermediate.

question_text: Which one of the following species is an intermediate in the reaction shown below $2\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CHO} \xrightarrow{\text{NaOH}} \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}(\text{OH}).\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3).\text{CHO}$
explanation: This is an aldol condensation reaction where the base generates a carbanion/enol species from propanal, specifically acting via a carbanion/enolate derivative related to $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}.\text{CHO}$.

question_text: Which detector is used in gas chromatography for halogen containing compounds specifically
explanation: The electron capture detector (ECD) is extremely sensitive to electronegative functional groups such as halogens, nitro groups, and organometallics.

question_text: Precessional frequency of a nucleus depends on the followings: [P] : Quantum of externally applied magnetic field [Q] : Quantum of electron density present around the nucleus [R] : Frequency of applied electromagnetic radiations [S] : Electronegativity of the element Choose the correct combination of statements.
explanation: The precessional (Larmor) frequency depends on the strength of the external magnetic field and the local magnetic environment (shielding due to electron density/electronegativity).

question_text: Some statements are given about disodium edetate: [P] : Disodium edetate is a bidentate ligand [Q] : Disodium edetate is a complexing agent but not a chelating agent [R] : Disodium edetate can be used for the assay of lithium carbonate [S] : Disodium edetate can be used for the assay of zinc sulphate Choose the correct answer.

options.D: P, Q, R & S all are true

explanation: Disodium edetate is a hexadentate chelating agent used in complexometric titrations for metal ions like zinc sulfate, making only statement S true among the given assertions.

question_text: Which one of the following amino acids is the most effective contributor of protein buffer?
explanation: Histidine contains an imidazole ring with a pKa of approximately 6.0, which is very close to physiological pH, making it an excellent buffer in proteins.

question_text: Given are some statements about cycloalkanes: [P] : Bayer's theory does not apply to four membered rings. [Q] : Cyclohexane and cyclodecane rings are not flat but are puckered. [R] : Chair form of cyclohexane experiences van der Waals strain due to flagpole interactions. [S] : Boat form of cyclohexane experiences both torsional and van der Waals strain. Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P, Q & R are true and S is false
options.B: Q & S are true and P & R are false
options.C: P, Q& S are true and R is false
options.D: Q, R & S are true while P & Q are false

explanation: Cyclohexane and cyclodecane are puckered to relieve strain, and the boat form experiences torsional strain and steric (flagpole) interactions, making Q and S correct.

question_text: Phenols are more acidic than alcohols. This is due to one of the following reasons. Identify that.

options.A: Alkoxide ions are better stabilized by the electron releasing alkyl groups
options.B: Resonance stabilizes both phenols and phenoxide ions to the same extent
options.C: Phenols are better stabilized than the phenoxide ions while reverse is true for alcohols and alkoxides
options.D: Phenoxide ions are much better stabilized than the alkoxide ions

explanation: The greater acidity of phenols compared to alcohols is primarily due to the resonance stabilization of the resulting phenoxide ion.

question_text: Study the following statements on alkylating agents as antineoplastics: [P] : They get converted to azindinium ions and bind to 7th position -N atom of guanine of DNA base pairs [Q] : Nitrogen mustards and Sulfur mustards belong to this class of drugs [R] : They inhibit dihydrofolate reductase enzyme thereby inhibiting DNA synthesis [S] : They chelate electropositive atoms present in the DNA thereby inhibiting DNA uncoiling Choose the correct combination of statements.
explanation: Nitrogen mustards and sulfur mustards form aziridinium ion intermediates that alkylate the N-7 position of guanine residues in DNA.

question_text: Study the following statements about the stereochemistry of steroidal aglycones in cardiac glycosides: [P] : Rings A-B and C-D are cis fused while B-C is trans fused. [Q] : Rings A-B and C-D are trans fused while B-C is cis fused. [R] : Rings A-B are trans fused while B-C and C-D are cis fused. [S] : Rings A-B are cis fused while B-C and C-D are trans fused. Choose the correct statement

options.A: P is true while Q, R and S are false
options.B: Q is true while P, R and S are false
options.C: R is true while P, Q and S are false
options.D: S is true while P, R and Q are false

explanation: In cardiac glycosides, the A/B rings are typically cis-fused (or trans in rare cases, but predominantly cis), B/C rings are trans-fused, and C/D rings are cis-fused, fitting statement S.

question_text: Following are some statements about Captopril: [P] : It is a prototype molecule in the design of ACE inhibitors [Q] : It contains a suiphonyl group in its structure [R] : It has a proline moiety in its structure [S] : It has an ester linkage Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P & Q are true while R & S are false
options.B: Q & R are true while P & S are false
options.C: P & R are true while Q & S are false
options.D: R & S are true while P & Q are false

explanation: Captopril is a prototype ACE inhibitor containing a proline ring and a thiol (sulfhydryl) group, not a sulphonyl group or an ester linkage.

question_text: Cetirizine as an antihistaminic agent has a low sedative potential due to one of the following reasons. Identify that.

options.B: It has high log P value

explanation: Second-generation antihistamines like cetirizine exhibit lower sedation because they are more polar and less able to cross the blood-brain barrier.

question_text: There are some criteria which an ideal antacid should fulfill. Some of them given below: [P] : The antacid should be absorbable orally and should buffer in the pH range of 4 - 6 [Q] : The antacid should exert its effect rapidly and should not cause a large evolution of gas [R] : The antacid should not be a laxative or should not cause constipation [S] : The antacid should react with the gastric acid and should inhibit pepsin Choose the correct combination of criteria for an ideal antacid.
explanation: Ideal antacids should be non-absorbable (to avoid systemic alkalosis), act rapidly without excessive gas, not cause bowel irregularities (laxation/constipation), and neutralize acid.

question_text: Titanium dioxide is used in sun screen products as a topical protective. The topical protective effect of titanium dioxide is arising due to one of the following properties. Identify that.

options.A: It has a high bulk density
options.B: It has a high LW absorptivity
options.C: It has a low water solubility
options.D: It has a high refractive index

explanation: Titanium dioxide acts as a physical sunscreen by reflecting and scattering UV radiation due to its high refractive index and particulate nature.

question_text: Deferoxamine is used for the treatment of toxicity caused by one of the following ions. Identify that.
explanation: Deferoxamine is a specific chelating agent used to treat acute iron poisoning and chronic iron overload.

question_text: Parachor and Molar refraction can be categorized under one of the following properties. Identify that.
explanation: Parachor and molar refraction depend on both the sum of atomic contributions (additive) and the structural arrangement of atoms/bonds (constitutive).

question_text: East's camphor method is used for determination of molecular weight of solutes which are soluble in molten camphor. The basic principle of the method is dependent on one of the following properties. Identify that.

options.A: Elevation of freezing point of camphor by the solute
options.B: Lowering of vapour pressure of camphor by the solute
options.C: Lowering of freezing point of camphor by the solute
options.D: Elevation of boiling point of camphor by the solute

explanation: Rast's camphor method utilizes freezing-point depression (cryoscopy) using camphor as a solvent due to its unusually large cryoscopic constant.

question_text: In polarography, when the limiting current is achieved, one of the following processes takes place. Choose that.

options.A: The rate of electron transfer just matches the rate of mass transfer
options.B: The rate of electron transfer is slower than the rate of mass transfer
options.C: The rate of electron transfer becomes independent of the rate of mass transfer
options.D: The rate of electron transfer far exceeds the rate of mass transfer

explanation: At the limiting current, the electroactive species is reduced/oxidized as soon as it reaches the electrode surface, making the rate of electron transfer far greater than the rate of mass transfer (diffusion-limited).

question_text: Starch-iodide paste/paper is used as an external indicator in one of the following titrations. Identify that.

options.A: Iodometric titration of copper sulphate using sodium thiosulphate as titrant
options.B: Iodimetric titration of ascorbic acid using iodine solution as titrant
options.C: Diazotisation titration of sulphadiazine using Sodium nitrite as titrant
options.D: Potassium dichromate titration using sodium thiosulphate as titrant

explanation: Starch-iodide paper is famously used as an external indicator in diazotization titrations to detect the presence of excess nitrous acid.

question_text: For a dye to be used as metal indicator in complexometric titrations, some of the dye properties are listed below: [P] : The dye should have distinct colour than the dye-metal complex [Q] : The dye-metal complex should have a higher stability than the metal-chelate (titrant) complex [R] : The dye should be capable of complexing with the metal ions Choose the correct combination of statements for the dye to be used as an indicator in complexometric titrations.

options.A: P & Q are correct while R is not
options.B: Q & R are correct while P is not
options.C: P & Rare correct while Q is not
options.D: P, Q & R all are correct

explanation: A metal ion indicator must form a complex with the metal and show a distinct color change, but the dye-metal complex must have a lower stability than the titrant-metal (EDTA) complex so that EDTA can displace it at the endpoint.

question_text: In amperometry, rotating platinum electrode (RPE) is used as indicating electrode. It has certain advantages as well as disadvantages. Read the following statements about the use of rotating platinum electrode in amperometry: [P] : It causes large diffusion current due to rotation resulting in greater mass transfer [Q] : It causes greatly reduced residual current due to lack of condenser effect [R] : It has a low hydrogen over potential Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P, Q & R are all advantages of using RPE in amperometry
options.B: P & R are advantages of RPE while Q is a disadvantage
options.C: Q & R are advantages of RPE while P is a disadvantage
options.D: P & Q are advantages of RPE while R is a disadvantage

explanation: Rotation increases mass transfer (enhancing diffusion current) and platinum has a low hydrogen overpotential, while residual current is not reduced due to lack of condenser effect.

question_text: What will be the approximate $T_{\max}$ of a drug exhibiting $K_a$ of $2\text{ hr}^{-1}$ and $K$ of $0.2\text{ hr}^{-1}$?
explanation: Using $T_{\max} = \frac{2.303}{K_a - K} \log(K_a / K) = \frac{2.303}{2 - 0.2} \log(2 / 0.2) = \frac{2.303}{1.8} \times 1 \approx 1.28\text{ hr}$, which rounds to 1.2 hr.

question_text: There are some statements related to the protein binding of drugs as given below: [P] : Protein binding decreases the free drug concentration in the system. [Q] : Protein binding to plasma albumin is an irreversible process. [R] : Drugs with a low lipophilicity have a high degree of protein binding. [S] : Protein binding of one drug can be affected by the presence of other drug. Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P & Q are true while R & S are false
options.B: Q & R are true while P & S are false
options.C: R & S are true while P & Q are false
options.D: P & S are true while Q & R are false

explanation: Protein binding decreases free drug concentration and can be subject to displacement interactions by other drugs (competing for binding sites); albumin binding is generally reversible, and lipophilic drugs typically show higher protein binding.

question_text: Based on Henderson-Hasselbalch equation, at what pH value a weak acid would be 99.9% ionized?
explanation: For a weak acid, $\text{pH} = \text{pKa} + \log(\frac{[A^-]}{[HA]})$; for 99.9% ionization, the ratio is $99.9/0.1 = 1000$, and $\log(1000) = 3$, so $\text{pH} = \text{pKa} + 3$.

question_text: Some statements about crystals are given below: [P] : The crystal lattice is constructed from repeating units called unit cells. [Q] : The external appearance of a crystal is described by crystal habits, such as needles, prisms, rosettes etc. [R] : Polymorphism is the ability of a compound to crystallize as more than one distinct crystalline species with different internal lattice. [S] : Hydrates are always more soluble than anhydrous form of the same drug Choose the correct combination of statements about crystals.

options.A: Statement P, Q and S are correct but R is wrong
options.B: Statement P, Q and R are correct but S is wrong
options.C: Statement Q, R and S are correct but P is wrong
options.D: Statement R, S and P are correct but Q is wrong

explanation: Statements P, Q, and R correctly describe crystal structure, habit, and polymorphism, while statement S is false because anhydrous forms are frequently more soluble than hydrates.

question_text: Which one of the followings is NOT used in preparation of baby powders
explanation: Boric acid is avoided in baby powders due to its systemic toxicity and risk of absorption through damaged skin.

question_text: According to Kozeny Carmen equation a 10% change in porosity can produce:
explanation: The Kozeny-Carman equation relates porosity to permeability/flow, typically resulting in a dramatic non-linear change (often much greater than 2- or 3-fold depending on the cubic terms of porosity), making 'None of the above' the standard textbook choice for specific fold changes listed.

question_text: Speed disk atomizer rotates at a speed of:
explanation: Rotary disk atomizers in spray dryers operate at very high speeds, typically ranging from 3,000 to 50,000 revolutions per minute.

question_text: The thickness Gold coating on a USP Dissolution apparatus - I basket should be:

options.B: Not more than $0.001\text{ mm}$ in thickness
options.D: Not more than $0.1\text{ mm}$ in thickness

explanation: USP specifications for basket mesh coating (like gold) typically require a thin protective layer not exceeding $2.5\;\mu\text{m}$.

question_text: Containers used for aerosols should withstand a pressure of:
explanation: Aerosol containers must withstand high pressures safely, standardly tested to withstand 140-180 Psig at $130\;^{\circ}\text{F}$.

question_text: Study the following two statements: [X] : If the gas is cooled below its critical temperature, less pressure is required to liquefy it. [V] : At critical temperature and critical pressure, the liquid will have highest vapor pressure. Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: Both X and V are correct
options.B: X is incorrect and V is correct
options.C: X is correct and V is incorrect
options.D: Both X and Y are incorrect

explanation: Lowering the temperature below critical makes liquefaction easier (less pressure needed); statement V is incorrect because vapor pressure at the critical temperature equals the critical pressure, not necessarily the 'highest' in an absolute sense compared to other definitions.

question_text: Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]: Assertion [a] : For an API of approximately same particle size, the angle of repose will increase with departure from spherical shape. Reason [r] : Angle of repose is a function of surface roughness and particle size. With constant particle size, increase in roughness increases angle of repose.

options.A: Although [a] is true but [r] is false
options.C: Both [a] and [r] are true and [r] is the correct reason for [a]
options.D: Both [a] and [r] are true but [r] is NOT the correct reason for [a]

explanation: Both statements are true facts regarding powder flow and angle of repose, but the increase in angle of repose due to non-spherical shape is primarily due to interlocking and frictional resistance rather than surface roughness alone as stated in [r].

question_text: Study the following two statement [X] :When used as granulating agent PEG 6000 improves dissolution rate of the dosage form as it forms a complex with a better solubility., [Y] :Sodium CMC when used as a binder affects dissolution rate of the dosage form as it is converted to less soluble acid form at low pH of the gastric fluid. Choose the correct answer.

options.A: Both X and Y are correct
options.B: X is incorrect and Y is correct
options.C: X is correct and Y is incorrect
options.D: Both X and Y are incorrect

explanation: PEG 6000 can enhance dissolution via complexation/wetting, and sodium CMC can precipitate into less soluble free acid form at low gastric pH, affecting dissolution.

question_text: Study the following statements about Gram staining: [P] : Gram positive bacteria are stained deep violet and Gram negative bacteria are stained red. [Q] : Gram positive bacteria are stained red and Gram negative bacteria are stained deep violet. [R] : The sequence of addition of staining reagents is crystal violet, iodine solution, alcohol and safranin. [S] : In Gram positive bacteria the purple color developed during staining is lost during alcohol treatment. The cells later take up the safranin and stain red Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P, Q, R & S all are false
options.B: P & Q are false and R & S are true
options.C: P&S are false and Q&R are true
options.D: P&R are false and Q&S are true

explanation: Gram-positive bacteria retain crystal violet (deep violet) and Gram-negative bacteria take up safranin (red), making P and R true while Q and S describe the reverse/incorrect phenomena.

question_text: Choose the correct formula for the calculation of the retail price of a formulation, given by the Govt of India.
explanation: The standard Drug Price Control Order (DPCO) formula includes material cost, conversion cost, packaging charges, and packaging materials multiplied by the MAPE plus excise duty.

question_text:
Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]:
Assertion [a] In arsenic poisoning, dimercaprol, injected intramuscularly, acts as antidote by metal complexation.
Reason [r] EDTA acts as an antidote in lead poisoning, by solubilizing the toxic metal ions from the tissues.

options.A: Although [a] is true but [r] is false
options.C: Both [a] and [r] are true and [r] is the correct reason for [a]
options.D: Both [a] and [r] are true but [r] is NOT the correct reason for [a]

explanation: Both statements are factually true regarding chelation therapy, but the reason describes EDTA and lead rather than explaining dimercaprol and arsenic directly.

question_text:
Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reasons [r]
Assertion [a] : Butylated hydroxytoluene is added as one of the ingredients in the lipstick formulation.
Reason [r] : It is a good solvent for the wax - oil mixtures and coloring pigments present in the lipstick.
Reason [s] It Is an antioxidant and prevents rancidity on storage.

options.A: [a] is true, and [r] and [s] are true and correct reasons for [a]
options.C: [a] is true, [s] is false, and [r] is the correct reason for [a]
options.D: [a] is true, [r] is false, and [s] is the correct reason for [a]

explanation: BHT (Butylated hydroxytoluene) is a well-known antioxidant used to prevent rancidity, not a solvent.

question_text: Which one of the following statements is FALSE about Interferons?

options.A: Interferons are cellular glycoproteins produced by virus infected cell
options.B: Interferons have no effects on extracellular virus
options.C: Interferons are virus specific agents that can interfere with DNA or RNA virus
options.D: They are produced as potent broad spectrum antiviral agents

explanation: Interferons are host-cell specific, not virus-specific.

question_text:
In relation to sodium chloride and water mixture, read the following statements:
[P] : Mixture is eutectic in nature
[Q] : It has eutectic point $-21.2^{\circ}C$
[R] : The composition of eutectic is $25.3\%$ by Mass
[S] : The mixture is a true eutectoid and may exist as peritectic also.
Which of the set of statements is correct?
explanation: NaCl-water system is eutectic with a eutectic temperature of $-21.2^{\circ}C$ and $22.4\% - 25.3\%$ composition depending on literature, but typically P, R, and S capture the properties correctly in standard physical pharmacy contexts.

question_text: In relation to sterilization, what is the meaning of D300F - 2 minutes?

options.A: Death of all microorganisms in 2 minutes
options.C: Death of all microorganism in 2 minutes at $300^{\circ}F$
options.D: Death of $90\%$ microorganism in 2 minutes at $300^{\circ}F$

explanation: The D-value represents the time required to reduce the microbial population by 90% (1 log cycle) at a specified temperature.

question_text:
Choose the correct combination:
(i) Rod mill	(p) Dried plant drug
(ii) Hammer mill	(q) Thermolabile drug
(iii) Fluid energy mill	(r) Paint
explanation: Rod mills are used for fibrous and dried plant drugs, hammer mills for thermolabile/general grinding, and fluid energy mills for ultra-fine grinding like paints or pigments.

question_text: Which following statements Is NOT true for stainless steel 316?

options.A: It is also called inox steel
options.C: The presence of chromium it exhibits passivation phenomenon
options.D: It is not affected by acids

explanation: Stainless steel is highly corrosion-resistant but can still be attacked by certain acids (like hydrochloric acid).

question_text: Precise control of flow is obtained by which one of the followings?
explanation: Needle valves are designed specifically for fine, precise control of fluid flow.

question_text: Heat sensitive materials like fruit juice are evaporated in which one of the followings?
explanation: Falling film evaporators operate with short contact times, making them ideal for heat-sensitive materials.

question_text: Which of the following conditions favor formation of large crystals?
explanation: A low nucleation rate allows existing nuclei to grow into larger crystals rather than forming many small ones.

question_text: If M, L, T, Q and $\theta$ are dimensional representations of mass, length, time, heat and temperature respectively, then what is the dimension of fluid thermal conductivity?
explanation: Thermal conductivity has dimensions of heat per unit time per length per temperature ($Q / (T \cdot L \cdot \theta)$).

question_text: Which one of the following properties is characteristic of microemulsions

options.A: These are transparent systems with droplet size less than $1\mu m$
options.B: These are transparent systems with droplet size less than $10\mu m$
options.C: These are non-transparent systems with droplet size less than $1\mu m$
options.D: These are transparent systems with droplet size less than $1 nm$

explanation: Microemulsions are thermodynamically stable, transparent dispersions typically ranging from 10 to 100 nm (less than $1\mu m$).

question_text: Which one of the followings would be an offence in accordance with the provisions of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940?

options.A: Packing of Paediatric oral drops in 30 ml pack
options.B: Packing of Oxytocin injection in a single unit blister pack
options.C: Packing of Schedule X drugs in 5 ml injection pack
options.D: Packing of Aspirin tablets (75 mg) in 14 tablet strip pack

explanation: Oxytocin injections are strictly regulated to prevent misuse and must be packaged in single unit blister packs as per specific amendments to prevent abuse, making B or C potential regulatory constraints; specifically, oxytocin misuse led to single-dose blister packaging mandates.

question_text: Which one of the following colours is NOT permitted to be used in drugs by the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940?
explanation: Amaranth (FD&C Red No. 2) is a prohibited color under various schedules of the D&C Act due to safety concerns.

question_text: At equal concentrations which one of the following mucilages will possess maximum viscosity?
explanation: Potato starch contains a high proportion of long-chain amylopectin molecules, giving its mucilage the highest viscosity.

question_text: By which mechanism the microorganisms are killed by autoclaving?

options.A: Coagulation of the cellular proteins of the microorganisms
options.B: Alkylation of essential cellular metabolites of microorganisms
options.C: Stopping reproduction of microorganism cells as a result of lethal mutations

explanation: Moist heat sterilization (autoclaving) kills microorganisms primarily through the denaturation and coagulation of cellular proteins.

question_text:
Manufacture and sale of some of the following drugs is prohibited in India:
[P] : Fixed dose combination of atropine and antidiarrhoeals
[Q] : Penicillin eye ointment
[R] : Nimesulide paediatric drops
[S] : Gatifloxacin tablets
Choose the drugs which are prohibited?
explanation: All listed FDCs and formulations have been subject to bans or severe restrictions under Indian drug regulations due to toxicity or irrationality.

question_text:
Following are the phases of clinical trials:
[P] : Human pharmacology	[Q] : Therapeutic confirmatory trials
[R] : Post marketing trials	[S] : Therapeutic exploratory trials
Choose the correct order of phases of clinical trial.
explanation: Clinical trial phases correspond to Phase I (Human pharmacology), Phase II (Therapeutic exploratory), Phase III (Therapeutic confirmatory), and Phase IV (Post marketing).

question_text:
The integrity of seals in case of vials and bottles is determined by some tests. Some of them are given below:
[P]: Leaker's test	[Q]: Water hammer test	[R]: Spark tester probe
Choose the correct answer.
explanation: All three are recognized methods or tests used to check container-closure integrity and seal defects in pharmaceutical packaging.

question_text:
Study the following four statements:
[P] : Gram negative bacteria produce potent pyrogenic substances called endotoxins
[Q] : Ethylene oxide mixed with carbon dioxide or fluorinated hydrocarbons is used in gas sterilization
[R] : D value is the time (for heat or chemical exposure) or the dose (for radiation exposure) required for the microbial population to decline by one logarithmic unit
[S] : Spores of Geobacillus stearothermophilus (Bacillus stearothermophilus) are used for sterility testing of moist heat sterilization process
Choose the correct answer.

options.A: P, Q & R are correct but S is incorrect
options.B: Q, R & S are correct but P is incorrect
options.C: R, S & P are correct but Q is incorrect
options.D: P, Q, R & S all are correct

explanation: Every single statement provided regarding microbiology and sterilization parameters is accurate.

question_text:
Read the following statements:
[P] : The surface area measurement using BET approach utilizes argon gas for adsorption
[Q] : Full form of BET is Brunauer, Emmett and Teller
Choose the correct answer.

options.B: P is correct but Q is incorrect
options.C: Q is correct but P is incorrect

explanation: The BET method typically uses nitrogen gas (or krypton), not argon, making P incorrect while Q correctly identifies the acronym.

question_text: Based on the DLVO theory of force of interaction between colloidal particles, which one of the followings lead to attractive interaction between two particles?
explanation: DLVO theory combines van der Waals attractive forces and electrostatic repulsive forces.

question_text:
Read the following statements with regard to viscosity of a polymer solution:
[P] : Specific viscosity of a polymer solution is obtained as relative viscosity + 1
[Q] : Relative viscosity is the ratio of the viscosity of the solution to the viscosity of pure solvent
[R] : Kinematic viscosity is defined as the viscosity of the liquid at a definite temperature
[S] : The unit for kinematic viscosity is poise or dyne sec cm-2 Indicate the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P & S are correct but Q & R are wrong
options.B: Q & R are correct but P & S are wrong
options.C: P & Q are correct but R & S are wrong
options.D: R & S are correct but P & Q are wrong

explanation: Relative viscosity is solution/solvent viscosity (Q is correct), kinematic viscosity is dynamic viscosity divided by density (R is correct, though definition is slightly loose, P is wrong since specific viscosity is relative viscosity - 1, and S is wrong since poise is dynamic viscosity unit).

question_text:
Determine the correctness or otherwise of the following Assertion [a] and the Reason [r]
Assertion [a] : Salts having no ions in common with the slightly soluble electrolyte increase its solubility
Reason [r] : Such salts lower the activity coefficient of the slightly soluble electrolyte

options.A: Both [a] and [r] are true and [r] is the correct reason for [a]
options.C: Although [a] is true but [r] is false
options.D: Both [a] and [r] are true but [r] is NOT the correct reason for [a]

explanation: Diverse ion effect (salting-in) increases solubility by increasing ionic strength, which lowers the activity coefficient.

question_text: What negative adsorption would do

options.A: Decrease the surface free energy as well as the surface tension
options.B: Increase the surface free energy as well as the surface tension
options.C: Decrease the surface free energy but increase the surface tension
options.D: Increase the surface free energy but decrease the surface tension

explanation: Negative adsorption occurs when solute concentration at the surface is less than in the bulk, which increases surface tension and surface free energy.

question_text:
Read the following statements:
[P] : At temperature below Kraft point, micelles will, not form
[Q] : At Kraft point, solubility of surfactant equals CMC
[R] : Kraft point increases with increasing chain length of hydrocarbon
[S] : Kraft point is normally exhibited by non-ionic surfactants
Choose the correct combination of answers.

options.A: P is correct but Q, R & S are wrong
options.B: R & S are correct but P & Q are wrong
options.C: P, Q & R are correct but S is wrong

explanation: Kraft point is characteristic of ionic surfactants, not non-ionic surfactants, making S incorrect while P, Q, and R are correct.

question_text:
Two statements are given regarding the uniformity of dispersion test (LP):
[P] : It is evaluated using 6 tablets and 500 mL water
[Q] : It involves measuring the dispersion time of each tablet
Choose the correct set of statements.

options.A: P is correct while Q is incorrect
options.C: P is incorrect while Q is correct

explanation: Both statements describe the standard Pharmacopeial test for dispersible tablets.

question_text:
Read the following statements:
[P] : Caramelization occurs in acidic conditions
[Q] : Caramel is optically inactive glucose
[R] : Caramel is obtained by burning of glucose
[S] : Caramel is obtained by degradation of fructose
Choose the right combination of statements.

options.A: P & Q are true but R & S are false
options.B: P & S are true but Q & R are false
options.C: Q & R are true but P & S are false
options.D: R & S are true but P & Q are false

explanation: Caramel is produced by the controlled pyrolysis or thermal degradation/burning of sugars like glucose and fructose, typically catalyzed under specific pH conditions.

question_text:
Read the following statements regarding value added tax (VAT):
[P] : It is an indirect tax	[Q] : It is charged at the rate of $8\%$
[R] : It is tax at source	[S] : It is effective since April 2010
Choose the correct option.

options.A: P&Q are true R&S are false
options.B: R & S are true P & Q are false
options.C: P&R are true Q&S are false
options.D: Q&S are true P&R are false

explanation: VAT is an indirect tax and can be viewed as tax collected at various stages (tax at source/collection point), while rates vary and effective dates depend on jurisdiction.

question_text: Find the process by which the conversion of sulfasalazine to sulfapyridine and 5-amino salicylic acid takes place in the colon
explanation: Colonic bacteria possess azo reductases that cleave the azo bond of sulfasalazine to release sulfapyridine and 5-ASA.

question_text: How much quantity (In grams) of sodium chloride is needed to make 30 ml of a $2\%$ isotonic drug (sodium chloride equivalent 0.20) solution
explanation: Using sodium chloride equivalents: NaCl needed for isotonicity of total volume minus drug contribution yields approximately 0.27 g.

question_text:
Read the following statements about lyophilization:
[P] : Lyophilization cannot be done in final containers like multiple dose containers.
[Q] : Lyophilized product needs special methods for reconstitution.
[R] : Lyophilization causes protein denaturation in tissues.
[S] : Lyophilization is suitable for drying the thermolabile products.
Choose the correct combination of statements.

options.A: P is true and Q R & S are false
options.B: Q is true and P, R & S are false
options.C: R is true and P, Q & S are false
options.D: S is true and Q & R are false

explanation: Lyophilization (freeze-drying) is ideally suited for thermolabile products because it operates at low temperatures.

question_text: In a pharmacokinetic model depicted In the following scheme, what is the half-life of the drug if the apparent volume of distribution of the drug is 25 L?
explanation: Using the elimination rate constant $k = 0.173 \text{ hr}^{-1}$, half-life $t_{1/2} = 0.693 / 0.173 \approx 4 \text{ hr}$ or based on specific multi-compartment values matching the diagram's calculated parameters.

question_text: A sample of paracetamol tablets claims to contain 500 mg of paracetamol But, on analysis by Govt. Analyst, it was found to contain 200 mg. As per Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, this product would be categorized as what?
explanation: When a drug is manufactured with a lower than claimed active ingredient proportion (subpotent/substituted), it falls under adulterated or spurious definitions depending on exact intent, frequently categorized as adulterated or spurious under Indian law.

question_text: Use of which of the following artificial sweeteners is permitted in various dosage forms of Ayurveda, Siddha and Unani proprietary medicines?
explanation: Regulatory amendments in India permit the use of approved artificial sweeteners like saccharin, aspartame, and sucralose in ASU medicines under specified conditions.

question_text: Heckel's plot represents ...............

options.A: Extent of plastic and elastic deformation of material during compaction

explanation: Heckel's plot is used in compaction studies to relate powder porosity to the applied pressure.

question_text: Which of the following would cause increase in the binding strength at the dry granulation process in significant degree
explanation: Macrogol 4000 (polyethylene glycol) acts as an effective dry binder to increase mechanical strength in dry granulation.

question_text: The correct statements concerning concertation microencapsulation (1) Concertation always leads to monophasic microcapsule (2) When the gelatin is used for microcapsule's wall material, the concertation is bound to happen (3) Only gelatin can be used for microcapsule's wall (4) Simple or compound concertation can be distinguished according to the number of macromolecular colloids taking part in the process (5) The pH conditions of the system and the solubility of the auxiliary materials do not have any effect on the preparation of the microcapsule
explanation: Coacervation (referred to as concertation in scan typo) can be classified into simple or complex based on the number of macromolecular colloids, and gelatin is a classic wall material often associated with it.

question_text: Cyclohexanone exhibits only ............... peaks in $^{13}CNMR$ spectrum due to symmetry
explanation: Cyclohexanone has plane symmetry reducing its unique carbons to 4 ($C1=O$, $C2$, $C3$, $C4$, wait $C2,6$ and $C3,5$ are equivalent, giving 4 distinct signals).

question_text: If an organic compound does not absorb UV visible radiation it means compound does not contain ...............
explanation: UV-Vis absorption typically requires conjugated systems, chromophores, or heteroatoms with n-electrons; lack of conjugation shifts absorption out of the UV-Vis range.

question_text: The positively polarized carbon atom of a carbonyl group acts as...........

options.A: An electrophile and a lewis base
options.B: A nucleophile and a lewis acid
options.C: A nucleophile and a lewis base
options.D: An electrophile and a lewis acid

explanation: The carbonyl carbon is electron-deficient (positively polarized), making it an electrophile and an electron-pair acceptor (Lewis acid).

question_text: The Pinene hydrochloride rearranged into bornylterpenoid is called as...........

options.B: A nucleophile and a lewis acid

explanation: The conversion of pinene hydrochloride to bornyl chloride is a classic Wagner-Meerwein carbonium ion rearrangement.

question_text: The mouse model for type I diabetes mellitus is...........
explanation: The Non-Obese Diabetic (NOD) mouse is the standard animal model for autoimmune Type 1 diabetes.

question_text: Cholesterol contributors to ............... Of the biological membrane
explanation: Cholesterol buffers membrane fluidity, preventing extremes of too much fluidity or rigidity across temperatures.

question_text: Active site for all serine proteases consists of which triad
explanation: The catalytic triad of serine proteases classically consists of Serine, Histidine, and Aspartate.

question_text: ..........., Anthelmintics having Immunosuppressant activity.
explanation: Levamisole is an anthelmintic agent that also possesses immunomodulatory/immunosuppressant properties.

question_text: Which of the following is selective $\alpha_2$ selective antagonist
explanation: Yohimbine is a well-known competitive $\alpha_2$-adrenergic receptor antagonist.

question_text: Which one of the following is NOT a protoplast fusion agent
explanation: Colchicine is a mitotic inhibitor (microtubule polymerization blocker), not a fusogen for protoplast fusion.

question_text: Clinically used Labetolol is ...............
explanation: Labetalol has two chiral centers and the clinically used active isomer combination is (1R, 1'S)-Labetalol (R, S).

question_text: For intramuscular injection, angle of administration is ............... Degree
explanation: Intramuscular injections are administered at a 90-degree angle to reach deep muscle tissue.

question_text: Aromatase is an enzyme complex that is the target for several anticancer drugs. Which of the following anticancer drugs targets aromatase
explanation: Aminoglutethimide is an aromatase inhibitor used in breast cancer treatment.

question_text: Vinca alkaloids that are used in combination therapy to treat a variety of tumors. How to cancer cells normally gain resistance to these agents

options.B: Overexpression of the carrier protein called P- glycoprotein
options.D: Decreased ability of the drug to enter target cells

explanation: Tumors typically develop multi-drug resistance against vinca alkaloids via overexpression of P-glycoprotein efflux pumps.

question_text: A set of closely related genes of generic markers that are inherited as a single unit is
explanation: A haplotype is a combination of alleles or gene markers on a single chromosome that are inherited together.

question_text: Ginseng saponins belong to the series of ...............
explanation: Ginsenosides (ginseng saponins) are primarily triterpene saponins of the dammarane series.

question_text: Stokes Einstein equation to the series of ...............

options.A: Enegy changes in Sedimentaition suspension setting

explanation: The Stokes-Einstein equation relates the diffusion coefficient of spherical particles to particle radius and solvent viscosity.

question_text: The source of radiation for FAR IR spectrometer is ...............
explanation: A high-pressure mercury arc lamp is commonly used as a radiation source in the far-infrared region.

question_text: Which of the following alkaloids derived from lysine
explanation: Lobeline is a piperidine alkaloid derived biosynthetically from lysine.

question_text: The agent that can only be given intravenously for heart failure is ...............
explanation: Dobutamine is a catecholamine with a very short half-life requiring continuous intravenous infusion.

question_text: A prescription order for an antibiotic preparation includes the directions 'ii gtt AU q.i.d' what auxiliary label should be affixed to the prescription order container
explanation: AU stands for 'aurque utraque' which means both ears, so the auxiliary label should specify 'For the ear'.

question_text: Which one of the following amino acid residues is specifically recognized by chymotrypsin during peptide bond cleavage
explanation: Chymotrypsin preferentially cleaves peptide bonds at the C-terminal side of large hydrophobic amino acid residues like Phenylalanine (Phe), Tryptophan, and Tyrosine.

question_text: Which of the following criteria should be considered when reviewing a medication for addition to the hospital formulary

options.A: The amount of samples provided to hospital physicians
options.B: Research funds donated to the hospital by the pharmaceutical company
options.D: Whether is a gluten-free oral formulation

explanation: Safety profile and national adverse drug reaction reports are critical clinical criteria when evaluating drugs for a hospital formulary.

question_text: Identify the GABA reuptake inhibitor
explanation: Tiagabine (often spelled Tigabine in exams) is a selective GABA reuptake inhibitor (GAT-1).

question_text: What in the reason of complicated penetration of some drugs through brain-blood barrier

options.A: High lipid solubility of a drug
options.B: High endocytosis degree in a brain capillary
options.C: Absence of pores in the brain capillary endothelium

explanation: The blood-brain barrier features tight junctions and the absence of fenestrations (pores) in endothelial cells, restricting paracellular drug penetration.

question_text: Reynold's number is given by ...............
explanation: Reynolds number (Re) is defined as inertial forces divided by viscous forces: $Re = \rho VD/\mu$.

question_text: The increase in concentration of second messengers (cAMP, cGMP, Ca^{2+} etc.) leads to:

options.A: Inhibition of intracellular protein kinases and protein phosphorylation
options.B: Protein kinases activation and protein phosphorylation
options.C: blocking of interaction between a receptor and an effector

explanation: Secondary messengers like cAMP activate protein kinases (e.g., PKA) leading to downstream protein phosphorylation cascades.

question_text: Which of the following cholinomimetics activates both muscarinic and nicotinic receptors
explanation: Carbachol possesses both potent muscarinic and nicotinic receptor agonist activity.

question_text: Deoxy position of deoxyribose in DNA is at ...............
explanation: Deoxyribose lacks an oxygen atom at the C-2' position compared to ribose.

question_text: All are potent 3A4 inhibitors EXCEPT ...............
explanation: Barbiturates are classic inducers of CYP3A4, not inhibitors.

question_text: 'Probability of nonsterility' is given by ...............
explanation: Sterility Assurance Level (SAL) or probability of non-sterility is typically calculated using kinetic parameters but not directly represented by F, Z, or D values alone which describe thermal destruction time.

question_text: Which of the following is a selective medium for the growth of vibreocholerae
explanation: TCBS (Thiosulfate-citrate-bile salts-sucrose) agar is the selective and differential medium used for the isolation of Vibrio cholerae.

question_text: Specific conductance unit is ...............
explanation: Specific conductance (conductivity) is expressed in Siemens per cm or $Mho\ cm^{-1}$.

question_text: Karplus curve is associated with which spectroscopy
explanation: The Karplus equation relates ${}^3J$ coupling constants to dihedral angles in 1H NMR spectroscopy.

question_text: Which of the following pair of volumetric method of argentometric titration and indicator used is matched correctly (1) Fajan's Method: Chromate (2) Mohr's method: Fluroescein (3) Vohlard's method: Ferric salt. The method and indicator matches correctly in ...............
explanation: Volhard's method uses ferric alum (ferric salt) as an indicator. Mohr's uses chromate, Fajan's uses fluorescein (the pairs in 1 and 2 are swapped).

question_text: The reaction of the citric acid cycle that is most similar to the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex catalyzed conversion of pyruvate to acetyl-CoA is the conversion of
explanation: The alpha-ketoglutarate dehydrogenase complex mechanism and coenzymes are virtually identical to the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex.

question_text: Which one of the following pairs of lipids & related compounds exhibist opposite biological activities
explanation: 5-HPETE is a precursor/intermediate, whereas Leukotriene D4 is a potent bronchoconstrictor/inflammatory mediator acting downstream or via different pathways compared to general precursors.

question_text: HIV may NOT respond to ...............
explanation: Neuraminidase inhibitors (e.g., oseltamivir) are used for influenza virus, not HIV.

question_text: Palmitic, oleic or stearic acid ester of cholesterol used manufacture of cosmetic creams is ...............
explanation: Lanolin consists predominantly of sterol esters (cholesterol esters) of fatty acids like palmitic, oleic, and stearic acids.

question_text: ..........., Is needed for suspensions, lotions, emulsions, creams and ointments to keeps a high container consistency and yet pour and spread easily when needed. It also is satisfactory for IM slow release yet easy to inject
explanation: Thixotropy is the property where gels or fluids thin out upon shearing (shaking/pouring) and recover at rest, ideal for suspensions and creams.

question_text: The enzyme superoxide dismutase (SOD) converts
explanation: Superoxide dismutase catalyzes the dismutation of superoxide radicals into molecular oxygen and hydrogen peroxide.

question_text: For first order reactions the rate constant, k, has the units as ...............
explanation: First-order reaction rate constants have units of inverse time ($s^{-1}$ or $time^{-1}$).

question_text: Which of the following may be used to assess the relative bioavailability of two chemically equivalent drug product in a crossover study

options.D: Area under the plasma level time curve

explanation: Area Under the Curve (AUC) is the primary pharmacokinetic parameter used to assess relative bioavailability.

question_text: A 25.0 mL sample of a solution of a monoprotic acid is titrated with a $0.115\ M\ NaOH$ solution the titration curve shows equivalence point at 7.05. which of the following indicators would be best for this titration
explanation: An equivalence point near 7.05 represents a neutral titration endpoint best matched by bromothymol blue (pH range ~6.0-7.6).

question_text: Which of the following in termed as mass filter
explanation: A quadrupole mass spectrometer acts as a mass filter by allowing only ions of a specific m/z to pass through.

question_text: Which of the following is produced in phenyl propanoid pathway
explanation: The phenylpropanoid pathway produces various phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and lignin starting from phenylalanine.

question_text: A diode array detector coupled with UV detection is advantageous because it

options.B: Allow lower concentrations of analyte to be detected
options.C: Speeds up the detection at a single wavelength
options.D: Allows a single wavelength of detection to be moreprecisely chosen

explanation: Diode array detectors (DAD) capture a wide spectrum of wavelengths simultaneously.

question_text: The LOD of an analysis is at the femtogram level. This corresponds to detection at the
explanation: Femtogram ($10^{-15}$ g) detection level corresponds to parts-per-quadrillion or $10^{-15}$ scale.

question_text: Which are those therapeutic systems, which liberate the active ingredient through a special hole, prepared by laser
explanation: OROS (Oral Osmotic) systems utilize laser-drilled delivery orifices to release drug osmotically.

question_text: Which of following chromatographic technique is most suitable for small, nonvolatile water-insoluble solutes
explanation: Reverse-phase liquid chromatography is standard for small, non-volatile, water-insoluble or hydrophobic molecules.

question_text: Which of the following antiviral agent in not a nucleoside analog
explanation: Moroxydine is a biguanide derivative antiviral, not a nucleoside analog.

question_text: Regarding two compartment pharmcokenitics all are true EXCEPT

options.A: A drug is always removed from the peripheral compartment
options.B: A drug with a high volume of distribution is likely to be lipophilic
options.C: A drug can have a short duration of action while being eliminated very slowly
options.D: Most anesthetic drugs are modelled well with a two-compartment model

explanation: Drugs are eliminated from the central compartment, not the peripheral compartment.

question_text: Phenothiazine is obtained by ............... with sulfur
explanation: Phenothiazine is synthesized by the reaction of diphenylamine with sulfur in the presence of a catalyst.

question_text: Vitamin K is constituted of ............... ring
explanation: Vitamin K derivatives contain a 2-methyl-1,4-naphthoquinone ring structure.

question_text: To balace intellectual property protection, competition and access to affordable prescription drug, the act made by US government is
explanation: The Drug Price Competition and Patent Term Restoration Act of 1984 is widely known as the Hatch-Waxman Act.

question_text: Gridnard test is used for the detection of ...............
explanation: Grignard test (or Guignard test) using picrate paper is used to detect cyanogenetic glycosides via liberated HCN.

question_text: Which hormone works antagonistically to parathormone ...............

question_text: Drugs that have been found to be useful in one or more types of heart failure include all of the following EXCEPT ...............

options.B: Protein kinases activation and protein phosphorylation

explanation: Glycosides are compounds consisting of a sugar (glycone) and a non-sugar moiety (aglycone or genin) linked together.

question_text: Using Young's rule, calculate the dose for a 5 year old child if the adult dose is 340mg

options.B: Polarography involves plotting of conductance - voltage

question_text: Phase 0 studies means

options.D: Studies carried out on small number of animals

explanation: Condensation of diethyl malonate substituted with an ethyl and an isopentyl (3-methylbutyl) group with urea yields pentobarbitone.

explanation: Clavulanic acid is a suicide beta-lactamase inhibitor that protects beta-lactam antibiotics from inactivation.

explanation: Distillation under reduced pressure (vacuum distillation) lowers the boiling point, enabling separation of heat-sensitive compounds without thermal decomposition.

question_text: The preferred rheological behavior of Pharmaceutical suspensions is that of
explanation: Pharmaceutical suspensions ideally exhibit pseudoplastic flow with thixotropy so they thin upon shaking and recover consistency at rest to prevent rapid settling.

question_text: An inventory turnover of ......... a year is considered satisfactory
explanation: An inventory turnover of four to six times a year is generally considered standard and satisfactory for retail/pharmaceutical inventory management.

explanation: Alpha-cyclodextrin consists of 6 glucopyranose units, whereas beta has 7 and gamma has 8.
